jobs.description:
Mission

• The Data-Driven Mechanics Laboratory invites applications for a fully funded PhD position at
• the intersection of computational mechanics, multiphysics of geomaterials, and interpretable
• machine learning. The project focuses on the discovery of governing equations and constitutive
• relations for key multiphysics phenomena on the basis of rich micromechanical and
• experimental data. It pushes the boundaries of modeling and understanding crucial processes
• in geomaterials across scales, with application to geophysics, energy and sustainability.

Main roles and responsibilities

• The successful candidate will contribute to a next-generation data-driven framework for
• scientific discovery in geomaterials. Research will involve the development of techniques
• spanning mechanics and AI, including physics-based modeling across scales
• (discrete/mesoscale/continuum), thermodynamics-informed machine learning and
• neurosymbolic AI. They will also have the opportunity to lead international collaborations with
• experimental research groups.

Requirements

• ● Master’s degree in Mechanics, Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Geophysics,
• Applied Mathematics, Computational Science or related areas.
• ● Strong computational/programming skills (Python/C/C++) including computational
• mechanics, and scientific machine learning.
• ● Excellent English communication skills (oral and written).

We offer

• ● World-class multi-cultural environment on the shores of beautiful Lake Leman.
• ● Innovative interdisciplinary research at the Data-Driven Mechanics Lab.
• ● Exceptional research infrastructure and access to world-class computational resources.
• ● Competitive salary and employment conditions.

Informations

• Please email a single PDF consisting of i) a Curriculum vitae (max. 2 pages) with contact details
• of at least 2 referees, ii) Detailed transcripts, and iii) a Motivation letter (max. 1 page), to
• konstantinos.karapiperis@epfl.ch, indicating in the subject “PhD Application LMD – Last Name”
• until July 15th 2026. Applications will be evaluated on a rolling basis in the order that they are
• received. For inquiries please contact Prof. Kostas Karapiperis at the same email.

Contract Start Date: Fall/Winter 2026

Activity Rate : 100.00

Contract Type: One-year renewable contract

Duration: 4 years

Reference: 2267

• dati sperimentali. Spinge i confini della modellazione e della comprensione dei processi cruciali

jobs.description:
Mission

The Chair of Operations, Economics and Strategy (OES) at the College of Management of Technology at EPFL invites applications for a full-time PhD student position within the EPFL doctoral school program in Management of Technology (EDMT).

We are offering a challenging full-time PhD student position at the Chair of Operations, Economics and Strategy (OES) at EPFL.

The mission of OES is to conduct world-class research and teaching at the intersection of operations, economics, and strategy, with a focus on organizations and their interactions.

At OES, you will have the opportunity to work on the design, analysis, and implementation of innovative models for decision-making, economics, and operations. Research topics may include optimization, decision-making under uncertainty, market design and pricing, operations research, dynamic systems, and strategy-relevant applications.

Main duties and responsibilities

• Develop and complete an original doctoral dissertation

• Conduct independent research in close interaction with the Chair and, where appropriate, with external or industry partners

• Contribute to teaching activities, including co-supervision of student projects

• Provide limited support for academic and administrative activities of the Chair

Profile

• An excellent Master’s-level degree in Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Operations Research, Economics, Industrial Engineering, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field

• A strong mathematical background, including familiarity with optimization, probability, and the analysis of mathematical models

• A sincere interest in business-related, economic, and operational problems

• Proficiency in English

• Strong motivation for academic research, critical thinking, independence, good self-management skills, and team spirit

• Interest in a career involving research and teaching is an asset

We offer

• Excellent working conditions in an international research environment

• Individual and intensive supervision of your PhD project

• Financial support in accordance with EPFL doctoral student conditions

• The opportunity to work on rigorous, practically relevant research at the interface of operations, economics, and strategy

Informations

Your application should include:

• CV

• Motivation letter

• Diplomas

• Transcripts/grades from Bachelor’s and Master’s studies

To be eligible for a PhD at EPFL, candidates must be admitted to an EPFL doctoral school program. For this position, candidates should also apply to the EPFL EDMT Doctoral School :
https://www.epfl.ch/education/phd/edmt-management-of-technology/edmt-how-to-apply/

Application deadlines: January 15, 2027 and April 15, 2027. Applications to OES may be reviewed on a rolling basis; formal admission to EDMT requires a complete application by one of these deadlines.

Expected start date: September 1st, 2027. An alternative start date may exceptionally be agreed upon by mutual agreement.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Missione La Cattedra di Operazioni, Economia e Strategia (OES) presso il College of Management of Technology di EPFL invita le domande per una posizione di dottorato di ricerca a tempo pieno all'interno del programma di scuola di dottorato EPFL in Management of Technology (EDMT). Stiamo offrendo una posizione di studio di dottorato a tempo pieno impegnativo presso la Cattedra di Operazioni, Economia e Strategia (OES) presso EPFL. La missione di OES è di condurre la ricerca e l'insegnamento di livello mondiale all'incrocio di operazioni, economia e strategia, con un focus sulle organizzazioni e le loro interazioni. A OES, avrete l'opportunità di lavorare sulla progettazione, l'analisi e l'implementazione di modelli innovativi per il processo decisionale, l'economia e le operazioni. Gli argomenti di ricerca possono includere l'ottimizzazione, il processo decisionale in incertezza, progettazione di mercato e prezzi, ricerca operativa, sistemi dinamici e applicazioni strategiche rilevanti. Principali doveri e responsabilità
• Sviluppare e completare una tesi di dottorato originale
• condurre ricerche indipendenti in stretta interazione con la sedia e, se del caso, con partner esterni o industriali
• Contribuire alle attività didattiche, compresa la co-supervisione dei progetti degli studenti
• Fornire un sostegno limitato alle attività accademiche e amministrative della Cattedra Profilo
• Un eccellente grado di Master in Ingegneria, Matematica Applicata, Ricerca Operativa, Economia, Ingegneria Industriale, Matematica, Scienza Informatica, o un campo quantitativo relativo
• Un forte background matematico, compresa la familiarità con l'ottimizzazione, la probabilità e l'analisi dei modelli matematici
• Un interesse sincero per i problemi di business, economici e operativi
• Proficienza in inglese
• Forte motivazione per la ricerca accademica, il pensiero critico, l'indipendenza, le buone capacità di autogestione e lo spirito di squadra
• L'interesse per una carriera che coinvolge la ricerca e l'insegnamento è un bene Offriamo
• eccellenti condizioni di lavoro in un ambiente di ricerca internazionale
• supervisione individuale e intensiva del progetto PhD
• Sostegno finanziario in conformità alle condizioni di dottorato dell'EPFL
• L'opportunità di lavorare su una ricerca rigorosa e praticamente rilevante nell'interfaccia di operazioni, economia e strategia Informazioni La tua domanda dovrebbe includere:
• CV
• Lettera di motivazione
• Diploma
• Trascrizioni/classi degli studi di Bachelor e Master Per poter beneficiare di un dottorato in EPFL, i candidati devono essere ammessi a un programma di dottorato in EPFL. Per questa posizione, i candidati devono applicare anche alla scuola medica EPFL EDMT : http://www.epfl.ch/education/phd/edmt-management-of-technology/edmt-how-to-apply/ Termine per la richiesta: 15 gennaio 2027 e 15 aprile 2027. Le domande a OES possono essere riesaminate su base regolare; l'ammissione formale a EDMT richiede una domanda completa entro una di queste scadenze. Data di inizio prevista: 1 settembre 2027. Una data di inizio alternativa può essere eccezionalmente concordata con un accordo reciproco. Verranno contattati solo i candidati a lista corta.

• Compétence en anglais

jobs.description:
Mission

Despite recent technological advances both in the data management and in computer architecture domains, our ability to analyze data still falls behind the unstoppable data collection rates. Data-intensive applications are increasingly more demanding in sophisticated algorithms to store, manage, and interpret data. To meet the challenges, database software needs to communicate efficiently both with the application layer and with the underlying hardware platforms, and deliver seamless computational and data management support. Research in the DIAS lab addresses both aspects of the challenge: we adapt data management technology to computer architecture trends by designing data manipulation techniques that exploit optimally the underlying hardware and I/O devices, and we enable new discoveries in scientific domains through automating physical database design and revolutionizing exploration algorithms in very large data repositories. The DIAS lab pioneers just-in-time query engines which support analytics on raw data, data cleaning and query optimization for heterogeneous distributed data, and hardware/software codesigned engines for demanding applications.

Main duties and responsibilities

•
Work closely with all members of the lab carrying out excellent research

•
Supervise students and collaborate with other postdocs

•
(optional) Contribute to teaching (especially if interested in an academic career)

Profile

•
Highly motivated with proven scientific excellence in the areas of vector query processing, serverless/just-in-time query execution, parallel and distributed data management, and data management systems on emerging hardware

•
Passionate about inventing, building, and publishing quality database systems research

•
A strong publication record and hands-on experience in system development are especially important

We offer

• The DIAS Lab team is renowned for its collaborative and nourishing culture, which supports the lab’s members since their first day in the team and long after their departure

•
Excellent working conditions

•
The contract is fixed for one year initially, renewable up to four years

Informations

Interested parties should send an application through the system including a CV, a research statement, and the names of at least three references. For inquiries regarding the research aspects of the position, contact Prof. Anastasia Ailamaki .

Das DIAS-Labor ist Pionier bei Just-in-Time-Abfrage-Engines, die Analysen von Rohdaten, Datenbereinigung und Abfrageoptimierung für heterogene verteilte Daten sowie mitentwickelte Hardware-/Software-Engines für anspruchsvolle Anwendungen unterstützen.

jobs.description:
Mission

We are offering a challenging position as a full-time (100%) PhD Student at School of Engineering - STI at EPFL. At the Laboratory for fundamental BioPhotonics - LBP we are developing nonlinear imaging techniques to study, characterize and image water in different configuration.

Introduction

Water is the liquid of life. It is intimately linked to our well-being. Without water, cell membranes cannot function. Charges and charged groups cannot be dissolved, self-assembly cannot occur, and proteins cannot fold. That water is intimately linked with life, we experience time and again when we quench our thirst, but how does this link work?

Osmosis is the flow of water across a (cell) membrane that separates two aqueous solutions with different concentrations of a solutes. Regulating osmotic pressure is a key survival strategy of cells and plays an important role in the functioning of every organism. How osmotic pressure and cell membrane tension are regulated on the molecular level is not known. It is the aim of the ERC Synergy Grant R2-Tension, a collaboration between EPFL (Prof. S. Roke) and the University of Geneva (Prof. A. Roux) to work this out. To do so, we will develop new technology and perform experiments in vitro and vivo.

The Project at EPFL – focused on technology development & in vitro studies

Nonlinear optical imaging and new ultrafast spectroscopic techniques have recently been developed in the Roke lab and used to image in real time interfacial water and electrostatic potentials on membrane interfaces of model membranes and in living cells.

We will use second harmonic water imaging to (1) image interfacial water in real time as well as the electrostatic field lines on lipid membrane interface model systems, and (2) image in real time membrane fusion and osmosis. The imaging data will be used to link molecular level information to electrostatics and mechanics of membranes.

Main duties and responsibilities

As a PhD Student, you will be expected to:

• Have full responsibility for your own dissertation

• Research in close collaboration with industry partners

• Experiment design and execution

• Analyze and interpret experimental results

• Write scientific articles for publication in peer-reviewed journals

• Present at international conferences

• Participate in education and supervise student project

This research has many interdisciplinary aspects that demand a highly motivated candidate with strong analytical abilities that is able to think out of the box. The diverse aspects of the project allow a wide range of backgrounds that should include photonics, physics, chemistry/material science, electrical or bioengineering. Experience in nonlinear optics / microscopy, or ultrafast spectroscopy is a bonus. We offer excellent working conditions and a state-of-the-art infrastructure in a highly dynamic and international environment at the forefront of research.

Profile

• A MSc degree

• Good communication skills and willingness to work as part of a team

• Enthusiasm, scientific curiosity, eager to learn, good organizational skills, rigor in experimental work

• High level of motivation for academic research work

• Fluency in English is essential, French / German / Italian would be an asset

We offer

• 4 years to complete your PhD with a competitive remuneration

• An opportunity to develop a scientific career

• A world-class research and training environment with access to state-of-the-art research facilities

• A multi-cultural and stimulating work environment

• A 1-year fixed-term contract (CDD), renewable for 4 years

Informations

The selection process involves multiple stages, and short-listed candidates will be requested to apply to a specific EPFL Doctoral Program to qualify for a PhD at EPFL, photonics, materials science, or electrical engineering.
Please check this page for additional information on admission.

Missione Stiamo offrendo una posizione impegnativa come uno studente di dottorato a tempo pieno (100%) a Scuola di Ingegneria - STI a EPFL. Al Laboratorio per BioPhotonics fondamentali - LBP stiamo sviluppando tecniche di imaging non lineare per studiare, caratterizzare e immagine acqua in diversa configurazione. Introduzione L'acqua è il liquido della vita. È intimamente legata al nostro benessere. Senza acqua, le membrane cellulari non possono funzionare. Le spese e i gruppi carichi non possono essere dissolti, l'auto-assemblaggio non può verificarsi e le proteine non possono piegarsi. Che l'acqua è intimamente legata alla vita, sperimentiamo tempo e di nuovo quando sperimentiamo la nostra sete, ma come funziona questo collegamento? L'osmosi è il flusso d'acqua attraverso una membrana (cell) che separa due soluzioni acquose con diverse concentrazioni di un soluto. Regolare la pressione osmotica è una strategia chiave di sopravvivenza delle cellule e svolge un ruolo importante nel funzionamento di ogni organismo. Come la pressione osmotica e la tensione della membrana cellulare sono regolate a livello molecolare non è noto. È l'obiettivo della ERC Synergy Grant R2-Tension, una collaborazione tra EPFL (Prof. S. Roke) e l'Università di Ginevra (Prof. A. Roux) per risolvere questo problema. Per farlo, svilupperemo una nuova tecnologia e faremo esperimenti in vitro e vivo. Il progetto EPFL – focalizzato sullo sviluppo tecnologico e gli studi in vitro L'imaging ottico non lineare e le nuove tecniche spettroscopiche ultraveloci sono state recentemente sviluppate nel laboratorio Roke e utilizzate per l'immagine in tempo reale dell'acqua interfacciale e dei potenziali elettrostatici sulle interfacce a membrana delle membrane dei modelli e nelle cellule viventi. Useremo la seconda immagine armonica dell'acqua a (1) immagine dell'acqua interfacciale in tempo reale, così come le linee di campo elettrostatiche sui sistemi di interfaccia della membrana lipidica modello, e (2) immagine in tempo reale fusione e osmosi della membrana. I dati di imaging saranno utilizzati per collegare le informazioni a livello molecolare agli elettrostatici e alla meccanica delle membrane. Principali doveri e responsabilità Come studente di dottorato, ci si aspetta di:
• Avere piena responsabilità per la propria dissertazione
• Ricerca in stretta collaborazione con partner industriali
• Progettazione sperimentale ed esecuzione
• Analizzare e interpretare i risultati sperimentali
• Scrivere articoli scientifici per la pubblicazione in riviste peer-reviewed
• Presente alle conferenze internazionali
• Partecipare all'istruzione e supervisionare il progetto degli studenti Questa ricerca ha molti aspetti interdisciplinari che richiedono un candidato altamente motivato con forti capacità analitiche che è in grado di pensare fuori dalla scatola. I diversi aspetti del progetto permettono una vasta gamma di sfondi che dovrebbero includere fotonici, fisica, chimica/scienza materiale, elettrico o bioingegneria. Esperienza in ottica non lineare / microscopia, o spettroscopia ultraveloce è un bonus. Offriamo eccellenti condizioni di lavoro e un'infrastruttura all'avanguardia in un ambiente altamente dinamico e internazionale all'avanguardia della ricerca. Profilo
• Un grado MSc
• Buona capacità di comunicazione e disponibilità a lavorare come parte di un team
• Enthusiasm, curiosità scientifica, desideroso di imparare, buone capacità organizzative, rigore nel lavoro sperimentale
• Alto livello di motivazione per il lavoro di ricerca accademica
• La fluenza in inglese è essenziale, francese / tedesco / italiano sarebbe un bene Offriamo
• 4 anni per completare il dottorato con una remunerazione competitiva
• Un'opportunità per sviluppare una carriera scientifica
• Un ambiente di ricerca e formazione di livello mondiale con accesso a strutture di ricerca all'avanguardia
• Un ambiente di lavoro multiculturale e stimolante

Mission Wir bieten eine herausfordernde Position als Vollzeit (100%) Doktorand an der School of Engineering - STI an der EPFL. Im Labor für grundlegende Biophotoniks - LBP entwickeln wir nichtlineare Bildgebungstechniken, um Wasser in unterschiedlicher Konfiguration zu studieren, zu charakterisieren und zu bilden. Einleitung Wasser ist die Lebensflüssigkeit. Es ist eng mit unserem Wohlbefinden verbunden. Ohne Wasser können Zellmembranen nicht funktionieren. Ladungen und geladene Gruppen können nicht gelöst werden, Selbstmontage kann nicht auftreten, und Proteine können nicht falten. Das Wasser ist eng mit dem Leben verbunden, wir erleben immer wieder, wenn wir unseren Durst stillen, aber wie funktioniert dieser Link? Die Osmose ist der Wasserfluss über eine (Zell-)Membran, die zwei wässrige Lösungen mit unterschiedlichen Konzentrationen einer Lösung trennt. Das Regulieren des osmotischen Drucks ist eine zentrale Überlebensstrategie der Zellen und spielt eine wichtige Rolle bei der Funktion jedes Organismus. Wie osmotischer Druck und Zellmembranspannung auf molekularer Ebene geregelt werden, ist nicht bekannt. Ziel des ERC Synergy Grant R2-Tension, einer Zusammenarbeit zwischen EPFL (Prof. S. Roke) und der Universität Genf (Prof. A. Roux) ist es, dies auszuarbeiten. Dazu werden wir neue Technologien entwickeln und Experimente in vitro und vivo durchführen. Das Projekt bei der EPFL konzentrierte sich auf Technologieentwicklung & in vitro Studien Nichtlineare optische Bildgebung und neue ultraschnelle spektroskopische Techniken wurden kürzlich im Roke-Labor entwickelt und verwendet, um in Echtzeit interfacial Wasser und elektrostatische Potentiale auf Membranschnittstellen von Modellmembranen und in lebenden Zellen abzubilden. Wir werden die zweite harmonische Wasserabbildung zu (1) Bild-Interface-Wasser in Echtzeit sowie die elektrostatischen Feldlinien auf Lipidmembran-Interface-Modellsysteme und (2) Bild in Echtzeit Membranfusion und Osmose verwenden. Die Abbildungsdaten werden verwendet, um molekulare Informationen an die Elektrostatik und die Mechanik der Membranen zu verknüpfen. Hauptaufgaben und Zuständigkeiten Als Doktorand erwartet Sie:

Mission Nous offrons un poste difficile comme doctorant à temps plein (100%) à l'École d'ingénierie - STI à l'EPFL. Au Laboratoire de BioPhotonique fondamentale - LBP, nous développons des techniques d'imagerie non linéaire pour étudier, caractériser et imager l'eau dans différentes configurations. Présentation L'eau est le liquide de la vie. Elle est intimement liée à notre bien-être. Sans eau, les membranes cellulaires ne peuvent pas fonctionner. Les charges et les groupes chargés ne peuvent pas être dissous, l'auto-assemblage ne peut pas se produire et les protéines ne peuvent pas se replier. Cette eau est intimement liée à la vie, nous expérimentons à maintes reprises quand nous étanchons notre soif, mais comment fonctionne ce lien? L'osmose est le flux d'eau à travers une membrane (cellule) qui sépare deux solutions aqueuses avec des concentrations différentes d'un soluté. La régulation de la pression osmotique est une stratégie clé de survie des cellules et joue un rôle important dans le fonctionnement de chaque organisme. On ne sait pas comment la pression osmotique et la tension de la membrane cellulaire sont régulées au niveau moléculaire. C'est l'objectif de l'ERC Synergy Grant R2-Tension, une collaboration entre l'EPFL (Prof. S. Roke) et l'Université de Genève (Prof. A. Roux) pour y parvenir. Pour ce faire, nous allons développer de nouvelles technologies et effectuer des expériences in vitro et vivo. Le projet de l'EPFL – axé sur le développement technologique et les études in vitro L'imagerie optique non linéaire et les nouvelles techniques spectroscopiques ultrarapides ont récemment été développées dans le laboratoire Roke et utilisées pour l'image en temps réel de l'eau interfaciale et des potentiels électrostatiques sur les interfaces membranaires des membranes modèles et dans les cellules vivantes. Nous utiliserons la deuxième imagerie harmonique de l'eau pour (1) l'image de l'eau interfaciale en temps réel ainsi que les lignes de champ électrostatiques sur les systèmes de modèles d'interface membrane lipidique, et (2) l'image en temps réel fusion membrane et osmose. Les données d'imagerie serviront à lier l'information sur le niveau moléculaire à l'électrostatique et à la mécanique des membranes. jobs.description:
Mission

We are offering a challenging position as a full-time (100%) PhD Student at School of Engineering - STI at EPFL. At the Laboratory for fundamental BioPhotonics - LBP we are developing nonlinear imaging techniques to study, characterize and image water in different configuration.

Introduction

Electrolyte solutions in water are an essential ingredient of many aspects of life and technology: the bodily fluids (blood and cellular fluid are prime examples), but also are the key contents of batteries. The electrolyte in batteries determines the power output, life span and efficient energy storage. Electrolyte solutions are commonly described as homogeneous mixtures in which ions are statistically distributed. However, it is well known from theoretical considerations in the 1930’s that this simple description is incomplete for the relevant concentration range and that the structure of electrolyte solutions is far more complex. Experiments to understand this need to cover time scales ranging from femto- to milliseconds, and length scales from atomistic dimensions to microns, a huge challenge.

The Project at EPFL

We will use various novel home-built technologies based on nonlinear optical scattering and imaging methods to achieve this: second harmonic imaging, angle-resolved-second harmonic scattering, and correlated vibrational spectroscopy, all ultrafast optical methods, supplemented by standard linear spectroscopy and light scattering methods. These methods will be applied to simple 3D electrolytes in water, and 2D electrolyte regions at aqueous interfaces. Linking all datasets will allow to map both short – and long-range interactions and collective effects pertaining to all molecular actors. This allows to solve the puzzle surrounding concentrated electrolyte solutions and how they work, for example in their charge transmitting/storing functions and lead to a better understanding, and ultimately new technology.

Main duties and responsibilities

As a PhD Student, you will be expected to:

• Have full responsibility for your own dissertation

• Research in close collaboration with industry partners

• Experiment design and execution

• Analyze and interpret experimental results

• Write scientific articles for publication in peer-reviewed journals

• Present at international conferences

• Participate in education and supervise student project

This research has many interdisciplinary aspects that demand a highly motivated candidate with strong analytical abilities that can think out of the box. The successful candidate has a background in photonics, physics, chemistry/material science, or electrical engineering, ideally supplemented by hands-on experience in free space optics / microscopy, nonlinear optics or ultrafast spectroscopy. We offer excellent working conditions and a state-of-the-art infrastructure in a highly dynamic and international environment at the forefront of research.

Profile

• A MSc degree

• Good communication skills and willingness to work as part of a team

• Enthusiasm, scientific curiosity, eager to learn, good organizational skills, rigor in experimental work

• High level of motivation for academic research work

• Fluency in English is essential, French / German / Italian would be an asset

We offer

• 4 years to complete your PhD with a competitive remuneration

• An opportunity to develop a scientific career

• A world-class research and training environment with access to state-of-the-art research facilities

• A multi-cultural and stimulating work environment

• A 1-year fixed-term contract (CDD), renewable for 4 years

Informations

The selection process involves multiple stages, and short-listed candidates will be requested to apply to a specific EPFL Doctoral Program to qualify for a PhD at EPFL, photonics, materials science, or electrical engineering.
Please check this page for additional information on admission.

Please note that this is a separate application process ne

Al Laboratorio per BioPhotonics fondamentali - LBP stiamo sviluppando tecniche di imaging non lineare per studiare, caratterizzare e immagine acqua in diversa configurazione. Introduzione Le soluzioni elettrolitiche in acqua sono un ingrediente essenziale di molti aspetti della vita e della tecnologia: i fluidi corporei (il sangue e il liquido cellulare sono esempi primi), ma sono anche il contenuto chiave delle batterie. L'elettrolita nelle batterie determina l'uscita di potenza, la durata di vita e l'accumulo di energia efficiente. Le soluzioni elettrolitiche sono comunemente descritte come miscele omogenee in cui gli ioni sono statisticamente distribuiti. Tuttavia, è ben noto da considerazioni teoriche negli anni '30 che questa semplice descrizione è incompleta per la relativa gamma di concentrazione e che la struttura delle soluzioni elettrolitiche è molto più complessa. Esperimenti per capire questa necessità di coprire scale di tempo che vanno da femto a millisecondi, e scale di lunghezza da dimensioni atomiste a micron, una sfida enorme. Il progetto in EPFL Useremo varie nuove tecnologie home-built basate su metodi di spargimento ottico non lineare e di imaging per raggiungere questo obiettivo: seconda imaging armonico, angolo-risolto-secondo spargimento armonico, e spettroscopia vibrazionale correlata, tutti i metodi ottici ultraveloci, integrati da spettroscopia lineare standard e metodi di spargimento della luce. Questi metodi saranno applicati a semplici elettroliti 3D in acqua, e regioni elettrolitiche 2D a interfacce acquose. Collegare tutti i dataset permetterà di mappare sia le interazioni brevi, sia quelle a lungo raggio e gli effetti collettivi relativi a tutti gli attori molecolari. Questo permette di risolvere il puzzle che circonda soluzioni elettrolitiche concentrate e come funzionano, ad esempio nelle loro funzioni di trasmissione / memorizzazione di carica e portare a una migliore comprensione, e in ultima analisi, nuova tecnologia. Il candidato di successo ha uno sfondo in fotonici, fisica, chimica / scienza materiale, o ingegneria elettrica, idealmente integrato da esperienza hands-on in ottica spazio libero / microscopia, ottica non lineare o spettroscopia ultraveloce. jobs.description:
Mission

EPFL is one of the most dynamic university campuses in Europe, ranks among the top 20 universities worldwide and offers an exceptional working environment with very competitive salaries. The LTS2 Lab https://lts2.epfl.ch offers a highly motivating, interdisciplinary scientific environment with many opportunities to interact between different projects and researchers, and has an excellent network of collaborative research projects with applications ranging from biology to neuroscience. The objective of this project is to develop groundbreaking generative AI methodologies for the design of novel materials. This is part of a large ERC Synergy project involving de novo simulations, automated experimental platforms driven by AI models. It offers extraordinary opportunites to collaborate with materials scientists on a quest to set-up a new blueprint for materials discovery, from computational approaches to actual synthesis and characterization.

Profile

We are looking for 2 PhD students who will contribute novel multimodal generative AI architectures, latent diffusion processes, and reinforcement learning approaches. Interestingly, the proposed model will interface with an automated platform performing experimental materials synthesis and incorporate data from experimental characterization and simulations.

We are looking for PhD candidates with a strong analytical background, and an outstanding MSc degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Physics, Applied Mathematics, or a related field. You should be proficient in or willing to learn generative deep learning – in particular based on latent diffusion, multimodal approaches, statistics and learning theory. We expect the candidate to be self-driven with strong problem-solving abilities and out-of-the-box thinking. You are willing to contribute and understand new AI architectures, implement and test them. More importantly, you are willing to partake in a collective international research endeavour involving researchers from different disciplines. Professional command of English (both written and spoken) is mandatory. To be eligible for these positions you must also apply and be accepted to the doctoral program in Electrical Engineering. The LTS2 Lab https://lts2.epfl.ch offers a highly motivating, interdisciplinary scientific environment with many opportunities to interact between different projects and researchers, and has an excellent network of collaborative research projects with applications ranging from biology to neuroscience. The objective of this project is to develop groundbreaking generative AI methodologies for the design of novel materials. jobs.description:
Mission

The CONSTRUCT Laboratory at the School of Architecture, Civil and Environmental Engineering (ENAC), EPFL, led by Prof. David Ruggiero, is seeking two highly motivated PhD candidates to join a newly funded Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) project: “Multiscale Modelling of Cracked Reinforced Concrete: From Aggregate Interlock to Structural Assessment”. The positions are expected to start in early 2027 (or upon agreement).
The PhD research will focus on the development of a new framework for the mechanics-based assessment of cracked reinforced concrete structures, enabling engineers to directly incorporate observed crack behaviour (shape, width, slip) into structural analysis and evaluation. The project combines experimental testing, advanced sensing, and multiscale modelling, spanning from crack-scale behaviour to full structural systems.
Research activities include:
- Investigation of crack behaviour in concrete under complex loading conditions
- Development of path-dependent constitutive models for crack interface mechanics (aggregate interlock)
- Large-scale testing of reinforced concrete elements (panels, beams, walls)
- Development of analytical and numerical models for crack-based structural assessment
- Integration of experimental data into practical engineering tools and simplified models
The successful candidates will join the Concrete Behaviour and Structural Design Laboratory (CONSTRUCT), which focuses on the mechanics of reinforced concrete structures, with particular emphasis on:
- Experimental investigation of reinforced concrete behaviour
- Development of mechanics-based models for structural response
- Integration of research into engineering practice and design methods
- Sustainable design and assessment of buildings and infrastructure
The lab offers access to state-of-the-art experimental facilities, including large-scale structural testing systems (e.g., Panel Element Tester) and advanced instrumentation (e.g., Digital Image Correlation and Distributed Fibre Optic Sensing), as well as strong links to international collaborators and industry partners.

Main duties and responsibilities

As a PhD candidate, you will be expected to:
- Conduct cutting-edge research including experimental design, testing, data analysis, and modelling
- Develop analytical and numerical models of the structural behaviour of cracked reinforced concrete
- Publish results in peer-reviewed journals and present at international conferences
- Collaborate with academic and industry partners
- Contribute to laboratory activities, including supervision of MSc students and teaching assistance

Profile

- Master’s degree in Civil Engineering, preferably with focus on reinforced concrete structures (completed or expected before the employment start date)
- Interest in both experimental and analytical aspects of structural engineering
- Experience with large-scale structural testing, ideally using Digital Image Correlation and/or Distributed Fibre Optic Sensing
- Solid analytical and problem-solving skills
- Programming experience (e.g., Python, MATLAB) and experience operating on large datasets
- Ability to work both independently and collaboratively
- Strong communication skills in English (written and spoken)

We offer

- A world-class research and training environment at EPFL
- Competitive salary and excellent working conditions, 1-year fixed-term contract (CDD), renewable for 3 years (4 years in total) to complete your PhD

Missione

Il Laboratorio CONSTRUCT presso la Scuola di Architettura, Ingegneria Civile e Ambientale (ENAC), EPFL, guidato dal Prof. David Ruggiero, sta cercando due candidati di dottorato altamente motivati ad aderire ad un progetto della Fondazione svizzera per la scienza nazionale (SNSF): “Multiscale Modelling of Cracked Reinforced Concrete: From Aggregate Interlock to Structural Assessment”. Le posizioni dovrebbero iniziare all'inizio del 2027 (o al momento dell'accordo).
La ricerca PhD si concentrerà sullo sviluppo di un nuovo quadro per la valutazione meccanica delle strutture in cemento armato incrinato, consentendo agli ingegneri di incorporare direttamente il comportamento di crepa osservato (forma, larghezza, slip) nell'analisi strutturale e nella valutazione. Il progetto combina test sperimentali, rilevamento avanzato e modellazione multiscala, che spaziano dal comportamento su larga scala ai sistemi strutturali completi.
Le attività di ricerca includono:
- Indagine sul comportamento della crepa in calcestruzzo in condizioni di carico complesse
- Sviluppo di modelli costitutivi di percorso-dipendenti per la meccanica dell'interfaccia di crack (interlock aggregato)
- Test su larga scala di elementi in cemento armato (pannelli, travi, pareti)
- Sviluppo di modelli analitici e numerici per la valutazione strutturale basata sulla crepa
- Integrazione dei dati sperimentali in strumenti di ingegneria pratica e modelli semplificati
I candidati di successo si uniranno al Concrete Behaviour and Structural Design Laboratory (CONSTRUCT), che si concentra sulla meccanica delle strutture in cemento armato, con particolare enfasi su:
- Indagine sperimentale sul comportamento cemento armato
- Sviluppo di modelli basati sulla meccanica per la risposta strutturale
- Integrazione della ricerca nella pratica ingegneristica e nei metodi di progettazione
- Progettazione sostenibile e valutazione di edifici e infrastrutture

- Condurre ricerca all'avanguardia tra cui progettazione sperimentale, test, analisi dei dati e modellazione
- Sviluppare modelli analitici e numerici del comportamento strutturale del cemento armato incrinato
- Pubblica i risultati in riviste peer-reviewed e presenti a conferenze internazionali
- Collabora con partner accademici e industriali
- Contribuire alle attività di laboratorio, compresa la supervisione degli studenti MSc e l'assistenza didattica

- Esperienza con test strutturali su larga scala, idealmente utilizzando Digital Image Correlation e/o Distributed Fibre Optic Sensing
- Competenze analitiche e problem solving solide
- Esperienza di programmazione (ad esempio, Python, MATLAB) e esperienza operativa su grandi set di dati
- Capacità di lavorare in modo indipendente e collaborativo
- Forte capacità di comunicazione in inglese (scritto e parlato)

Offriamo

- Entwicklung von mechanikbasierten Modellen für strukturelle Reaktionen
- Integration der Forschung in die Ingenieurpraxis und Designmethoden
- Nachhaltige Gestaltung und Bewertung von Gebäuden und Infrastruktur
Das Labor bietet Zugang zu hochmodernen experimentellen Einrichtungen, einschließlich groß angelegter Strukturtestsysteme (z. B. Panel Element Tester) und fortschrittlicher Instrumente (z. B. Digital Image Correlation und Distributed Fibre Optic Sensing) sowie starke Verbindungen zu internationalen Mitarbeitern und Industriepartnern.

Hauptaufgaben und Zuständigkeiten

Als Doktorand werden Sie erwartet:
- Führen Sie Spitzenforschung durch, einschließlich experimentellem Design, Tests, Datenanalyse und Modellierung
- Entwicklung analytischer und numerischer Modelle des strukturellen Verhaltens von Stahlbetonriss
- Ergebnisse in Peer-Review-Zeitschriften veröffentlichen und auf internationalen Konferenzen präsentieren
- Zusammenarbeit mit akademischen und industriellen Partnern
- Beitrag zu Laboraktivitäten, einschließlich der Betreuung von MSc-Studenten und Lehrunterstützung

Profil

- Master-Abschluss in Bauingenieurwesen, vorzugsweise mit Schwerpunkt auf Stahlbetonkonstruktionen (abgeschlossen oder erwartet vor dem Arbeitsbeginn)
- Interesse an experimentellen und analytischen Aspekten des Bauingenieurwesens
- Erfahrung mit groß angelegten Strukturtests, idealerweise mit Digital Image Correlation und/oder Distributed Fibre Optic Sensing
- Solide analytische und problemlösende Fähigkeiten
- Programmiererfahrung (z. B. Python, MATLAB) und Erfahrung mit großen Datensätzen
- Fähigkeit, sowohl unabhängig als auch kooperativ zu arbeiten
- Starke Kommunikationsfähigkeiten in Englisch (geschrieben und gesprochen)

Wir bieten

- Eine Weltklasse-Forschungs- und Ausbildungsumgebung an der EPFL
- Wettbewerbsfähiges Gehalt und ausgezeichnete Arbeitsbedingungen, 1-Jahres-Befristungsvertrag (CDD), erneuerbar für 3 Jahre (4 Jahre insgesamt), um Ihre Promotion abzuschließen
- Zugang zu einer einzigartigen experimentellen Infrastruktur
- Möglichkeiten zur Veröffentlichung in führenden Zeitschriften und Präsentation auf internationalen Konferenzen
- Zusammenarbeit mit führenden Forschern und Industriepartnern
- Ein anregendes und internationales Arbeitsumfeld in Lausanne

Informationen

Der Auswahlprozess umfasst mehrere Phasen, und die in die engere Auswahl genommenen Kandidaten werden auch aufgefordert, sich für das Doktorandenprogramm in Civil and Environmental Engineering (EDCE) zu bewerben. Bewerber, die sich bereits beworben haben oder waren
descriptionByLocale.fr:
Mission

The CONSTRUCT Laboratory at the School of Architecture, Civil and Environmental Engineering (ENAC), EPFL, led by Prof. David Ruggiero, is seeking two highly motivated PhD candidates to join a newly funded Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) project: “Multiscale Modelling of Cracked Reinforced Concrete: From Aggregate Interlock to Structural Assessment”. The positions are expected to start in early 2027 (or upon agreement).
The PhD research will focus on the development of a new framework for the mechanics-based assessment of cracked reinforced concrete structures, enabling engineers to directly incorporate observed crack behaviour (shape, width, slip) into structural analysis and evaluation. The project combines experimental testing, advanced sensing, and multiscale modelling, spanning from crack-scale behaviour to full structural systems.
Research activities include:
- Investigation of crack behaviour in concrete under complex loading conditions
- Development of path-dependent constitutive models for crack interface mechanics (aggregate interlock)
- Large-scale testing of reinforced concrete elements (panels, beams, walls)
- Development of analytical and numerical models for crack-based structural assessment
- Integration of experimental data into practical engineering tools and simplified models
The successful candidates will join the Concrete Behaviour and Structural Design Laboratory (CONSTRUCT), which focuses on the mechanics of reinforced concrete structures, with particular emphasis on:
- Experimental investigation of reinforced concrete behaviour
- Development of mechanics-based models for structural response
- Integration of research into engineering practice and design methods
- Sustainable design and assessment of buildings and infrastructure
The lab offers access to state-of-the-art experimental facilities, including large-scale structural testing systems (e.g., Panel Element Tester) and advanced instrumentation (e.g., Digital Image Correlation and Distributed Fibre Optic Sensing), as well as strong links to international collaborators and industry partners.

Main duties and responsibilities

As a PhD candidate, you will be expected to:
- Conduct cutting-edge research including experimental design, testing, data analysis, and modelling
- Develop analytical and numerical models of the structural behaviour of cracked reinforced concrete
- Publish results in peer-reviewed journals and present at international conferences
- Collaborate with academic and industry partners
- Contribute to laboratory activities, including supervision of MSc students and teaching assistance

Profile

- Master’s degree in Civil Engineering, preferably with focus on reinforced concrete structures (completed or expected before the employment start date)
- Interest in both experimental and analytical aspects of structural engineering
- Experience with large-scale structural testing, ideally using Digital Image Correlation and/or Distributed Fibre Optic Sensing

- Ability to work both independently and collaboratively
- Strong communication skills in English (written and spoken)

- A stimulating and international work environment in Lausanne

jobs.description:
Your mission

The Hybrid Photonics Laboratory at EPFL is seeking for talented and motivated candidates to work in the field of Integrated Photonics for building fully integrated microcombs for atomic clocks.
This is a part of a European consortium (with UK and Germany) within the QUANTERA funding network.

Atomic clocks are used for precise timing where an accurate knowledge of the absolute time is needed. Based on ultraprecise transitions in atoms, these devices require precise laser control. At the same time, their deployment requires miniaturization away from table-top laser systems towards compact, on-chip laser sources. The aim of this project is a butterfly packaged, soliton-based optical frequency comb (OFC) device which will be used to interrogate a 2-photon Rb based quantum optical clock. Its stabilization requires f-2f frequency locking, and our lab will contribute thin film lithium niobate for this task. Our lab has been making significant progress in developing TFLN photonics for various applications. Building upon these demonstrations, we want to develop periodically poled lithium niobate devices for these metrology tasks.

You will exploit the low-loss thin film lithium niobate photonics platform, which we can fabricate in-house, at EPFL, to realize efficient and low-foot print frequency converters. In parallel, you will study the performance of these devices at frequencies away of the telecom C-band. You will fabricate these hybrid devices in-house at EPFL cleanroom using newly developed fabrication protocols available in the group.

As a successful candidate of a dynamic team, you will shape the future of photonics-based atomic clock technology in our young and dynamic lab. You will push forward our TFLN technology.

You will kick off diverse aspects of the experimental effort: technical (setting up an optical measurement setup design, including multi-frequency setups and custom-tailored mechanical components) and conceptual (develop the theory of frequency conversion inside photonic chips). In the lab, you will learn about integrated and free-space quantum optical technologies and engineering, and nonlinear optics. You will contribute to the automatisation of measurement routines, comprehensive characterisation of fabricated samples and to bridging the area of microwave/terahertz-optical science and technology with the most modern integrated photonic techniques.

Main duties and responsibilities

• Develop miniaturised frequency converters and apply them to microcombs within the consortium, together with their driving software/hardware, automatize measurement procedures.

• Simulate optical properties using simulations software such as COMSOL or CST.

• Characterize samples in the lab.

• Model experimental data from first principles using Matlab/Python codes.

• Write scientific publications, file patents, disseminate work at national and international conferences.

descriptionByLocale.en:
Your mission

The Hybrid Photonics Laboratory at EPFL is seeking for talented and motivated candidates to work in the field of Integrated Photonics for building fully integrated microcombs for atomic clocks.
This is a part of a European consortium (with UK and Germany) within the QUANTERA funding network.

Atomic clocks are used for precise timing where an accurate knowledge of the absolute time is needed. Based on ultraprecise transitions in atoms, these devices require precise laser control. At the same time, their deployment requires miniaturization away from table-top laser systems towards compact, on-chip laser sources. The aim of this project is a butterfly packaged, soliton-based optical frequency comb (OFC) device which will be used to interrogate a 2-photon Rb based quantum optical clock. Its stabilization requires f-2f frequency locking, and our lab will contribute thin film lithium niobate for this task. Our lab has been making significant progress in developing TFLN photonics for various applications. Building upon these demonstrations, we want to develop periodically poled lithium niobate devices for these metrology tasks.

You will exploit the low-loss thin film lithium niobate photonics platform, which we can fabricate in-house, at EPFL, to realize efficient and low-foot print frequency converters. In parallel, you will study the performance of these devices at frequencies away of the telecom C-band. You will fabricate these hybrid devices in-house at EPFL cleanroom using newly developed fabrication protocols available in the group.

As a successful candidate of a dynamic team, you will shape the future of photonics-based atomic clock technology in our young and dynamic lab. You will push forward our TFLN technology.

You will kick off diverse aspects of the experimental effort: technical (setting up an optical measurement setup design, including multi-frequency setups and custom-tailored mechanical components) and conceptual (develop the theory of frequency conversion inside photonic chips). In the lab, you will learn about integrated and free-space quantum optical technologies and engineering, and nonlinear optics. You will contribute to the automatisation of measurement routines, comprehensive characterisation of fabricated samples and to bridging the area of microwave/terahertz-optical science and technology with the most modern integrated photonic techniques.

Main duties and responsibilities

• Develop miniaturised frequency converters and apply them to microcombs within the consortium, together with their driving software/hardware, automatize measurement procedures.

• Simulate optical properties using simulations software such as COMSOL or CST.

• Characterize samples in the lab.

• Model experimental data from first principles using Matlab/Python codes.

• Write scientific publications, file patents, disseminate work at national and international conferences.

• Maintain collaborations and deliver periodic reports that describe your progress within the project.

Ziel dieses Projekts ist ein mit Schmetterlingen verpacktes OFC-Gerät (Optical Frequency Comb), das zur Abfrage einer optischen 2-Photonen-Rb-basierten Quantenuhr verwendet wird. Seine Stabilisierung erfordert eine f-2f-Frequenzblockierung, und unser Labor wird Dünnfilm-Lithiumniobat für diese Aufgabe beitragen. Votre mission Le Laboratoire de photonique hybride de l'EPFL cherche des candidats talentueux et motivés à travailler dans le domaine de la photonique intégrée pour construire des microcombes entièrement intégrés pour les horloges atomiques. Il fait partie d'un consortium européen (avec le Royaume-Uni et l'Allemagne) au sein du réseau de financement QUANTERA. Les horloges atomiques sont utilisées pour un moment précis où une connaissance précise du temps absolu est nécessaire. Basé sur des transitions ultraprécises dans les atomes, ces dispositifs nécessitent un contrôle laser précis. Dans le même temps, leur déploiement nécessite une miniaturisation loin des systèmes laser de table vers des sources laser compactes sur puce. Le but de ce projet est un appareil de peigne optique de fréquence (OFC) à base de soliton, qui sera utilisé pour interroger une horloge optique quantique à 2 photons Rb. High-End-Mikrowellen-Instrumentierung ist der Kern der Kommunikation, Computing, Metrologie, Sensorik oder Ranking. Dennoch verbindet es die Verfügbarkeit von breitbandig abstimmbaren, schmalen Linienbreiten und hellen Mikrowellenquellen, die verwendet werden können, um eine Hochfrequenzschaltung anzuregen oder ihre Reaktion über Heterodyn-Techniken zu erkennen.

Sie werden Hybrid-Photonik-Spintronik-Chips auf Siliziumnitrid erforschen, eine integrierte photonische Plattform, die eine ultra-verlustarme, vernachlässigbare Zwei-Photonen-Absorption, hohe optische Nichtlinearität, Möglichkeiten zur Konstruktion sowohl positiver als auch negativer Gruppengeschwindigkeitsdispersion durch Wellenleiterdesign und optische Hochleistungsresonatoren bietet, mit dem Ziel, kompakte und effiziente Quellen für gepulste und kontinuierliche Wellenterahertzstrahlung im Band von 100 GHz bis 10 THz zu entwickeln.

Mission

The Hybrid Photonics Laboratory at EPFL is seeking for talented and motivated candidates to join our growing team in the field of Integrated Photonics for generation of high-quality electronic signals at elevated frequencies beyond 100 GHz. This is a collaborative project with IEMN Lille as part of a Swiss-French collaborative project.
High-end microwave instrumentation is at the core of communications, computing, metrology, sensing or ranging. Yet, it relies on the availability of broadband tunable, narrow linewidth, and bright microwave sources that can be used to excite a high-frequency circuit or to detect its response via heterodyne techniques.

You will research hybrid photonic-spintronic chips on silicon nitride, an offering integrated photonic platform providing ultra low-loss, negligible two-photon absorption, high optical nonlinearity, possibilities to engineer both positive and negative group velocity dispersion through waveguide design and high-Finesse optical resonators, with the aim to develop compact and efficient sources of pulsed and continuous wave terahertz radiation in the band from 100 GHz to 10 THz.
As a successful candidate of a dynamic team, you will shape the future of photonics-based millimeterwave-optical technology in our young and dynamic lab. You will develop first-of-their kind hybrid platforms that enable complex high-frequency operations directly inside miniaturized photonic chips.
You will kick off diverse aspects of the experimental effort: technical (setting up an optical measurement setup design, including design of high-frequency electronics and custom-tailored mechanical components) and conceptual (develop the theory of millimeterwave/terahertz generation inside photonic chips). In the lab, you will learn about integrated and free-space quantum optical technologies and engineering, and nonlinear optics. You will contribute to the automatisation of measurement routines, comprehensive characterisation of fabricated samples and to bridging the area of microwave/terahertz-optical science and technology with the most modern integrated photonic techniques.

Main duties and responsibilities

• Develop miniaturised millimeterwave/terahertz oscillator and apply them to photonic circuits, together with their driving software/hardware, automatize measurement procedures.

jobs.description:
About the Role

The NLP & AIMM Labs at EPFL are looking for a Teaching Program Coordinator to manage the operational backbone of their teaching portfolios. You will be the central point of coordination across three courses:

• CS-552 Modern Natural Language Processing

• CS-461 Foundation Models and Generative AI

• and an upcoming bachelor's-level **AI-101** (launching in Fall 2027)

In this role, you will manage the execution of these courses during the semester in which they offered, as well as their preparation throughout the rest of the year. You will ensure teams are organized and assignments, exams, and project milestones are prepared, tested, and released on schedule.

Beyond these three courses, you will optionally also help coordinate broader teaching activities and logistics across AI-related faculty at EPFL, acting as a connecting point for shared resources, timelines, and best practices between courses and instructors.

Main duties and responsibilities

Course operations (CS-552, CS-461, AI-101)

- Organize and manage the TA team for each course: recruitment support, onboarding, task allocation, and weekly coordination
- Own the semester production calendar for assignments, midterms, and project milestones; ensuring each is drafted, tested, and released on time
- Coordinate testing/QA of assignments and autograders before release, working directly with TAs and the course instructor
- Manage course infrastructure (Moodle, autograding platforms, Ed forums, GitHub Classroom, etc.)
- Track and triage student questions/issues during the semester, escalating to TAs or instructor as needed
- Support exam logistics: room booking, proctoring schedules, grading coordination

Cross-course and cross-faculty coordination

- Serve as a liaison between the NLP and AIMM Labs's courses and other AI-related courses/faculty at EPFL, surfacing opportunities to share materials, infrastructure, or TA capacity
- Contribute to planning for the new AI-101 bachelor's course ahead of its Fall 2027 launch, including TA team build-out and initial infrastructure setup
- Help standardize teaching operations practices (grading rubrics, release checklists, TA onboarding materials) across courses
- Support broader teaching-related administrative tasks (scheduling, reporting, budget tracking for TA hours) as needed

Your profile

• University degree (Bachelor's or Master's) in Computer Science, Data Science, or a related technical field

• Prior experience as a TA, head TA, or in course/program coordination, ideally in a technical or CS-related field

• Strong organizational skills and comfort managing multiple parallel timelines and stakeholders

• Working familiarity with tools such as Moodle, GitHub/GitHub Classroom, and autograding systems (or willingness to learn quickly)

• Some technical fluency in NLP/ML concepts is a strong plus, though this is not a research or teaching role

• Fluent in English; French is an asset for interacting with EPFL's administration

• Reliable, proactive, and comfortable working directly with faculty, PhD students, and undergraduate TAs

What We Offer

• A role at the operational heart of EPFL's teaching activities in two of the most active NLP/AI labs in Switzerland

• Direct exposure to state-of-the-art course content in NLP and foundation models

• EPFL's standard employment conditions: flexible working hours, on-campus childcare and sports facilities, and a diverse international campus community

Information

Activity Rate : 80-100%

Duration : 1 year, renewable

Contract Type: Fixed-term contract (CDD)

jobs.description:
EPFL, the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne, is one of Europe’s most dynamic university campuses and ranks among the world’s top universities. With more than 6,500 employees, EPFL advances its core missions of education, research and innovation within an international community of over 18,500 people, including more than 14,000 students and 4,000 researchers from over 120 countries.

Within this stimulating and international research environment, the Communauté d’études pour l’aménagement du territoire (CEAT) at EPFL is recruiting a postdoctoral researcher in urban verticality, Earth Observation, environmental modelling and geospatial data science. The position is part of Vertical Africa (VERTICAF), an interdisciplinary research project funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF).

We are looking for a full time postdoctoral researcher at EPFL Lausanne.

Information

Contract duration: 48 months
Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (EPFL, CEAT), with fieldwork assignments in Kigali, Dakar and Luanda
Activity rate: 100 %
Start date : 02/2027
Scientific supervisor: Prof. Jérôme Chenal

Project context

Vertical Africa is a four-year interdisciplinary research project funded by the SNSF, bringing together EPFL (Prof. Jérôme Chenal), the University of Geneva (Prof. Armelle Choplin and Prof. Didier Péclard) and African academic and institutional partners in Kigali (Rwanda), Dakar (Senegal) and Luanda (Angola).

Against the backdrop of accelerating verticalisation in African cities, VERTICAF offers the first systematic and diachronic analysis of how cities are expanding not only horizontally but also vertically. The project combines urban studies, remote sensing, 3D modelling, environmental science, architecture, political science and participatory approaches to investigate the environmental, social and political implications of vertical urban development.

The project has three main ambitions: (1) developing methods to measure verticality and its impacts in data-scarce contexts, in Africa and elsewhere; (2) documenting, theoretically and empirically, the interactions between vertical growth, capitalism, governance, inequalities and everyday life; (3) co-designing more sustainable and inclusive models for the future of African cities.

The research is organised into four work packages. The postdoctoral researcher will contribute to measuring urban verticality and its environmental impacts (WP1), while providing scientific coordination for the geospatial, modelling and digital observatory components of the project (WP4).

Research Focus

How can verticalisation and its environmental consequences be measured, modelled and projected in data-scarce African cities, and how can these results be translated into an open and reproducible digital observatory supporting research, planning and participatory exploration of future urban scenarios?

The postdoctoral researcher will develop an integrated analytical framework connecting:

Verticalisation → 3D urban morphology → environmental processes → climate and flood impacts → future urban scenarios

descriptionByLocale.de:
EPFL, die Eidgenössische Technische Hochschule in Lausanne, ist eine der dynamischsten Universitäten Europas und gehört zu den Top-Universitäten der Welt. Mit mehr als 6.500 Mitarbeitern treibt die EPFL ihre Kernaufgaben Bildung, Forschung und Innovation in einer internationalen Gemeinschaft von über 18.500 Menschen voran, darunter mehr als 14.000 Studenten und 4.000 Forscher aus über 120 Ländern.

In diesem anregenden und internationalen Forschungsumfeld rekrutiert die Communauté d’études pour l’aménagement du territoire (CEAT) an der EPFL einen Postdoktoranden für urbane Vertikalität, Erdbeobachtung, Umweltmodellierung und Geodatenwissenschaft. Die Stelle ist Teil von Vertical Africa (VERTICAF), einem interdisziplinären Forschungsprojekt, das vom Schweizerischen Nationalfonds (SNF) gefördert wird.

Wir suchen einen Vollzeit-Postdoktoranden an der EPFL Lausanne.

Information

Vertragslaufzeit: 48 Monate
Standort: Lausanne, Schweiz (EPFL, CEAT), mit Feldforschung in Kigali, Dakar und Luanda
Aktivitätsrate: 100 %
Startdatum: 02/2027
Wissenschaftlicher Leiter: Prof. Jérôme Chenal

Projektkontext

Vertical Africa ist ein vom SNF finanziertes vierjähriges interdisziplinäres Forschungsprojekt, das die EPFL (Prof. Jérôme Chenal), die Universität Genf (Prof. Armelle Choplin und Prof. Didier Péclard) und afrikanische akademische und institutionelle Partner in Kigali (Ruanda), Dakar (Senegal) und Luanda (Angola) zusammenbringt.

Vor dem Hintergrund der beschleunigten Vertikalisierung in afrikanischen Städten bietet VERTICAF die erste systematische und diachrone Analyse, wie Städte nicht nur horizontal, sondern auch vertikal expandieren. Das Projekt kombiniert Stadtstudien, Fernerkundung, 3D-Modellierung, Umweltwissenschaft, Architektur, Politikwissenschaft und partizipative Ansätze, um die ökologischen, sozialen und politischen Auswirkungen der vertikalen Stadtentwicklung zu untersuchen.

Das Projekt verfolgt drei Hauptziele: (1) Entwicklung von Methoden zur Messung der Vertikalität und ihrer Auswirkungen in datenarmen Kontexten in Afrika und anderswo; (2) theoretische und empirische Dokumentation der Wechselwirkungen zwischen vertikalem Wachstum, Kapitalismus, Governance, Ungleichheiten und Alltag; (3) Mitgestaltung nachhaltigerer und integrativer Modelle für die Zukunft afrikanischer Städte.

Die Forschung ist in vier Arbeitspakete gegliedert. Der Postdoktorand wird zur Messung der vertikalen Stadtverhältnisse und ihrer Umweltauswirkungen (WP1) beitragen und gleichzeitig die wissenschaftliche Koordination für die Geodaten-, Modellierungs- und Digital-Observa-Komponenten des Projekts (WP4) bereitstellen.

Forschung

Wie können die Vertikalisierung und ihre Umweltfolgen in datenarmen afrikanischen Städten verstanden, modelliert und projiziert werden, und wie können diese Ergebnisse in einem offenen und reproduzierbaren digitalen Observatorium zusammengefasst werden, das die Erforschung, Planung und partizipative Erkundung zukünftiger urbaner Landschaften unterstützt?

Der Postdoktorand wird einen integrierten analytischen Rahmen entwickeln, der Folgendes verbindet:

Verticalisation → 3D urbane Morphologie → Umweltprozesse → Klima und Überschwemmungen → zukünftige urbane Landschaften

Die Forschung wird über Stadt-, Nachbarschafts- und Gebäudeskalen hinweg und entlang städtischer Transekte durchgeführt, die historische zentrale Bezirke abdecken, Nachbarschaften und neu entwickelte periphere Stadtzentren schrittweise vertikalisieren.

Aufgaben und Aufgaben

WP1 - Umweltindikatoren und Fernerkundung

• Entwicklung und Harmonisierung von Erdbeobachtungs-Workflows unter Verwendung von Sentinel-1/2, Landsat, MODIS, GHSL, Open Buildings 2.5D, OpenStreetMap, Copernicus und anderen verfügbaren Datensätzen für urbane Morphologie, Vertikalisierung und Land-Oberfläche-Änderung, einschließlich der Rekonstruktion der zeitlichen Dynamik durch multitemporale Bilder und Änderungserkennungsansätze.

• Ableitung und Analyse von Stadt- und Umweltindikatoren im Zusammenhang mit der Vertikalisierung, einschließlich Gebäudehöhe und -dichte, Bauvolumen, Lampen und NDVI, Dichtigkeit, Albedo, Landoberflächentemperatur, Klimatisierung
descriptionByLocale.fr:
L'EPFL, l'Institut fédéral suisse de technologie de Lausanne, est l'une des universités les plus dynamiques d'Europe et parmi les meilleures universités du monde. Avec plus de 6 500 employés, l'EPFL poursuit ses missions essentielles d'éducation, de recherche et d'innovation au sein d'une communauté internationale de plus de 18 500 personnes, dont plus de 14 000 étudiants et 4 000 chercheurs de plus de 120 pays.

Dans cet environnement de recherche stimulant et international, la Communauté d'études pour l'aménagement du territoire (CEAT) de l'EPFL recrute un chercheur postdoctoral en verticalité urbaine, observation de la Terre, modélisation environnementale et sciences des données géospatiales. Ce poste fait partie de Vertical Africa (VERTICAF), un projet de recherche interdisciplinaire financé par la Fondation nationale suisse des sciences (SNSF).

Nous recherchons un chercheur postdoctoral à temps plein à l'EPFL Lausanne.

Informations

Durée du contrat : 48 mois
Lieu: Lausanne, Suisse (EPFL, CEEA), avec des travaux sur le terrain à Kigali, Dakar et Luanda
Taux d'activité: 100 %
Date de début: 02/2027
Superviseur scientifique: Prof. Jérôme Chenal

Contexte du projet

Vertical Africa est un projet de recherche interdisciplinaire de quatre ans financé par la SNSF, réunissant l'EPFL (Prof. Jérôme Chenal), l'Université de Genève (Prof. Armelle Choplin et Prof. Didier Péclard) et des partenaires académiques et institutionnels africains à Kigali (Rwanda), Dakar (Sénégal) et Luanda (Angola).

Dans le contexte de l'accélération de la verticalisation dans les villes africaines, VERTICAF propose la première analyse systématique et diachronique de l'expansion des villes non seulement horizontalement mais aussi verticalement. Le projet combine études urbaines, télédétection, modélisation 3D, sciences de l'environnement, architecture, sciences politiques et approches participatives pour étudier les implications environnementales, sociales et politiques du développement urbain vertical.

Le projet a trois ambitions principales : 1) développer des méthodes de mesure de la verticalité et de ses impacts dans des contextes de données, en Afrique et ailleurs; 2) documenter, théoriquement et empiriquement, les interactions entre croissance verticale, capitalisme, gouvernance, inégalités et vie quotidienne; 3) co-concevoir des modèles plus durables et inclusifs pour l'avenir des villes africaines.

La recherche est organisée en quatre groupes de travail. Le chercheur postdoctoral contribuera à la mesure de la verticalité urbaine et de ses impacts environnementaux (WP1), tout en assurant la coordination scientifique des composantes géospatiales, de modélisation et d'observation numérique du projet (WP4).

Recherche

Comment comprendre, modéliser et projeter la verticalisation et ses conséquences sur l'environnement dans les villes africaines, et comment résumer ces résultats en un observatoire numérique ouvert et reproductible soutenant la recherche, la planification et l'exploration participative des paysages urbains futurs?

Le chercheur postdoctoral élaborera un cadre analytique intégré reliant :

verticalisation → morphologie urbaine 3D → processus environnementaux → impact du climat et des inondations → paysages urbains futurs

Les travaux de recherche se dérouleront à l'échelle des villes, des quartiers et des bâtiments et le long de transects urbains couvrant les quartiers centraux historiques, les quartiers en voie de verticalisation progressive et les nouveaux centres urbains périphériques.

Tâches

WP1 - Indicateurs environnementaux et télédétection

• Développer et harmoniser les flux de travail d'observation de la Terre en utilisant Sentinel-1/2, Landsat, MODIS, GHSL, Open Buildings 2.5D, OpenStreetMap, Copernicus et d'autres ensembles de données disponibles pour la morphologie urbaine, la verticalisation et le changement de surface, y compris la reconstruction de la dynamique temporelle par des approches d'imagerie multitemporelle et de détection du changement.

• Déterminez et analysez les indicateurs urbains et environnementaux liés à la verticalisation, y compris la hauteur et la densité du bâtiment, le volume construit, les lampes et la NDVI, l'imperviosité, l'albédo, la température de surface du sol, le climat

jobs.description:
Mission

The Extreme Environments Research Laboratory (EERL) is looking for a PhD student for our Antarctica InSync activities. Within Antarctica InSync we will study aerosol-cloud interactions over coastal Antarctica and the Southern Ocean sea ice with instruments placed on a tethered balloon and at ground.

Your mission will be to perform and analyze vertically resolved measurements of aerosols, trace gases and meteorological variables using EERL’s helikite facility and to conduct ground based aerosol chemical observations using the new nano-mechanical membrane infrared spectroscopy method (NEMS-FTIR) that we developed.

The EERL focuses on understanding natural and anthropogenic atmospheric processes, as well as exchange processes between the atmosphere and cryosphere, ocean and land that have climate impact and are impacted by climate. Within Antarctica InSync, the EERL will deploy instruments on the icebreaker Polarstern that will drift in the Weddell Sea and at Neumayer station as part of the DOMINO project.

Main tasks and responsibilities

• Perform field observations with a small team in Antarctica using the helikite facility

• Enhance the helikite's measurement capabilities by adding new instrumentation for chemical analyses and cloud observations with the support of a technician

• Analyze samples of aerosols and trace gases in laboratory, for e.g., chemical composition and ice nucleating particles

• Data analysis of observations, numerical model output and remote sensing data

• Tight collaboration with the project partners and participation in working meetings

• Teaching assistantship

• Part-time supervision of MSc students

Profile

• A master degree or (equivalent) in atmospheric, climate, or environment science, engineering, meteorology, physics or similar

• Interest in atmospheric studies and polar regions

• Desire to do field work

• Desire to do laboratory work

• Interested in improving the tethered balloon payload with support of EERL's technician

• Capable of conducting scientific research independently

• Basic knowledge of scientific programming

• Data handling skills

• Good interpersonal skills, team player

• Good knowlege of English (written and spoken)

We offer

• A dynamic, interdisciplinary and young research group

• A vibrant, internationally visible and rising academic institution in alpine and polar environments research

• A great working atmosphere and ample opportunities for professional and personal development with access to many continuing education courses

• 4 years to complete your PhD with a competitive remuneration

• A 1-year fixed-term contract (CDD), renewable for 4 years

Informations

The selection process involves multiple stages, and short-listed candidates will be requested to apply to the Doctoral Program in Civil and Environmental Engineering ( EDCE ). Only applicants admitted to EDCE can be considered for this position.

Your application should contain: A motivation Letter, Your detailed CV, Contact information, The names and contact information of 3 references willing to write a recommendation letter

For the application, you must submit your documents in two places (Please check this page for additional information on admission) .:

1) Via the EPFL recruitment platform: Please submit a motivation letter with your interests and qualifications, a CV and publication list (if applicable), your bachelor and master curriculum with grades, and contacts of three references.

2) Please ensure to submit as well an application to the Doctoral Program in Civil and Environmental Engineering (EDCE). Only applicants admitted to EDCE can be considered for this position. The submission deadline for EDCE is September 15, 2026.

Please note, PhD positions are awarded initially for one year. After one year of successful probation, the initial contract can be extended up to a total of four years.

Application deadline: 15/09/2026

Contract Start Date: 01/10/2026

La vostra missione sarà di eseguire e analizzare le misurazioni verticalmente risolte di aerosol, gas di traccia e variabili meteoologiche utilizzando EERL

L'EERL si concentra sulla comprensione dei processi atmosferici naturali e antropogeni, nonché sui processi commerciali tra l'atmosfera e la criosfera, l'oceano e la terra che hanno un impatto climatico e sono influenzati dal clima. All'interno dell'Antartide InSync, l'EERL distribuirà strumenti sul rompicapo Polarstern che andrà alla deriva nel Mar di Weddell e nella stazione di Neumayer come parte del progetto DOMINO.

descriptionByLocale.fr:
Mission

The Extreme Environments Research Laboratory (EERL) is looking for a PhD student for our Antarctica InSync activities. Within Antarctica InSync we will study aerosol-cloud interactions over coastal Antarctica and the Southern Ocean sea ice with instruments placed on a tethered balloon and at ground.

Your mission will be to perform and analyze vertically resolved measurements of aerosols, trace gases and meteorological variables using EERL’s helikite facility and to conduct ground based aerosol chemical observations using the new nano-mechanical membrane infrared spectroscopy method (NEMS-FTIR) that we developed.

The EERL focuses on understanding natural and anthropogenic atmospheric processes, as well as exchange processes between the atmosphere and cryosphere, ocean and land that have climate impact and are impacted by climate. Within Antarctica InSync, the EERL will deploy instruments on the icebreaker Polarstern that will drift in the Weddell Sea and at Neumayer station as part of the DOMINO project.

Main tasks and responsibilities

• Perform field observations with a small team in Antarctica using the helikite facility

• Enhance the helikite's measurement capabilities by adding new instrumentation for chemical analyses and cloud observations with the support of a technician

• Analyze samples of aerosols and trace gases in laboratory, for e.g., chemical composition and ice nucleating particles

• Data analysis of observations, numerical model output and remote sensing data

• Tight collaboration with the project partners and participation in working meetings

• Teaching assistantship

• Part-time supervision of MSc students

Profile

• A master degree or (equivalent) in atmospheric, climate, or environment science, engineering, meteorology, physics or similar

• Interest in atmospheric studies and polar regions

• Desire to do field work

• Desire to do laboratory work

• Interested in improving the tethered balloon payload with support of EERL's technician

• Capable of conducting scientific research independently

• Basic knowledge of scientific programming

• Data handling skills

• Good interpersonal skills, team player

• Good knowlege of English (written and spoken)

We offer

• A dynamic, interdisciplinary and young research group

• A vibrant, internationally visible and rising academic institution in alpine and polar environments research

• A great working atmosphere and ample opportunities for professional and personal development with access to many continuing education courses

• 4 years to complete your PhD with a competitive remuneration

• A 1-year fixed-term contract (CDD), renewable for 4 years

Informations

The selection process involves multiple stages, and short-listed candidates will be requested to apply to the Doctoral Program in Civil and Environmental Engineering ( EDCE ). Only applicants admitted to EDCE can be considered for this position.

Your application should contain: A motivation Letter, Your detailed CV, Contact information, The names and contact information of 3 references willing to write a recommendation letter

For the application, you must submit your documents in two places (Please check this page for additional information on admission) .:

1) Via the EPFL recruitment platform: Please submit a motivation letter with your interests and qualifications, a CV and publication list (if applicable), your bachelor and master curriculum with grades, and contacts of three references.

2) Please ensure to submit as well an application to the Doctoral Program in Civil and Environmental Engineering (EDCE). Only applicants admitted to EDCE can be considered for this position. The submission deadline for EDCE is September 15, 2026.

Please note, PhD positions are awarded initially for one year. After one year of successful probation, the initial contract can be extended up to a total of four years.
