jobs.description:
Mission

Within the faculty of engineering (STI), the Galatea Laboratory explores novel paradigms to tailor material properties locally using lasers. Our research involves three main clusters: understanding and exploring laser-matter interaction phenomena, investigating new manufacturing processes based on 3D direct-write laser methods, and finally, exploring novel concepts of multi-scale systems based on single monolith. The lab features state-of-the-art laser facilities and infrastructure for pioneer research.

The Galatea Lab is located in the vibrant Neuchâtel’s campus of EPFL, part of Microcity, a ecosystem with a focused on micro-technologies.

To strengthen our research program on laser-based methods to tailor material properties, we are looking for a post-doc to investigate advanced wavefront shaping methods based on adaptive optics applied to the context of nonlinear laser-matter interaction.

Main duties and responsibilities

• Define relevant research and experimental plans, sustained with theoretical considerations and knowledge of the relevant literature.

• Conduct experiments and analyze data.

• Report and disseminate the research outcome in journal publications and at international conferences.

• Interact and collaborate with other lab members as well as with industrial partners.

• Occasionally supervise undergraduate students (bachelor or master levels).

• Contribute to the laboratory operations through shared duties.

Profile

• You recently obtained a PhD in optics, applied physics or related fields with a strong knowledge of optics.

• You have experience in adaptive optics as well as hands-on experience with optical setups involving lasers.

• You have a keen interest in research in the field of nonlinear optics, ultrafast lasers and/or laser-matter interaction.

• You are independent, creative, solution-oriented, flexible and a team-player.

We offer

• Opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge emerging research topics.

• Opportunity to work in an established multidisciplinary lab in ultrafast laser-matter interaction and advanced manufacturing processes, as well as optomechanical designs.

• Opportunity to access state-of-the-art research facilities and laboratory resources.

• Opportunity to collaborate with world-leading research groups through international collaborations.

• Opportunity to interact with multidisciplinary projects with strong links to industry and spin-offs.

• EPFL is an international and top-ranking university. It offers a young, stimulating, dynamic, interdisciplinary, and international working environment, a broad range of scientific training and networking events and hosts a vibrant entrepreneurial community.

• EPFL is an equal-opportunity employer. Candidates will be recruited solely based on merit.

Informations

Only applications submitted through the online platform are considered.

A brief cover letter (pdf, up to 2 pages).

And in one PDF:

A CV with a publication list.
A research statement (pdf, up to 3 pages).
Contact details for 3 referees.

For any further information, please contact: prof. Yves Bellouard - yves.bellouard@epfl.ch

Keywords: Adaptive optics, beam shaping, nonlinear optics, laser-matter interaction, ultrafast lasers.

Mission

Au sein de la faculté de couture (STI), le Laboratoire Galatea explore de nouveaux paradigmes pour les propriétés matérielles localement à l'aide de lasers. Notre recherche porte sur trois grands groupes : la compréhension et l'exploration des phénomènes d'interaction laser-matière, les nouveaux procédés de fabrication présumés basés sur des méthodes laser à écriture directe en 3D, et enfin, l'exploration de nouveaux concepts de systèmes à plusieurs échelles basés sur un seul monolithe. Le laboratoire dispose d'installations laser de pointe et d'infrastructures pour la recherche pionnière.

Le Galatea Lab est situé dans le vibrant campus de Neuchâtel de l'EPFL, une partie de Microcity, un écosystème axé sur les micro-technologies.

Pour renforcer notre programme de recherche sur les méthodes basées sur le laser pour adapter les propriétés du matériau, nous cherchons un post-doc pour étudier les méthodes avancées de façonnage front d'onde basées sur l'optique adaptative appliquée au contexte de l'interaction laser-matière non linéaire.

Principaux actifs

• Définir des plans de recherche et d'expérimentation pertinents, soutenus par des considérations théoriques et des connaissances de la littérature pertinente.

• Faire rapport et diffuser les résultats de la recherche dans des publications de revues et des conférences internationales.

• Vous êtes très intéressé par la recherche dans le domaine de l'optique non linéaire, des lasers ultrarapides et/ou de l'interaction laser-matière.

jobs.description:
Postdoc position (100%) at the Digital and Cognitive Musicology Lab, EPFL Lausanne

We are looking for a researcher who shares our fascination for musical structure and the musical mind and is ready to tackle it using advanced computational modeling, mathematical modeling, or experimental psychology.

Profile

We thrive on interdisciplinary collaboration. You should hold a PhD in musicology, computer science, cognitive science, psychology, mathematics, or a related field. While you will bring your own specialization, you must possess:

• Strong analytical skills and a track record of planning and conducting empirical research.

• Proficiency in programming and statistics/data science.

• A genuine passion for music and a solid understanding of music.

• Fluent English and a collaborative team spirit.

We offer

• World-Class Research: EPFL is a top-tier international institution. You will join a young, dynamic team integrating diverse disciplines.

• Employment Benefits: Postdocs at EPFL are regular full-term employees with excellent social benefits and competitive salaries.

• Career Growth: Opportunities to gain experience in teaching, mentoring and supervision within a supportive ecosystem.

• Life in Lausanne: Located on the shores of Lake Geneva (Lac Léman) with a view of the Alps, Lausanne offers a picturesque setting with vibrant cultural events and outdoor activities.

Informations

Only applications submitted through the online platform are considered. You are asked to supply:

• A cover letter

• A CV with a publication list

• Contact details for 2 references

Women are strongly encouraged to apply.

For any further information, please contact: martin.rohrmeier@epfl.ch

Review of applications begins March 23, 2026, and continues until the position is filled.

Our research project is funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF).

Contract Start Date : Flexible (Summer 2026 preferred)

Activity Rate : 100%

Contract Type: CDD

Duration: One year, renewable

Reference: 2065

jobs.description:
Mission

The Zenk Lab (NeuroNA Chair in Epigenomics of Neurodevelopmental disorders – EpiGN) is seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher with strong training in computational biology and/or machine learning to join an interdisciplinary project at the interface of single-cell genomics, data integration, and developmental biology.
The project focuses on the integration and analysis of multi-modal single-cell datasets, including scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, scCUT&Tag, HiC, and proteomics, with an emphasis on trajectory inference, regulatory dynamics, and cell fate decisions. A key goal is to integrate multimodal data using machine learning approaches to uncover principles of cellular state transitions. The work will be carried out in close collaboration with other labs at EPFL, offering a uniquely rich environment combining experimental biology and computational genomics.

Main duties and responsibilities

• Working and collaborating on research projects

• Analysis and publication of results

• Build a strong network in the field of research

• Participate in education, and PhD and master student supervision

Profile

• Strong background in computational biology, bioinformatics, machine learning, or a related quantitative field

• Experience with machine learning and/or statistical modeling applied to biological data

• Proven expertise in single-cell data analysis (scRNA-seq and/or scATAC-seq)

• Interest or experience in multi-modal data integration and trajectory inference

• Proficiency in Python and/or R

• Interest in developmental and human biology is highly valued, but not required

• Strong collaborative mindset and ability to work across disciplines

We offer

• A highly interdisciplinary research environment at the interface of ML and biology

• Access to large, state-of-the-art single-cell multi-omics datasets

• Close collaboration with leading groups in single-cell genomics and machine learning

• Strong support for high-impact publications and career development

Informations

Contract Start Date : 06/01/2026

Activity Rate : 100.00

Contract Type: CDD

Duration: 12 months

Reference: 2072

jobs.description:
Mission

The South–North Laboratory for Sustainable Construction and Conservation (SONO Lab) at EPFL is recruiting a full-time PhD Student (100%) within the School of Architecture, Civil and Environmental Engineering (ENAC), based at the EPFL Fribourg associated campus.

SONO Lab investigates low-carbon, climate-responsive and socially inclusive approaches to building design, construction and conservation. Its research combines architectural design, environmental assessment, digital methods, full-scale experimentation, building-performance monitoring and participatory approaches, with a particular focus on collaborations between Europe and Africa.

The successful candidate will contribute to REGEN4BE—Regenerative Design for the Built Environment, a Horizon Europe project developed within the New European Bauhaus framework. REGEN4BE seeks to make regenerative design measurable, interoperable and scalable through digital tools, innovative materials, participatory processes, Living Labs and policy development. Its outputs include a Regenerative Evaluation Framework and the Regenerative Design Intelligence Platform (REDIP). Fribourg is one of the project’s European demonstration and replication sites.

Within REGEN4BE, the candidate will develop and scientifically validate interoperable digital workflows linking Building Information Modelling (BIM), Building Energy Modelling (BEM), Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA), embodied and operational carbon, circularity and material-reuse indicators, building monitoring, sensor data, Post-Occupancy Evaluation (PoE), and feedback from building operation into future design decisions.

The methods will be developed and tested through the REGEN4BE Fribourg demonstration activities, using Smart Living Lab data and infrastructure in close collaboration with the Building2050 team.

As an integrated strand of the doctoral thesis, the candidate will apply and adapt the REGEN4BE framework to selected earth-block and Limestone Calcined Clay Cement (LC3)-based housing systems in African contexts. Building on SONO’s projects and partnerships, this research will examine how local materials, passive environmental strategies, construction processes, whole-life carbon, circularity, repairability, measured building performance and residents’ experience can inform regenerative design.

The European and African research strands will form one coherent doctoral project. The candidate will contribute to a generic interoperability framework within REGEN4BE and assess its transferability and necessary adaptation across different materials, climates, construction cultures and levels of digital infrastructure.

Main duties and responsibilities

As a PhD Student, you will take scientific responsibility for developing and completing your doctoral dissertation, formulate original research questions, and establish a rigorous methodology. You will conduct computational, experimental and field-based research in collaboration with academic, technical, institutional, software-development and industry partners. 
• Your responsibilities will include collecting, managing, analysing and interpreting quantitative and qualitative data, preparing articles for peer-reviewed journals, presenting findings at conferences, workshops and project meetings, contributing to REGEN4BE deliverables, demonstrations and dissemination activities, and participating in teaching and, where appropriate, the supervision of student projects.

Within REGEN4BE, you will contribute to the development and scientific validation of the Regenerative Design Intelligence Platform (REDIP) and its building-data and performance-assessment workflows. You will develop and test interoperable methods linking BIM, openBIM and IFC with building-energy models, Life-Cycle Assessment, whole-life-carbon calculations, circularity indicators, monitoring data, occupant feedback and Post-Occupancy Evaluation. You will investigate data continuity, traceability, uncertainty and interope

descriptionByLocale.it:
Missione

Il South-North Laboratory for Sustainable Construction and Conservation (SONO Lab) di EPFL sta reclutando un PhD Student a tempo pieno (100%) all'interno della School of Architecture, Civil and Environmental Engineering (ENAC), con sede nel campus associato di EPFL Fribourg.

SONO Lab indaga gli approcci a basso tenore di carbonio, a risposta climatica e socialmente inclusi per la progettazione, la costruzione e la conservazione. La sua ricerca combina il design architettonico, la valutazione ambientale, i metodi digitali, la sperimentazione su larga scala, il monitoraggio delle prestazioni edilizie e gli approcci partecipativi, con particolare attenzione alle collaborazioni tra Europa e Africa.

Il candidato di successo contribuirà a REGEN4BE — Design rigenerativo per l'ambiente costruito, un progetto Horizon Europe sviluppato nell'ambito del nuovo quadro europeo Bauhaus. REGEN4BE cerca di rendere il design rigenerativo misurabile, interoperabile e scalabile attraverso strumenti digitali, materiali innovativi, processi partecipativi, Living Labs e sviluppo delle politiche. I suoi risultati includono un quadro di valutazione rigenerativa e la piattaforma di intelligence per il design rigenerativo (REDIP). Fribourg è uno dei siti europei di dimostrazione e replica del progetto.

All'interno di REGEN4BE, il candidato svilupperà e convalidarà scientificamente i flussi di lavoro digitali interoperabili che collegano Building Information Modelling (BIM), Building Energy Modelling (BEM), Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA), carbonio incorporato e operativo, indicatori di circolarità e di riutilizzo dei materiali, monitoraggio degli edifici, dati dei sensori, valutazione post-Occupancy (PoE), e feedback dall'operazione di costruzione alle future decisioni di progettazione.

I metodi saranno sviluppati e testati attraverso le attività dimostrative REGEN4BE Fribourg, utilizzando i dati e le infrastrutture Smart Living Lab in stretta collaborazione con il team Building2050.

Come filo integrato della tesi di dottorato, il candidato applicherà e adattarà il quadro REGEN4BE a blocchi terrestri selezionati e Limestone Calcined Clay Cement (LC3)-based sistemi di alloggio in contesti africani. Sulla base dei progetti e dei partenariati di SONO, questa ricerca esaminerà come materiali locali, strategie ambientali passive, processi di costruzione, carbonio di tutta la vita, circolarità, riparabilità, prestazioni di costruzione misurate e l’esperienza dei residenti possano informare il design rigenerativo.

I fili di ricerca europei e africani costituiranno un progetto medico coerente. Il candidato contribuirà ad un generico quadro di interoperabilità all'interno di REGEN4BE e valuterà la sua trasferibilità e l'adattamento necessario in diversi materiali, climi, culture edili e livelli di infrastruttura digitale.

Principali doveri e responsabilità

In qualità di PhD Student, ti assumerai la responsabilità scientifica per lo sviluppo e il completamento della tua tesi di dottorato, formulare domande di ricerca originali e stabilire una metodologia rigorosa. Condurrà la ricerca computazionale, sperimentale e basata sul campo in collaborazione con partner accademici, tecnici, istituzionali, software-sviluppo e industria.
• Le vostre responsabilità comprendono la raccolta, la gestione, l'analisi e l'interpretazione di dati quantitativi e qualitativi, la preparazione di articoli per riviste peer-reviewed, la presentazione dei risultati a conferenze, workshop e incontri di progetto, contribuendo a REGEN4BE consegnabili, dimostrazioni e attività di diffusione, e la partecipazione all'insegnamento e, se del caso, alla supervisione dei progetti studenteschi.

All'interno di REGEN4BE, contribuirai allo sviluppo e alla validazione scientifica della Piattaforma di Intelligenza del Design Rigenerativo (REDIP) e dei suoi flussi di lavoro di data ed esecuzione-valutazione. Svilupperai e testerai metodi interoperabili che collegano BIM, openBIM e IFC con modelli di costruzione-energia, valutazione del ciclo vitale, calcoli interi-carbonio, indicatori di circolarità, dati di monitoraggio, feedback degli occupanti e valutazione post-Occupancy. Indagherete la continuità dei dati, la tracciabilità, l'incertezza e l'interope
descriptionByLocale.en:
Mission

The South–North Laboratory for Sustainable Construction and Conservation (SONO Lab) at EPFL is recruiting a full-time PhD Student (100%) within the School of Architecture, Civil and Environmental Engineering (ENAC), based at the EPFL Fribourg associated campus.

SONO Lab investigates low-carbon, climate-responsive and socially inclusive approaches to building design, construction and conservation. Its research combines architectural design, environmental assessment, digital methods, full-scale experimentation, building-performance monitoring and participatory approaches, with a particular focus on collaborations between Europe and Africa.

The successful candidate will contribute to REGEN4BE—Regenerative Design for the Built Environment, a Horizon Europe project developed within the New European Bauhaus framework. REGEN4BE seeks to make regenerative design measurable, interoperable and scalable through digital tools, innovative materials, participatory processes, Living Labs and policy development. Its outputs include a Regenerative Evaluation Framework and the Regenerative Design Intelligence Platform (REDIP). Fribourg is one of the project’s European demonstration and replication sites.

Within REGEN4BE, the candidate will develop and scientifically validate interoperable digital workflows linking Building Information Modelling (BIM), Building Energy Modelling (BEM), Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA), embodied and operational carbon, circularity and material-reuse indicators, building monitoring, sensor data, Post-Occupancy Evaluation (PoE), and feedback from building operation into future design decisions.

The methods will be developed and tested through the REGEN4BE Fribourg demonstration activities, using Smart Living Lab data and infrastructure in close collaboration with the Building2050 team.

As an integrated strand of the doctoral thesis, the candidate will apply and adapt the REGEN4BE framework to selected earth-block and Limestone Calcined Clay Cement (LC3)-based housing systems in African contexts. Building on SONO’s projects and partnerships, this research will examine how local materials, passive environmental strategies, construction processes, whole-life carbon, circularity, repairability, measured building performance and residents’ experience can inform regenerative design.

The European and African research strands will form one coherent doctoral project. The candidate will contribute to a generic interoperability framework within REGEN4BE and assess its transferability and necessary adaptation across different materials, climates, construction cultures and levels of digital infrastructure.

Main duties and responsibilities

As a PhD Student, you will take scientific responsibility for developing and completing your doctoral dissertation, formulate original research questions, and establish a rigorous methodology. You will conduct computational, experimental and field-based research in collaboration with academic, technical, institutional, software-development and industry partners. 
• Your responsibilities will include collecting, managing, analysing and interpreting quantitative and qualitative data, preparing articles for peer-reviewed journals, presenting findings at conferences, workshops and project meetings, contributing to REGEN4BE deliverables, demonstrations and dissemination activities, and participating in teaching and, where appropriate, the supervision of student projects.

Within REGEN4BE, you will contribute to the development and scientific validation of the Regenerative Design Intelligence Platform (REDIP) and its building-data and performance-assessment workflows. You will develop and test interoperable methods linking BIM, openBIM and IFC with building-energy models, Life-Cycle Assessment, whole-life-carbon calculations, circularity indicators, monitoring data, occupant feedback and Post-Occupancy Evaluation. You will investigate data continuity, traceability, uncertainty and interope
descriptionByLocale.de:
Mission

Das Süd-Nord-Labor für nachhaltiges Bauen und Konservieren (SONO Lab) an der EPFL rekrutiert einen Vollzeit-Doktoranden (100%) innerhalb der School of Architecture, Civil and Environmental Engineering (ENAC) mit Sitz auf dem EPFL Fribourg assoziierten Campus.

SONO Lab untersucht kohlenstoffarme, klimaresponsive und sozial integrative Ansätze für Gebäudeplanung, Bau und Erhaltung. Seine Forschung kombiniert architektonische Gestaltung, Umweltverträglichkeitsprüfung, digitale Methoden, umfassende Experimente, Überwachung der Gebäudeleistung und partizipative Ansätze mit einem besonderen Fokus auf die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Europa und Afrika.

Der erfolgreiche Kandidat wird einen Beitrag zu REGEN4BE – Regenerative Design for the Built Environment leisten, einem Horizon Europe-Projekt, das im Rahmen des Neuen Europäischen Bauhauses entwickelt wurde. REGEN4BE will regeneratives Design durch digitale Tools, innovative Materialien, partizipative Prozesse, Living Labs und Politikentwicklung messbar, interoperabel und skalierbar machen. Zu den Ergebnissen gehören ein Regenerative Evaluation Framework und die Regenerative Design Intelligence Platform (REDIP). Fribourg ist einer der europäischen Demonstrations- und Replikationsstandorte des Projekts.

Innerhalb von REGEN4BE wird der Kandidat interoperable digitale Workflows entwickeln und wissenschaftlich validieren, die Building Information Modeling (BIM), Building Energy Modeling (BEM), Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA), verkörperte und operative Kohlenstoff-, Zirkularitäts- und Materialwiederverwendungsindikatoren, Gebäudeüberwachung, Sensordaten, Post-Occupancy Evaluation (PoE) und Feedback aus dem Gebäudebetrieb zu zukünftigen Designentscheidungen verbinden.

Die Methoden werden im Rahmen der REGEN4BE-Demonstrationsaktivitäten in Fribourg entwickelt und getestet, wobei Daten und Infrastruktur des Smart Living Lab in enger Zusammenarbeit mit dem Team von Building2050 verwendet werden.

Als integrierter Teil der Doktorarbeit wird der Kandidat das REGEN4BE-Framework auf ausgewählte Erdblock- und Kalkstein-Tonzement (LC3)-basierte Gehäusesysteme im afrikanischen Kontext anwenden und anpassen. Aufbauend auf den Projekten und Partnerschaften von SONO wird diese Forschung untersuchen, wie lokale Materialien, passive Umweltstrategien, Bauprozesse, Kohlenstoff aus der gesamten Lebensdauer, Zirkularität, Reparaturfähigkeit, gemessene Gebäudeleistung und die Erfahrung der Bewohner das regenerative Design beeinflussen können.

Die europäischen und afrikanischen Forschungsstränge werden ein zusammenhängendes Doktorandenprojekt bilden. Der Kandidat wird zu einem generischen Interoperabilitätsrahmen innerhalb von REGEN4BE beitragen und seine Übertragbarkeit und notwendige Anpassung an verschiedene Materialien, Klimazonen, Baukulturen und Ebenen der digitalen Infrastruktur bewerten.

Hauptaufgaben und Zuständigkeiten

Als Doktorand übernehmen Sie die wissenschaftliche Verantwortung für die Entwicklung und den Abschluss Ihrer Dissertation, formulieren originelle Forschungsfragen und etablieren eine strenge Methodik. Sie führen computergestützte, experimentelle und feldbasierte Forschung in Zusammenarbeit mit akademischen, technischen, institutionellen, Softwareentwicklungs- und Industriepartnern durch.
• Ihre Aufgaben umfassen das Sammeln, Verwalten, Analysieren und Interpretieren quantitativer und qualitativer Daten, die Vorbereitung von Artikeln für von Experten begutachtete Zeitschriften, die Präsentation von Ergebnissen auf Konferenzen, Workshops und Projekttreffen, den Beitrag zu den Ergebnissen von REGEN4BE, Demonstrationen und Verbreitungsaktivitäten sowie die Teilnahme an der Lehre und gegebenenfalls der Betreuung von Studentenprojekten.

Innerhalb von REGEN4BE tragen Sie zur Entwicklung und wissenschaftlichen Validierung der Regenerative Design Intelligence Platform (REDIP) und ihrer Workflows für Gebäudedaten und Leistungsbewertung bei. Sie entwickeln und testen interoperable Methoden, die BIM, openBIM und IFC mit Gebäudeenergiemodellen, Life-Cycle-Bewertung, Gesamtlebenskohlenstoffberechnungen, Zirkularitätsindikatoren, Überwachungsdaten, Insassen-Feedback und Post-Occupancy-Bewertung verbinden. Sie untersuchen Datenkontinuität, Rückverfolgbarkeit, Unsicherheit und Interope
descriptionByLocale.fr:
Mission

Le Laboratoire Sud-Nord pour la Construction et la Conservation Durables (SONO Lab) de l'EPFL recrute un doctorant à plein temps (100%) à l'Ecole d'Architecture, Génie Civil et Environnemental (ENAC), basée sur le campus associé à l'EPFL Fribourg.

SONO Lab étudie les approches à faible émission de carbone, adaptées au climat et socialement inclusives de la conception, de la construction et de la conservation des bâtiments. Ses recherches combinent la conception architecturale, l'évaluation environnementale, les méthodes numériques, l'expérimentation à grande échelle, le suivi des performances du bâtiment et les approches participatives, en mettant l'accent sur les collaborations entre l'Europe et l'Afrique.

Le candidat retenu contribuera au projet REGEN4BE – Design régénératif pour l'environnement bâti, un projet Horizon Europe développé dans le cadre du nouveau Bauhaus européen. REGEN4BE cherche à rendre la conception régénératrice mesurable, interopérable et évolutive grâce à des outils numériques, des matériaux innovants, des processus participatifs, des laboratoires vivants et l'élaboration de politiques. Ses résultats comprennent un cadre d'évaluation régénératrice et la plateforme d'intelligence de conception régénératrice (REDIP). Fribourg est l'un des sites européens de démonstration et de réplication du projet.

Au sein de REGEN4BE, le candidat élaborera et validera scientifiquement des flux de travail numériques interopérables reliant la modélisation de l'information sur les bâtiments (BIM), la modélisation de l'énergie des bâtiments (BEM), l'évaluation du cycle de vie (LCA), des indicateurs de carbone, de la circularité et de la réutilisation des matériaux incorporés et opérationnels, la surveillance des bâtiments, les données des capteurs, l'évaluation post-occupation (EP) et la rétroaction de l'exploitation des bâtiments aux décisions de conception futures.

Les méthodes seront développées et testées dans le cadre des activités de démonstration REGEN4BE Fribourg, en utilisant les données et l'infrastructure du Smart Living Lab en étroite collaboration avec l'équipe Building2050.

En tant que volet intégré de la thèse de doctorat, le candidat appliquera et adaptera le cadre REGEN4BE à certains systèmes de logement à base de blocs de terre et de ciment calcaire calciné (LC3) dans des contextes africains. S'appuyant sur les projets et les partenariats SONO, cette recherche examinera comment les matériaux locaux, les stratégies environnementales passives, les processus de construction, le carbone tout-vivant, la circularité, la réparabilité, les performances mesurées des bâtiments et l'expérience des résidents peuvent éclairer la conception régénérative.

Les volets de recherche européen et africain formeront un projet de doctorat cohérent. Le candidat contribuera à l'élaboration d'un cadre d'interopérabilité générique au sein de REGEN4BE et évaluera sa transférabilité et l'adaptation nécessaire à différents matériaux, climats, cultures de construction et niveaux d'infrastructure numérique.

Principales fonctions et responsabilités

En tant qu'étudiant en doctorat, vous assumerez la responsabilité scientifique d'élaborer et de compléter votre thèse de doctorat, de formuler des questions de recherche originales et d'établir une méthodologie rigoureuse. Vous effectuerez des recherches informatiques, expérimentales et sur le terrain en collaboration avec des partenaires universitaires, techniques, institutionnels, de développement de logiciels et de l'industrie.
• Vos responsabilités comprendront la collecte, la gestion, l'analyse et l'interprétation de données quantitatives et qualitatives, la préparation d'articles pour des revues évaluées par des pairs, la présentation des résultats lors de conférences, d'ateliers et de réunions de projets, la contribution aux produits livrables REGEN4BE, les démonstrations et les activités de diffusion, ainsi que la participation à l'enseignement et, le cas échéant, la supervision de projets étudiants.

Au sein de REGEN4BE, vous contribuerez au développement et à la validation scientifique de la plateforme d'intelligence de conception régénératrice (REDIP) et de ses workflows de construction-données et d'évaluation des performances. Vous développerez et testerez des méthodes interopérables reliant BIM, openBIM et IFC avec des modèles building-énergie, Life-Cycle Assessment, des calculs carbone-tout-vie, des indicateurs de circularité, des données de surveillance, des commentaires des occupants et une évaluation post-occupation. Vous étudierez la continuité des données, la traçabilité, l'incertitude et l'interope

jobs.description:
General

The Artificial Intelligence in Molecular Medicine (AIMM) Lab, led by Prof. Charlotte Bunne at EPFL, sits at the interface of computer science, artificial intelligence, and biomedical applications. The lab is affiliated with both the School of Computer and Communication Sciences and the School of Life Sciences, as well as the EPFL AI Center.

We are recruiting a postdoctoral researcher with strong expertise in modern AI, in particular the development of generative AI technologies such as diffusion models, flow matching, generative transformers, or related architectures. The position is highly methodological and focuses on developing new generative modeling approaches, scalable training algorithms, and foundation model technologies.

The role is suited for candidates with a strong machine learning background who are excited to advance the state of the art in generative AI. Prior experience with biological or biomedical data is not required. The position comes with dedicated access to the Swiss National Supercomputing Centre and the Swiss AI Initiative, and offers opportunities for collaboration across AI, science, and industry.

Research directions include

• Generative AI: development of diffusion models, flow matching, autoregressive models, normalizing flows, or related generative architectures.

• Foundation model development: novel pretraining objectives, scalable architectures, tokenization, and model adaptation strategies.

• Scalable AI training: distributed training, efficient fine-tuning, evaluation, and deployment on large-scale compute.

• Multimodal learning: representation learning and generative modeling across heterogeneous data modalities.

• AI for scientific discovery: methodological advances with potential applications across biomedical and scientific domains.

We are looking for candidates with

• A PhD in machine learning, computer science, applied mathematics, statistics, physics, engineering, or a closely related field, completed or near completion.

• Demonstrated expertise in generative AI, such as diffusion models, flow matching, normalizing flows, VAEs, generative transformers, or related methods.

• Strong programming skills and experience with modern deep learning frameworks.

• Experience with large-scale model training, distributed training, or substantial compute.

• A strong publication record at top-tier machine learning conferences and/or relevant scientific journals.

• Excellent communication skills and enthusiasm for ambitious, interdisciplinary AI research.

We offer

• Competitive EPFL postdoc salary and full social benefits.

• Dedicated compute allocation on CSCS and the Swiss AI Initiative.

• A methodologically ambitious research environment at the interface of generative AI, foundation models, and scientific AI.

• Opportunities for collaboration with academic and industry partners.

• Mentorship toward an independent academic or industry research career.

• An international, collaborative environment at one of Europe's leading technical universities

Activity rate : 100%.

Start date : ideally Fall 2026, with later start dates possible by arrangement.

To apply, please send a CV, a brief statement of research interests (1 page), and the names of two references. More information via aimm.epfl.ch . Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

descriptionByLocale.it:
Informazioni sul laboratorio AIMM

Il Laboratorio di Intelligenza Artificiale in Medicina Molecolare (AIMM), condotto dalla Prof.ssa Charlotte Bunne all'EPFL, si occupa dell'interfaccia tra informatica, intelligenza artificiale e applicazioni biomediche. Il laboratorio è affiliato sia alla Scuola di Scienze del Computer e della Comunicazione che alla Scuola di Scienze della Vita, nonché al Centro EPFL AI.

Panoramica della posizione

Stiamo reclutando un ricercatore postdoctorale con una forte esperienza in AI moderna, in particolare lo sviluppo di tecnologie di AI generative come modelli di diffusione, matching di flusso, trasformatori generativi, o architetture correlate. La posizione è altamente metodologica e si concentra sullo sviluppo di nuovi approcci di modellazione generativa, algoritmi di formazione di scalabilità, e tecnologie di modelli di fondazione.

Il ruolo è adatto ai candidati con un forte background di apprendimento automatico che sono evocati per far progredire lo stato dell'arte in AI generativo. Non è richiesta una precedente esperienza con dati biologici o biomedici. La posizione viene fornita con un accesso dedicato al Centro nazionale svizzero di supercomputing e l'Iniziativa svizzera AI, e offre opportunità di collaborazione tra AI, scienza e industria.

Indicazioni di ricerca

Le indicazioni di ricerca includono

- Sviluppo di modelli di diffusione, di modelli di flusso, di modelli progressivi, di flussi di normalizzazione o di architetture generative correlate. - Sviluppo di modelli di fondazione: nuovi obiettivi di preformazione, architetture di scalabilità, tokenizzazione e strategie di adattamento dei modelli. - Formazione di base: formazione distribuita, messa a punto efficiente, valutazione e distribuzione su larga scala. - Apprendimento multimodale: apprendimento della rappresentazione e modellazione generativa attraverso modalità di dati eterogenei.

- AI per la scoperta scientifica: progressi metodologici con potenziali applicazioni in ambiti biomedici e scientifici.

Requisiti

Stiamo cercando candidati con

- Dottorato di ricerca in Machine Learning, informatica, matematica applicata, statistica, fisica, ingegneria o un campo strettamente correlato, completato o prossimo completamento. - Esperta dimostrativa in AI generativo, come modelli di diffusione, matching dei flussi, normalizzazione dei flussi, VAE, trasformatori generativi, o metodi correlati. - Forte capacità di programmazione ed esperienza con quadri di apprendimento profondo moderni. - Esperienza con formazione su grande scala di modelli, formazione distribuita, o calcolo sostanziale. - Un forte record di pubblicazione presso le conferenze di apprendimento automatico di livello superiore e / o riviste scientifiche pertinenti.

- Eccellenti capacità comunicative ed entusiasmo per una ricerca ambiziosa e interdisciplinare.

Cosa offriamo

- Località di calcolo dedicate su CSCS e l'iniziativa svizzera AI. - Un ambiente di ricerca metodologicamente ambizioso all'interfaccia di AI generativo, modelli di fondazione e AI scientifico. - Opportunità di collaborazione con partner accademici e industriali. - Mentoralizzazione verso una carriera accademica o di ricerca industriale indipendente. - Un ambiente internazionale e collaborativo in una delle principali università tecniche europee

Informazioni aggiuntive

Tasso di attività: 100%.

Data di inizio: idealmente caduta 2026, con date di inizio successive possibile per disposizione.

Contatto

Per richiedere, si prega di inviare un CV, una breve dichiarazione di interessi di ricerca (1 pagina), e i nomi di due riferimenti. Ulteriori informazioni via imm.epfl.ch. Le domande sono riviste su base continuativa.

descriptionByLocale.de:
Über das Amm Lab

Das Labor für Künstliche Intelligenz in der Molekularen Medizin (Amm) unter der Leitung von Prof. Charlotte Bunne von EPFL ist an der Schnittstelle von Informatik, Künstlicher Intelligenz und biomedizinischen Anwendungen angesiedelt. Es ist sowohl mit der School of Computer and Communication Sciences als auch mit der School of Life Sciences sowie dem EPFL AI Center verbunden.

Positionsübersicht

Wir rekrutieren einen Postdoc-Forscher mit starker Expertise in der modernen KI, insbesondere die Entwicklung generativer KI-Technologien wie Diffusionsmodelle, Flow Matching, generative Transformatoren oder verwandte Architekturen. Die Position ist hochmethodologisch und konzentriert sich auf die Entwicklung neuer generativer Modellierungsansätze, skalierbare Schulungsalgorithmen und Fundamentmodelltechnologien.

Die Rolle ist geeignet für Bewerber mit einem starken maschinellen Lernhintergrund, die begeistert sind, den Stand der Technik in generativer KI voranzutreiben. Vorkenntnisse mit biologischen oder biomedizinischen Daten sind nicht erforderlich. Die Position bietet einen engagierten Zugang zum Schweizerischen Nationalen Supercomputing Center und der Schweizer KI-Initiative und bietet Möglichkeiten für die Zusammenarbeit in KI, Wissenschaft und Industrie.

Forschungsanweisungen

Forschungsrichtungen sind:

- Generative KI: Entwicklung von Diffusionsmodellen, Flow Matching, Autore-Gigrate-Modelle, Normalisierungsflüssen oder verwandten generativen Architekturen. - Basismodellentwicklung: neuartige Vorschulungsziele, skalierbare Architekturen, Tokenisierung und Modellanpassungsstrategien. - Skalierbares KI-Training: verteiltes Training, effiziente Feinabstimmung, Auswertung und Bereitstellung auf großräumigen Rechenprozessen. - Multimodales Lernen: Repräsentationslernen und generative Modellierung über heterogene Datenmodalitäten hinweg.

- KI für wissenschaftliche Entdeckung: methodische Fortschritte mit potenziellen Anwendungen in biomedizinischen und wissenschaftlichen Bereichen.

Anforderungen

Wir suchen Kandidaten mit

- Ein Doktorat in Maschinenbau, Informatik, angewandter Mathematik, Statistik, Physik, Ingenieurwesen oder einem eng verwandten Bereich, abgeschlossen oder in der Nähe abgeschlossen. - Nachweis der Expertise in generativen KI, wie Diffusionsmodelle, Flow Matching, Normalisierung von Flüssen, VAEs, generative Transformatoren oder verwandte Methoden. - Starke Programmierfähigkeiten und Erfahrungen mit modernen Deep-Learning-Frameworks. - Erfahrung mit groß angelegten Modelltrainings, verteilten Schulungen oder wesentlichen Berechnungen. - Eine starke Publikationsbilanz auf hochkarätigen Machine-Learning-Konferenzen und/oder einschlägigen wissenschaftlichen Zeitschriften.

descriptionByLocale.fr:
General

The Artificial Intelligence in Molecular Medicine (AIMM) Lab, led by Prof. Charlotte Bunne at EPFL, sits at the interface of computer science, artificial intelligence, and biomedical applications. The lab is affiliated with both the School of Computer and Communication Sciences and the School of Life Sciences, as well as the EPFL AI Center.

We are recruiting a postdoctoral researcher with strong expertise in modern AI, in particular the development of generative AI technologies such as diffusion models, flow matching, generative transformers, or related architectures. The position is highly methodological and focuses on developing new generative modeling approaches, scalable training algorithms, and foundation model technologies.

The role is suited for candidates with a strong machine learning background who are excited to advance the state of the art in generative AI. Prior experience with biological or biomedical data is not required. The position comes with dedicated access to the Swiss National Supercomputing Centre and the Swiss AI Initiative, and offers opportunities for collaboration across AI, science, and industry.

Research directions include

• Generative AI: development of diffusion models, flow matching, autoregressive models, normalizing flows, or related generative architectures.

• Foundation model development: novel pretraining objectives, scalable architectures, tokenization, and model adaptation strategies.

• Scalable AI training: distributed training, efficient fine-tuning, evaluation, and deployment on large-scale compute.

• Multimodal learning: representation learning and generative modeling across heterogeneous data modalities.

• AI for scientific discovery: methodological advances with potential applications across biomedical and scientific domains.

We are looking for candidates with

• A PhD in machine learning, computer science, applied mathematics, statistics, physics, engineering, or a closely related field, completed or near completion.

• Demonstrated expertise in generative AI, such as diffusion models, flow matching, normalizing flows, VAEs, generative transformers, or related methods.

• Strong programming skills and experience with modern deep learning frameworks.

• Experience with large-scale model training, distributed training, or substantial compute.

• A strong publication record at top-tier machine learning conferences and/or relevant scientific journals.

• Excellent communication skills and enthusiasm for ambitious, interdisciplinary AI research.

• Competitive EPFL postdoc salary and full social benefits.

• A methodologically ambitious research environment at the interface of generative AI, foundation models, and scientific AI.

jobs.description:
Mission

A postdoctoral position is available in the laboratory of Prof. Alex Persat (EPFL School of Life Sciences, https://www.p-lab.science/ ) to establish a new image-based drug screening platform targeting gram-negative pathogens ( Klebsiella pneumoniae , Acinetobacter baumannii , Pseudomonas aeruginosa ). The project will combine single-cell/single-bacterium imaging approaches with the lab's tissue-engineered infection models to identify and characterize compounds active against these priority pathogens.

Main duties and responsibilities

• Design and build a microscopy-based phenotypic screening pipeline (live imaging, high-content, single-cell resolution) to assay compound activity

• Develop imaging assays capable of distinguishing mechanism of action (e.g. growth inhibition, biofilm/attachment disruption, membrane integrity)

• Develop or adapt image analysis and quantification pipelines with AI support to handle screen-scale data

• Follow up on screening hits to identify their molecular target or mechanism of action (e.g. via genetic, chemical-biology, or biophysical approaches), with support from other lab members' expertise in microbiology and drug discovery

• Collaborate with the lab's discovery and design efforts (natural products, AI-enabled molecular design) to feed prioritized targets and hits back into upstream design

• Apply the pipeline to screens in both standard culture and, in collaboration with other lab members, the group's organoid/tissue-engineered infection models (airway, gut) to prioritize physiologically relevant hits

• Co-supervise PhD students and contribute to method development, data management, and grant reporting

Profile

• PhD in microbiology, biophysics, bioengineering, or a related field (completed or near completion) with at least a first author publication.

• Hands-on experience with quantitative microscopy (live-cell imaging, high-content screening, or single-cell/single-bacterium imaging)

• Comfort with image analysis pipelines and scripting (Python), experience integrating ML-based image analysis is a plus but not required

• Interest in working across the interface of imaging, microbiology, and drug discovery

We offer

• The opportunity to build a new screening platform from the ground up, with significant ownership over pipeline design

• Access to the lab's existing imaging/biophysics infrastructure and tissue-engineered infection model systems

• Integration within the NCCR AntiResist consortium, with access to a broad network of AMR-focused groups across Switzerland

• Competitive salary (see EPFL postdoc salary scale)

• Support for independent fellowship applications (EMBO, HFSP, MSCA) where relevant

Informations

Applicants should submit

• A cover letter (PDF, up to 2 pages) describing research interests, achievements and fit

• A CV with publication list

• Contact details for 3 referees

Additional information

• Contract start date: negotiable

• For informal inquiries, contact: alexandre.persat@epfl.ch

• Applications accepted only through the EPFL careers portal

Activity Rate : 100.00

Contract Type: CDD

Duration: 1 year, renewable

Reference: 2441

descriptionByLocale.it:
Missione

Una posizione post-dottorale è disponibile nel laboratorio del Prof. Alex Persat (EPFL School of Life Sciences, https://www.p-lab.science/ ) per stabilire una nuova piattaforma di screening della droga basata sull'immagine che fissa gli agenti patogeni gram-negativi ( Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter Baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa). Il progetto unirà approcci di imaging a singola cellula/singola-batterio con i modelli di infezione creati dai tessuti del laboratorio per identificare e caratterizzare i composti attivi contro queste priorità agenti patogeni.

Principali doveri e responsabilità

• Progettare e costruire una pipeline di screening fenotico a base di microscopia (immaginazione dal vivo, alto contenuto, risoluzione di singole cellule) per l'attività di analisi dei composti

• Attacchi che immaginano lo sviluppo in grado di distinguere il meccanismo di azione (ad esempio inibizione della crescita, interruzione del biofilm/attacco, integrità della membrana)

• Sviluppo o adattamento dell'analisi delle immagini e delle pipeline di quantificazione con il supporto AI per gestire i dati su scala di schermo

• Seguire i colpi di screening per identificare il loro obiettivo molecolare o il meccanismo di azione (ad esempio attraverso approcci genetici, chimici o biofisici), con il supporto delle competenze di altri membri del laboratorio in microbiologia e scoperta della droga

• Collabora con gli sforzi di scoperta e progettazione del laboratorio (prodotti naturali, progettazione molecolare abilitata all'IA) per alimentare obiettivi prioritari e colpi di nuovo nel design a monte

• Applicare l'oleodotto allo schermo sia nella cultura standard che, in collaborazione con altri membri del laboratorio, i modelli di infezione organoid/tissue-engineered del gruppo (airway, gut) per privilegiare i risultati fisiologicamente segnalati

• Co-supervise PhD studenti e contributore allo sviluppo della metodologia, alla gestione dei dati e alla rendicontazione

Profilo

• PhD in microbiologia, biofisica, bioingegneria, o un campo correlato (completato o quasi completato) con almeno una prima pubblicazione dell'autore.

• Esperienza a mano con microscopia quantitativa (immaginazione a celle vive, screening ad alto contenuto, o immagini a singola cella / singolo batterio)

• Il comfort con l'analisi delle immagini e lo scripting (Python), l'esperienza che integra l'analisi delle immagini basata su ML è un obiettivo non richiesto

• Interessi nel lavorare attraverso l'interfaccia di immaginare, microbiologia e scoperta di droga

Offriamo

• L'opportunità di costruire una nuova piattaforma di screening da zero, con una notevole proprietà sulla progettazione di pipeline

• Accesso ai sistemi esistenti di imaging/biofisica del laboratorio e ai modelli di infezione creati dai tessuti

• Integrazione all'interno del consorzio NCCR AntiResist, con accesso ad una vasta rete di gruppi focalizzati su AMR in tutta la Svizzera

• Stipendio competitivo (vedi scala salariale postdoc EPFL)

• Supporto per le applicazioni di borsa di studio indipendenti (EMBO, HFSP, MSCA) laddove pertinenti

Informazioni

I candidati devono presentare

• Una lettera di presentazione (PDF, fino a 2 pagine) che descrive interessi di ricerca, risultati e vestibilità

• Un CV con lista di pubblicazione

• Contatti per 3 referenze

Ulteriori informazioni

• Data di inizio del contratto: negoziabile

• Per informazioni, contattare: alexandre.persat@epfl.ch

• Applicazioni accettate solo attraverso il portale di carriera EPFL

Tasso di attività: 100.00

Tipo di contratto: CDD

Durata: 1 anno, rinnovabile

descriptionByLocale.de:
Mission

Eine Postdoc-Stelle ist im Labor von Prof. Alex Persat (EPFL School of Life Sciences, https://www.p-lab.science/ ) zur Einrichtung einer neuen bildbasierten Arzneimittel-Screening-Plattform zur Einstellung gramnegativer Pathogene (Klebsiella pneumoniae , Acinetobacter Baumannii , Pseudomonas aeruginosa ). Das Projekt wird Einzelzell-/Einzelbakterium-Imaginationsansätze mit den Gewebe-entwickelten Infektionsmodellen des Labors kombinieren, um Verbindungen zu identifizieren und zu charakterisieren, die gegen diese prioritären Pathogene aktiv sind.

Hauptaufgaben und Zuständigkeiten

• Entwerfen und Bauen einer mikroskopiebasierten phänotischen Screening-Pipeline (Live-Imagining, High-Content, Einzelzellauflösung) zur Assay-Verbindungsaktivität

• Entwicklungsvorstellung von Angriffen, die den Wirkungsmechanismus unterscheiden können (z. B. Wachstumshemmung, Biofilm-/Anhaftungsstörung, Membranintegrität)

• Entwicklung oder Anpassung von Bildanalyse- und Quantifizierungspipelines mit KI-Unterstützung für den Umgang mit Daten im Bildschirmmaßstab

• Follow-up bei Screening-Hits zur Identifizierung ihres molekularen Ziels oder Wirkungsmechanismus (z. B. über genetische, chemische oder biophysikalische Ansätze) mit Unterstützung der Expertise anderer Labormitglieder in Mikrobiologie und Wirkstoffforschung

• Zusammenarbeit mit den Entdeckungs- und Designbemühungen des Labors (Naturprodukte, AI-fähiges molekulares Design), um priorisierte Ziele zu speisen und in das Upstream-Design zurückzukehren

• Wenden Sie die Pipeline sowohl in der Standardkultur als auch in Zusammenarbeit mit anderen Labormitgliedern in den organoiden / gewebetechnischen Infektionsmodellen der Gruppe (Airway, Darm) an, um physiologische Treffer zu priorisieren

• Co-Betreuung von Doktoranden und Mitwirkenden für Methodikentwicklung, Datenmanagement und Stipendienberichterstattung

Profil

• PhD in Mikrobiologie, Biophysik, Bioengineering oder einem verwandten Bereich (abgeschlossen oder kurz vor Abschluss) mit mindestens einer Erstveröffentlichung.

• Praktische Erfahrung mit quantitativer Mikroskopie (Live-Cell-Imagination, High-Content-Screening oder Einzelzell- / Einzelbakterium-Imagination)

• Komfort mit Bildanalyse-Pipelines und Skripting (Python), Erfahrung mit der Integration von ML-basierter Bildanalyse ist ein Ziel, das nicht erforderlich ist

• Interesse an der Arbeit über die Schnittstelle von Vorstellungskraft, Mikrobiologie und Wirkstoffforschung

Wir bieten

• Die Möglichkeit, eine neue Screening-Plattform von Grund auf zu bauen, mit erheblicher Beteiligung am Pipeline-Design

• Zugriff auf die bestehende Vorstellungs-/Biophysik-Infrastruktur des Labors und gewebebasierte Infektionsmodellsysteme

Mission

A postdoctoral position is available in the laboratory of Prof. Alex Persat (EPFL School of Life Sciences, https://www.p-lab.science/ ) to establish a new image-based drug screening platform targeting gram-negative pathogens ( Klebsiella pneumoniae , Acinetobacter baumannii , Pseudomonas aeruginosa ). The project will combine single-cell/single-bacterium imaging approaches with the lab's tissue-engineered infection models to identify and characterize compounds active against these priority pathogens.

Main duties and responsibilities

• Design and build a microscopy-based phenotypic screening pipeline (live imaging, high-content, single-cell resolution) to assay compound activity

• Develop imaging assays capable of distinguishing mechanism of action (e.g. growth inhibition, biofilm/attachment disruption, membrane integrity)

• Develop or adapt image analysis and quantification pipelines with AI support to handle screen-scale data

• Follow up on screening hits to identify their molecular target or mechanism of action (e.g. via genetic, chemical-biology, or biophysical approaches), with support from other lab members' expertise in microbiology and drug discovery

• Collaborate with the lab's discovery and design efforts (natural products, AI-enabled molecular design) to feed prioritized targets and hits back into upstream design

• Apply the pipeline to screens in both standard culture and, in collaboration with other lab members, the group's organoid/tissue-engineered infection models (airway, gut) to prioritize physiologically relevant hits

• Co-supervise PhD students and contribute to method development, data management, and grant reporting

Profile

• PhD in microbiology, biophysics, bioengineering, or a related field (completed or near completion) with at least a first author publication.

• Hands-on experience with quantitative microscopy (live-cell imaging, high-content screening, or single-cell/single-bacterium imaging)

• Comfort with image analysis pipelines and scripting (Python), experience integrating ML-based image analysis is a plus but not required

• Interest in working across the interface of imaging, microbiology, and drug discovery

We offer

• The opportunity to build a new screening platform from the ground up, with significant ownership over pipeline design

• Access to the lab's existing imaging/biophysics infrastructure and tissue-engineered infection model systems

• Integration within the NCCR AntiResist consortium, with access to a broad network of AMR-focused groups across Switzerland

jobs.description:
Mission

We are offering two challenging positions as a full-time (100%) PhD Student at ENAC at EPFL, Lausanne, Switzerland. Our Laboratory EESD is focused on investigating the seismic behavior of reinforced concrete and unreinforced masonry buildings. Our approaches include numerical and mechanical modeling, large-scale testing as well as data-driven methods. The PhD candidates will contribute to advancing the understanding of the seismic behavior of historic brick masonry building aggregates through a combination of large-scale experimental testing, field investigations, and numerical simulations. The research will focus on the behavior and interaction of buildings within masonry aggregates, supporting the development of innovative assessment approaches and resilient retrofit solutions for historic urban environments exposed to earthquake risk.

You will be working on the ZAGGREGATE project, a collaborative research initiative between EPFL, University of Zagreb, and other academic and professional partners. The project aims to improve the understanding, assessment and rehabilitation of historic masonry building aggregates in seismic regions. The successful candidates will join a team of researchers working at the interface of structural engineering, earthquake engineering, and heritage conservation, and will have opportunities for collaboration and research visits in Croatia.

Main duties and responsibilities

As a PhD student you will be expected to:

• Conduct original doctoral research using experimental, numerical, and analytical methods to investigate the seismic response of masonry buildings as stand-alone buildings and within aggregates

• Contribute to the development of innovative assessment methodologies and resilient retrofit strategies for historic urban environments exposed to earthquake hazard

• Collaborating with project partners at EPFL, the University of Zagreb, and other international institutions

• Disseminating research findings through scientific publications and conference presentations

• Have full responsibility for your own dissertation

• Participating in education and co-supervise student projects

Profile

• A MSc degree (or equivalent) in Civil Engineering with a focus on Structural Engineering

• Experience or strong interest in experimental and/or numerical methods in structural engineering

• Interest in traditional construction techniques and interdisciplinary collaboration (engineering, heritage, architecture)

• Self-motivated, independent, and collaborative mindset with a high level of rigor for academic research work

• Excellent communication skills in English (written and spoken) and willingness to work as part of a team

• Familiarity with Python, MATLAB or similar for data analysis

• Familiarity with numerical modeling tools (e.g. OpenSees, Abaqus, DIANA) is an asset

We offer

• A stimulating and international working environment

• Competitive salary and excellent working conditions, 1-year fixed-term contract (CDD), renewable for 3 years (4 years in total) to complete your PhD; more information can be found on our website

• You will be part of the EDCE doctoral program

• Opportunity to perform state-of-the-art research in one of the most dynamic scientific institutions in Europe

• Opportunity to interact with internationally renowned experts, and with a strong team of postdoctoral researchers and PhD students

• Opportunity to conduct meaningful research bridging engineering, cultural heritage, and development

Informations

The selection process involves multiple stages, and short-listed candidates will be requested to apply to a specific EPFL Doctoral Program to qualify for a PhD at EPFL, i.e. Doctoral School of Civil and Environmental Engineering (EDCE) .
Please check this page for additional information on admission.

Please note that this is a separate application process necessary to be eligible to complete your PhD at EPFL.

Missione Offriamo due posizioni stimolanti come dottorando a tempo pieno (100%) presso l'ENAC presso l'EPFL, Losanna, Svizzera. Il nostro Laboratorio EESD è focalizzato sullo studio del comportamento sismico degli edifici in cemento armato e muratura non armata. I nostri approcci includono modellazione numerica e meccanica, test su larga scala e metodi basati sui dati. I dottorandi contribuiranno a migliorare la comprensione del comportamento sismico degli aggregati edilizi storici in muratura attraverso una combinazione di prove sperimentali su larga scala, indagini sul campo e simulazioni numeriche. La ricerca si concentrerà sul comportamento e sull’interazione degli edifici all’interno degli aggregati di muratura, supportando lo sviluppo di approcci di valutazione innovativi e soluzioni di retrofit resilienti per ambienti urbani storici esposti al rischio sismico. Lavorerai al progetto ZAGGREGATE, un'iniziativa di ricerca collaborativa tra EPFL, Università di Zagabria e altri partner accademici e professionali. Il progetto mira a migliorare la comprensione, la valutazione e la riabilitazione degli aggregati edilizi in muratura storica nelle regioni sismiche. I candidati prescelti entreranno a far parte di un team di ricercatori che lavorano all'interfaccia tra ingegneria strutturale, ingegneria sismica e conservazione del patrimonio e avranno opportunità di collaborazione e visite di ricerca in Croazia. • Condurre ricerche di dottorato originali utilizzando metodi sperimentali, numerici e analitici per studiare la risposta sismica degli edifici in muratura come edifici autonomi e all'interno di aggregati
• Contribuire allo sviluppo di metodologie di valutazione innovative e strategie di retrofit resilienti per ambienti urbani storici esposti al rischio di terremoto
• Collaborare con i partner di progetto presso l'EPFL, l'Università di Zagabria e altre istituzioni internazionali

• Interesse per le tecniche di costruzione tradizionali e la collaborazione interdisciplinare (ingegneria, patrimonio, architettura)
• Mentalità automotivata, indipendente e collaborativa con un alto livello di rigore per il lavoro di ricerca accademica

Mission Wir bieten zwei herausfordernde Stellen als Vollzeit-Doktorand (100 %) am ENAC der EPFL, Lausanne, Schweiz, an. Unser Labor EESD konzentriert sich auf die Untersuchung des seismischen Verhaltens von Gebäuden aus Stahlbeton und unbewehrtem Mauerwerk. Unsere Ansätze umfassen numerische und mechanische Modellierung, groß angelegte Tests sowie datengesteuerte Methoden. Die Doktoranden werden durch eine Kombination aus groß angelegten experimentellen Tests, Felduntersuchungen und numerischen Simulationen dazu beitragen, das Verständnis des seismischen Verhaltens historischer Gebäudeaggregate aus Ziegelmauerwerk zu verbessern. Die Forschung wird sich auf das Verhalten und die Interaktion von Gebäuden innerhalb von Mauerwerksaggregaten konzentrieren und die Entwicklung innovativer Bewertungsansätze und widerstandsfähiger Sanierungslösungen für historische städtische Umgebungen unterstützen, die einem Erdbebenrisiko ausgesetzt sind. Sie werden am ZAGGREGATE-Projekt arbeiten, einer gemeinsamen Forschungsinitiative zwischen der EPFL, der Universität Zagreb und anderen akademischen und professionellen Partnern. Das Projekt zielt darauf ab, das Verständnis, die Bewertung und die Sanierung historischer Mauerwerksaggregate in seismischen Regionen zu verbessern. Die erfolgreichen Kandidaten werden Teil eines Forscherteams, das an der Schnittstelle von Bauingenieurwesen, Erdbebeningenieurwesen und Denkmalschutz arbeitet, und haben die Möglichkeit zur Zusammenarbeit und zu Forschungsaufenthalten in Kroatien. Hauptaufgaben und Verantwortlichkeiten Als Doktorand wird von Ihnen Folgendes erwartet:
• Durchführung origineller Doktorarbeiten mit experimentellen, numerischen und analytischen Methoden zur Untersuchung der seismischen Reaktion von Mauerwerksgebäuden als eigenständige Gebäude und innerhalb von Aggregaten
• Beitrag zur Entwicklung innovativer Bewertungsmethoden und widerstandsfähiger Sanierungsstrategien für historische städtische Umgebungen, die der Gefahr von Erdbeben ausgesetzt sind
• Zusammenarbeit mit Projektpartnern an der EPFL, der Universität Zagreb und anderen internationalen Institutionen
• Verbreitung von Forschungsergebnissen durch wissenschaftliche Veröffentlichungen und Konferenzpräsentationen

• Ein MSc-Abschluss (oder ein gleichwertiger Abschluss) in Bauingenieurwesen mit Schwerpunkt auf Bauingenieurwesen
• Erfahrung oder starkes Interesse an experimentellen und/oder numerischen Methoden im Bauingenieurwesen
• Interesse an traditionellen Bautechniken und interdisziplinärer Zusammenarbeit (Ingenieurwesen, Kulturerbe, Architektur)
• Selbstmotivierte, unabhängige und kollaborative Denkweise mit einem hohen Maß an Genauigkeit für akademische Forschungsarbeiten
• Ausgezeichnete Kommunikationsfähigkeiten in Englisch (schriftlich und mündlich) und Bereitschaft zur Teamarbeit

Mission Nous proposons deux postes stimulants en tant que doctorant à temps plein (100 %) à l'ENAC de l'EPFL, Lausanne, Suisse. Notre laboratoire EESD se concentre sur l'étude du comportement sismique des bâtiments en béton armé et en maçonnerie non armée. Nos approches incluent la modélisation numérique et mécanique, les tests à grande échelle ainsi que les méthodes basées sur les données. Les doctorants contribueront à faire progresser la compréhension du comportement sismique des agrégats de bâtiments historiques en maçonnerie de briques grâce à une combinaison d'essais expérimentaux à grande échelle, d'enquêtes sur le terrain et de simulations numériques. La recherche se concentrera sur le comportement et l'interaction des bâtiments au sein des agrégats de maçonnerie, soutenant le développement d'approches d'évaluation innovantes et de solutions de rénovation résilientes pour les environnements urbains historiques exposés au risque sismique. Vous travaillerez sur le projet ZAGGREGATE, une initiative de recherche collaborative entre l'EPFL, l'Université de Zagreb et d'autres partenaires académiques et professionnels. Le projet vise à améliorer la compréhension, l'évaluation et la réhabilitation des agrégats de bâtiments historiques en maçonnerie dans les régions sismiques. Les candidats retenus rejoindront une équipe de chercheurs travaillant à l'interface de l'ingénierie structurelle, de l'ingénierie parasismique et de la conservation du patrimoine, et auront des opportunités de collaboration et de visites de recherche en Croatie. • Mener des recherches doctorales originales en utilisant des méthodes expérimentales, numériques et analytiques pour étudier la réponse sismique des bâtiments en maçonnerie en tant que bâtiments autonomes et au sein d'agrégats.

Mission

Le CMi est une plateforme technologique dotée d’un important parc d’équipements de micro- et de nano- fabrication. Une équipe pluridisciplinaire de 25 personnes est en charge d’en assurer le fonctionnement et l’évolution. La plateforme accueille annuellement plus de 650 utilisateurs, principalement des doctorants de l’EPFL, et aussi des postdocs, des étudiants, des chercheurs internes et externes, ainsi que des industriels, qui réalisent tous eux-mêmes leurs procédés. Les challenges sont multiples, que ceci soit pour offrir des procédés du plus haut niveau, satisfaisant aux besoins de la recherche, pour assurer les formations, pour offrir une expertise et des conseils très larges, ou pour garantir la sécurité. Rapportant au responsable de l’équipe des ingénieurs des procédés, vous collaborez étroitement avec l’ensemble de l’équipe existante et pluridisciplinaire des ingénieurs et des techniciens. Nous cherchons une personne avec des connaissances de base solides, prête à s’investir et à progresser rapidement pour réaliser des interventions techniques et scientifiques exigeantes.

Principales tâches et responsabilités

• Former les utilisateurs sur les équipements.

• Conseiller les utilisateurs sur les meilleurs choix technologiques.

• Acquérir, installer, qualifier et exploiter des équipements dont la valeur dépasse le million de francs

• Travailler avec des prestataires externes.

• Documenter les équipements et les procédés.

Profil

Profil recherché :

• Master of sciences, ou titre jugé équivalent.

• Idéalement avec de l’expérience :

• dans les domaines CVD, PVD ou galvanoplastie.

• en métrologie des couches minces.

Compétences personnelles et sociales :

• Excellentes aptitudes à communiquer.

• Sens aigu du service.

• Esprit d'initiative.

• Rigueur et autonomie dans le travail.

• Capacité à travailler en équipe, ouvert d’esprit et engagé.

• Grand sens pratique.

• Résistance au stress.

Compétences Linguistiques :

• Très bonnes connaissances en français (lu, écrit, parlé), niveau équivalent C1.

• Bonnes connaissances en anglais (lu, écrit, parlé), niveau équivalent B2.

Nous offrons

• La possibilité d’intégrer une équipe dynamique et stimulante.

• Un environnement de travail multiculturel et académique de qualité.

• Des possibilités de formation continue.

• Un travail sur des équipements industriels dans une salle blanche évolutive de clase ISO5.

Informations

Date d'entrée en fonction : de suite ou à convenir

Taux d'occupation 100%

Type de contrat : CDD

jobs.description:
Mission

We are seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral fellow with a strong background in cancer biology, genetics, and epigenetics. The ideal candidate will have a proven track record of scientific excellence, demonstrated through high-quality publications.

The position is available in the Laboratory of Elisa Oricchio at the Swiss Institute of Experimental Cancer Research ISREC at EPFL. The lab is part of the vibrant research community of the Swiss Cancer Center Leman and is located on the EPFL main campus.

Main duties and responsibilities

In the Oricchio lab, we investigate the molecular mechanisms that drive tumor initiation and determine responses to therapy. A comprehensive understanding of tumor evolution requires integrating both genetic and non-genetic mechanisms. Thus, our research begins with the functional characterization of cancer-associated genomic alterations to determine how they reshape the structure and function of the epigenome. Over the past years, we have shown that remodeling the chromatin 3D structure is a key driver of tumor development and progression and demonstrated how specific genomic alterations reprogram the crosstalk between cancer cells and immune cells.

We offer

The position provides an exciting opportunity to further develop and expand these lines of research, and candidates are also encouraged to apply for individual fellowships to strengthen their CVs and future career prospects. A strong motivation and exceptional level of dedication and work ethic are essential. Prior experience with animal models, 3D culture systems and/or computational analyses will be an advantage. The salary will be according to EPFL standards.

Informations

Formal applications should be submitted as a single PDF file containing

(1) A cover letter outlining your research interests, relevant experience, and motivation for joining the lab and suggesting a possible project that the applicant would like to develop.

(2) A detailed CV including a full list of publications;

(3) Names and contact information of at least two referees who can provide recommendation letters.

Contract Start Date : 01/01/2027

Activity Rate : 100.00

Contract Type: CDD

Duration: One year, renewable

Reference: 2405

Missione

Stiamo vedendo una relazione postdoctoral altamente motivata con un forte background in biologia del cancro, genetica e epigenetica. Il candidato ideale avrà un comprovato record di eccellenza scientifica, dimostrato attraverso pubblicazioni di alta qualità.

La posizione è disponibile presso il Laboratorio di Elisa Oricchio presso l'Istituto svizzero di ricerca sperimentale del cancro ISREC presso EPFL. Il laboratorio fa parte della vivace comunità di ricerca dello Swiss Cancer Center Leman e si trova nel campus principale dell'EPFL.

Principali doveri e responsabilità

Nel laboratorio di Oricchio, studiamo i meccanismi molecolari che guidano l'iniziazione del tumore e determinano le risposte alla terapia. Una comprensione completa dei requisiti di evoluzione del tumore che integrano entrambi i meccanismi genetici e non genetici. Così, le nostre idee di ricerca con la caratterizzazione funzionale di alterazioni genetiche associate al cancro per determinare come modellano la struttura e la funzione dell'epigeno. Negli ultimi anni, abbiamo dimostrato che la ristrutturazione della struttura 3D della cromatina è un driver chiave dello sviluppo e della progressione del tumore e ha dimostrato come specifiche alterazioni genetiche riprogrammano il crosstalk tra cellule tumorali e cellule immunitarie.

Offriamo

La posizione offre un'opportunità entusiasmante per sviluppare e ampliare ulteriormente queste linee di ricerca, e i candidati sono anche incoraggiati a chiedere alle singole borse di studio per rafforzare i loro CV e le prospettive di carriera future. Una forte motivazione e un eccezionale livello di dedizione ed etica del lavoro sono essenziali. L'esperienza prioritaria con modelli animali, sistemi di cultura 3D e/o analisi computazionali sarà un vantaggio. Il sale sarà accordato agli standard EPFL.

Informazioni

Le domande formali devono essere presentate come un unico file PDF contenente

(1) Una lettera di copertura che delinea i vostri interessi di ricerca, l'esperienza di report e la motivazione per unire il laboratorio e suggerendo un progetto possibile che la domanda vorrebbe sviluppare.

(2) Un curriculum dettagliato che include un elenco completo delle pubblicazioni;

(3) Nomi e informazioni di contatto di almeno due arbitri che possono fornire lettere di raccomandazione.

Data di inizio del contratto: 01/01/2027

Tasso di attività: 100.00

Tipo di contratto: CDD

Durata: un anno, rinnovabile

descriptionByLocale.de:
Mission

Wir sehen ein hoch motiviertes Postdoc-Stipendium mit einem starken Hintergrund in Krebsbiologie, Genetik und Epigenetik. Der ideale Kandidat wird eine nachgewiesene Erfolgsbilanz wissenschaftlicher Exzellenz haben, die durch qualitativ hochwertige Publikationen demonstriert wird.

Die Stelle ist im Labor von Elisa Oricchio am Schweizerischen Institut für experimentelle Krebsforschung ISREC an der EPFL verfügbar. Das Labor ist Teil der lebendigen Forschungsgemeinschaft des Swiss Cancer Center Leman und befindet sich auf dem EPFL-Hauptcampus.

Hauptaufgaben und Zuständigkeiten

Im Oricchio-Labor untersuchen wir die molekularen Mechanismen, die die Tumorinitiation vorantreiben und die Reaktionen auf die Therapie bestimmen. Ein umfassendes Verständnis der Tumorentwicklungsanforderungen, das sowohl genetische als auch nicht-genetische Mechanismen integriert. Daher sind unsere Forschungsideen mit der funktionellen Charakterisierung von Krebs-assoziierten genetischen Veränderungen, um zu bestimmen, wie sie die Struktur und Funktion des Epigenoms formen. In den letzten Jahren haben wir gezeigt, dass die Umgestaltung der Chromatin-3D-Struktur ein wichtiger Treiber für die Tumorentwicklung und -progression ist, und gezeigt, wie spezifische genetische Veränderungen den Crosstalk zwischen Krebszellen und Immunzellen umprogrammieren.

Wir bieten

Die Position bietet eine spannende Gelegenheit, diese Forschungslinien weiterzuentwickeln und auszubauen, und die Kandidaten werden auch ermutigt, sich für individuelle Stipendien zu bewerben, um ihre Lebensläufe und zukünftigen Karriereaussichten zu stärken. Eine starke Motivation und ein außergewöhnliches Maß an Engagement und Arbeitsmoral sind unerlässlich. Vorrangige Erfahrungen mit Tiermodellen, 3D-Kultursystemen und/oder Computeranalysen sind von Vorteil. Das Salz wird auf EPFL-Standards abgestimmt.

Information

Formale Anträge sollten als eine einzige PDF-Datei mit

(1) Ein Anschreiben, das Ihre Forschungsinteressen, Berichtserfahrung und Motivation für den Beitritt zum Labor umreißt und ein mögliches Projekt vorschlägt, das die Anwendung entwickeln möchte.

jobs.description:
Mission

Le laboratoire Thomä de l’EPFL recherche un·e technicien·ne de laboratoire motivé·e pour soutenir divers projets de recherche dans le domaine de la découverte de médicaments. Vous travaillerez au sein d’une équipe de chercheur·euse·s postdoctoraux développant des composés de types « colles moléculaires ». Ce travail comprend le développement et l’optimisation de criblages in vitro et in vivo à haut débit, ainsi que les premières étapes de la découverte de médicaments, notamment l’optimisation des molécules actives initiales en candidats principaux (« hit-to-lead »). Si vous souhaitez rejoindre une équipe travaillant sur des projets scientifiques intéressants et susceptibles de déboucher sur des applications concrètes, nous vous invitons à soumettre votre candidature.

Principales tâches et responsabilités

Au sein de notre équipe de recherche, vous apporterez un soutien expérimental à différents projets. Vos responsabilités comprendront notamment :

• Réaliser des expériences de biologie moléculaire, notamment le clonage d’ADN, la préparation de plasmides et la validation de constructions

• Participer aux travaux de culture de cellules de mammifères et d’insectes, y compris l’entretien courant des cultures et les transfections

• Contribuer au développement et à la mise en œuvre de tests de criblage cellulaires ou moléculaires

• Préparer les échantillons et les réactifs, et tenir des dossiers expérimentaux précis

• Analyser les résultats expérimentaux et identifier d’éventuels problèmes techniques

• Participer à la gestion des stocks communs du laboratoire, à l’entretien des équipements et au maintien d’un environnement de travail propre et bien organisé

• Coordonner les expériences et les priorités avec plusieurs chercheur·euse·s

• Contribuer positivement à la vie scientifique et sociale du laboratoire

Profil

Vous êtes un·e professionnel·le de laboratoire motivé·e, fiable et curieux·se, qui apprécie l’apprentissage de nouvelles techniques et le travail au sein d’une équipe de recherche collaborative. Vous réalisez les expériences avec soin, adoptez une approche critique dans votre travail et êtes capable de travailler de manière autonome une fois formé·e.

Vous devez disposer des qualifications suivantes :

• Une formation en biologie, biotechnologie, biochimie, biologie moléculaire ou dans une discipline apparentée

• Une expérience pratique préalable en laboratoire

• Une bonne compréhension des bonnes pratiques de laboratoire, notamment en matière de rigueur et de stérilité

• La capacité à suivre des protocoles établis de manière précise et reproductible

• La capacité à organiser votre travail, à gérer plusieurs tâches et à documenter clairement les expériences

• Une approche réfléchie et systématique du travail expérimental, en particulier lors de la réalisation de criblages

• De bonnes compétences en communication et une attitude collégiale, orientée vers le travail en équipe

• La volonté d’apprendre de nouvelles méthodes et de vous adapter aux besoins de différents projets
Une bonne maîtrise de l’anglais

Une expérience dans un ou plusieurs des domaines suivants constituerait un atout :

• Clonage Gateway, Gibson ou fondé sur l’utilisation d’enzymes de restriction

• Techniques de culture de cellules de mammifères et d’insectes

• Techniques de microbiologie

• Techniques de criblage cellulaire ou moléculaire

• Cytométrie en flux ou tri cellulaire activé par fluorescence (FACS)

Il n’est pas attendu des candidat·e·s qu’ils ou elles maîtrisent l’ensemble des techniques mentionnées ci-dessus. Une formation sera assurée. La motivation, la fiabilité, la curiosité scientifique et la capacité à devenir un membre pleinement engagé du laboratoire sont des qualités essentielles pour ce poste.
