jobs.description:
Mission

L'École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL) est une institution de premier plan offrant un environnement de recherche et d'enseignement dynamique et multiculturel. Au sein de l’Institut de Physique (IPHYS, Faculté des Sciences de Base), nous développons des systèmes électroniques de pointe pour soutenir des projets de recherche ambitieux pour les laboratoires de l’IPHYS allant de l'instrumentation scientifique au sein des laboratoires, jusqu’à la réalisation ou la participation à des instruments pour des infrastructures de Recherche Internationales.

Principales tâches et responsabilités

En tant qu'Ingénieur Electronicien Team Lead, vous aurez la charge de piloter les activités de conception matérielle et de coordonner l'équipe technique du service électronique de l’IPHYS. Vos missions principales s'articulent autour des axes suivants :

• Prototypage de Cartes Électroniques, Firmware et Software : Réaliser des prototypes de cartes électroniques, incluant non seulement la conception hardware, mais également le développement du firmware (microcontrôleurs) et du software associé (pilotes, interfaces de contrôle et d'acquisition de données). Suivre et tester les cartes de productions.

• Management et Leadership : Encadrer, motiver et superviser une équipe d'ingénieurs et de techniciens en électronique. Planifier la charge de travail et accompagner le développement des compétences des collaborateurs.

• Gestion de Projets et Conception : Piloter des projets de conception de systèmes électroniques complexes (analogiques, numériques et mixtes), de la phase de spécification jusqu'au prototypage, au test et au déploiement.

• Support à la Recherche : Collaborer étroitement avec les chercheurs, les doctorants et les professeurs pour traduire leurs besoins expérimentaux en solutions électroniques robustes et innovantes.

• Gestion des Infrastructures et des Opérations : Assurer la maintenance et la mise à niveau des équipements, gérer les relations avec les fournisseurs et veiller au respect des normes de sécurité (HSE).

Profil

• Master (MSc) en génie électrique, microtechnique ou domaine équivalent.
• Minimum 8 ans d'expérience professionnelle dans la conception électronique, avec une expérience dans le pilotage de projets techniques et la gestion d'équipe.
• Maîtrise des outils de conception de circuits (ex. Altium Designer, Cadence), compétences approfondies en FPGA, microcontrôleurs, ainsi qu'en développement de firmware et de logiciels embarqués. Expériences dans l’utilisation d’outils d’intelligence artificielle (IA).
• Leadership naturel, excellentes capacités de communication, esprit d'analyse et sens aigu des responsabilités.
• Maîtrise courante du français et de l'anglais

Nous offrons

À l'EPFL, nous avons la conviction que chacun et chacune peut accomplir de grandes choses lorsqu'il ou elle évolue dans un environnement bienveillant, respectueux et propice à la réussite. En rejoignant notre institution, vous contribuerez à façonner l'avenir de la société grâce à l'éducation, la recherche et l'innovation.

Nous offrons un environnement de travail inspirant, international et collaboratif, où votre contribution a un impact concret et où vos idées sont valorisées. Grâce à un cadre de travail flexible et à des conditions d’emploi attractives, nous nous engageons à créer un environnement dans lequel chacun et chacune peut s’épanouir, développer son potentiel et faire la différence.

Au-delà de votre activité professionnelle, nos campus accueillent une communauté dynamique dans un cadre unique, porté par de nombreuses initiatives en faveur de l’égalité, de l’inclusion, de la diversité, du bien-être et de la durabilité. Tout au long de l’année, un programme varié d’activités culturelles, sportives et communautaires vient également renforcer la vie du campus.

Découvrez nos conditions d’emploi et les avantages offerts à nos collaboratrices et collaborateurs.

Within the Institute of Physics (IPHYS, Faculty of Basic Sciences), we develop advanced electronic systems to support ambitious research projects for IPHYS laboratories ranging from scientific instrumentation within laboratories, to the realization or participation in instruments for international research infrastructures.

At EPFL, we are convinced that everyone can accomplish great things when he or she evolves in a caring, respectful and successful environment. By joining our institution, you will help shape the future of society through education, research and innovation.

jobs.description:
EPFL, the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne, is one of the most dynamic university campuses in Europe and ranks among the top 20 universities worldwide. The EPFL employs more than 6,500 people supporting the three main missions of the institutions: education, research and innovation. The EPFL campus offers an exceptional working environment at the heart of a community of more than 18,500 people, including over 14,000 students and 4,000 researchers from more than 120 different countries.

As part of the Vertical Africa. Visualizing Urban Change, Negotiating Power, Designing Sustainable Cities (VERTICAF) project, funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation we are looking for a full time (100%) PhD student at EPFL Lausanne.

Vertical Africa : Visualizing Urban Change, Negotiating Power, Designing Sustainable Cities (VERTICAF) is funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) and co-led by Professors Didier Péclard (UNIGE), Armelle Choplin (UNIGE), and Jérôme Chenal (EPFL), in partnership with the Universities of Dakar, Kigali, and Luanda.

The Vertical Africa project (VERTICAF) aims to analyze the dynamics of verticalization in African cities and their implications for Africa’s urban future. It combines spatial analysis, political science, architecture, and urban studies to examine how vertical growth transforms cities environmentally, socially, and politically.

The project will be conducted in three cities—Dakar (Senegal), Kigali (Rwanda), and Luanda (Angola)—using a comparative approach focused on key urban areas, including historic centers, peri-urban areas, and satellite settlements.

VERTICAF’s scientific contribution is threefold: (1) to develop methods for measuring verticality and its impacts in data-scarce contexts, in Africa and elsewhere; (2) to document, both theoretically and empirically, the interactions between vertical growth, capitalism, governance, inequality, and everyday life; and (3) to co-design more sustainable and inclusive models for the future of African cities, which will represent a major challenge for global governance by 2100.

Information

Contract duration: 48 months

Location: Switzerland (EPFL), with fieldwork assignments

Start date: 02/2027

Thesis Topic

How can urban verticalization be measured, mapped, and quantified in African contexts with limited data, at the city, neighborhood, and building scales?

Tasks and responsibilities

• Build a harmonized database of urban verticality for the three cities (Dakar, Kigali, Luanda) since 2000;

• Develop a data processing pipeline to extract building heights at different points in time;

• Conduct targeted photogrammetric analyses and integrate geolocated crowdsourced images (Flickr, SenseCity) to supplement satellite data at the meso level;

• Compile “building profiles” (quantitative approach): measuring height, density, footprint, and temporal evolution for approximately 10 buildings per city.

Required Profile

Education

• Master’s degree (or equivalent) in geomatics, geography, data science, environmental engineering, quantitative urban planning, or a related field;

• Strong interest in African cities and sustainable urban development issues.

Technical Skills

• Proficiency in remote sensing (satellite image processing, GIS, photogrammetry);

• Programming skills for geospatial analysis: Python (rasterio, geopandas, scikit-learn) or R; experience with Google Earth Engine is a plus;

• Experience with open-source tools (QGIS, GRASS GIS, GDAL) and spatial databases.

Soft Skills

• Scientific rigor and autonomy in conducting research;

• Ability to work in an interdisciplinary and multicultural context;

• Excellent writing skills in English (the project’s primary publication language). Knowledge of French required. Knowledge of Portuguese, Wolof, or Kinyarwanda is an asset;

• Sensitivity to gender equity issues and North-South research dynamics.

descriptionByLocale.it:
EPFL, l'Istituto federale di tecnologia svizzero di Losanna, è uno dei campus universitari più dinamici d'Europa e si colloca tra le prime 20 università di tutto il mondo. L'EPFL impiega oltre 6.500 persone che sostengono le tre principali missioni delle istituzioni: istruzione, ricerca e innovazione. Il campus EPFL offre un ambiente di lavoro eccezionale al centro di una comunità di oltre 18.500 persone, tra cui oltre 14.000 studenti e 4.000 ricercatori provenienti da oltre 120 paesi diversi.

Come parte dell'Africa Verticale. Visualizzazione del progetto Urban Change, Negotiating Power, Designing Sustainable Cities (VERTICAF), finanziato dalla Swiss National Science Foundation stiamo cercando uno studente di dottorato a tempo pieno (100%) all'EPFL di Losanna.

L'Africa Verticale: Visualizing Urban Change, Negotiating Power, Designing Sustainable Cities (VERTICAF) è finanziata dalla Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) e co-diretto dai professori Didier Péclard (UNIGE), Armelle Choplin (UNIGE), e Jérôme Chenal (EPFL), in collaborazione con le Università di Dakar, Kigali e Luanda.

Il progetto Vertical Africa (VERTICAF) mira ad analizzare le dinamiche di verticalizzazione nelle città africane e le loro implicazioni per il futuro urbano dell’Africa. Combina l'analisi spaziale, la scienza politica, l'architettura e gli studi urbani per esaminare come la crescita verticale trasforma le città in ambiente, socialmente e politicamente.

Il progetto sarà condotto in tre città – Dakar (Senegal), Kigali (Rwanda), e Luanda (Angola) – utilizzando un approccio comparativo focalizzato su aree urbane chiave, tra cui centri storici, aree peri-urbane e insediamenti satellitari.

Il contributo scientifico di VERTICAF è triplice: (1) sviluppare metodi per misurare la verticalità e i suoi impatti nei contesti di data-scarce, in Africa e altrove; (2) documentare, sia teoricamente che empiricamente, le interazioni tra crescita verticale, capitalismo, governance, disuguaglianza e vita quotidiana; e (3) per co-progettare modelli più sostenibili e inclusivi per il futuro delle città africane, che rappresenteranno una grande sfida per la governance globale di 2100.

Informazioni

Durata del contratto: 48 mesi

Ubicazione: Svizzera (EPFL), con incarichi di lavoro sul campo

Data di inizio: 02/2027

Argomento della tesi

Come si può misurare, mappare e quantificare la verticalizzazione urbana in contesti africani con dati limitati, in città, quartiere e scale di costruzione?

Compiti e responsabilità

• Costruire un database armonizzato di verticalità urbana per le tre città (Dakar, Kigali, Luanda) dal 2000;

• Sviluppare un data processing pipeline per estrarre altezze di costruzione in diversi punti nel tempo;

• Condurre analisi fotogrammetriche mirate e integrare immagini geolocate crowdsourced (Flickr, SenseCity) per integrare i dati satellitari a livello di meso;

• Compile “profili di costruzione” (approccio quantitativo): altezza di misura, densità, impronta e evoluzione temporale per circa 10 edifici per città.

Istruzione

• Laurea magistrale (o equivalente) in geomatica, geografia, scienza dei dati, ingegneria ambientale, pianificazione urbana quantitativa, o un campo correlato;

• Forte interesse per le città africane e le questioni di sviluppo urbano sostenibile.

• Proficienza nel telerilevamento (elaborazione di immagini satellitari, GIS, fotogrammetria);

EPFL, the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne, is one of the most dynamic university campuses in Europe and ranks among the top 20 universities worldwide. The EPFL employs more than 6,500 people supporting the three main missions of the institutions: education, research and innovation. The EPFL campus offers an exceptional working environment at the heart of a community of more than 18,500 people, including over 14,000 students and 4,000 researchers from more than 120 different countries.

As part of the Vertical Africa. Visualizing Urban Change, Negotiating Power, Designing Sustainable Cities (VERTICAF) project, funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation we are looking for a full time (100%) PhD student at EPFL Lausanne.

Vertical Africa : Visualizing Urban Change, Negotiating Power, Designing Sustainable Cities (VERTICAF) is funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) and co-led by Professors Didier Péclard (UNIGE), Armelle Choplin (UNIGE), and Jérôme Chenal (EPFL), in partnership with the Universities of Dakar, Kigali, and Luanda.

The Vertical Africa project (VERTICAF) aims to analyze the dynamics of verticalization in African cities and their implications for Africa’s urban future. It combines spatial analysis, political science, architecture, and urban studies to examine how vertical growth transforms cities environmentally, socially, and politically.

The project will be conducted in three cities—Dakar (Senegal), Kigali (Rwanda), and Luanda (Angola)—using a comparative approach focused on key urban areas, including historic centers, peri-urban areas, and satellite settlements.

VERTICAF’s scientific contribution is threefold: (1) to develop methods for measuring verticality and its impacts in data-scarce contexts, in Africa and elsewhere; (2) to document, both theoretically and empirically, the interactions between vertical growth, capitalism, governance, inequality, and everyday life; and (3) to co-design more sustainable and inclusive models for the future of African cities, which will represent a major challenge for global governance by 2100.

Information

Contract duration: 48 months

Location: Switzerland (EPFL), with fieldwork assignments

Start date: 02/2027

Thesis Topic

How can urban verticalization be measured, mapped, and quantified in African contexts with limited data, at the city, neighborhood, and building scales?

Tasks and responsibilities

• Build a harmonized database of urban verticality for the three cities (Dakar, Kigali, Luanda) since 2000;

• Develop a data processing pipeline to extract building heights at different points in time;

• Conduct targeted photogrammetric analyses and integrate geolocated crowdsourced images (Flickr, SenseCity) to supplement satellite data at the meso level;

• Compile “building profiles” (quantitative approach): measuring height, density, footprint, and temporal evolution for approximately 10 buildings per city.

Required Profile

Education

• Master’s degree (or equivalent) in geomatics, geography, data science, environmental engineering, quantitative urban planning, or a related field;

• Strong interest in African cities and sustainable urban development issues.

Technical Skills

• Proficiency in remote sensing (satellite image processing, GIS, photogrammetry);

• Programming skills for geospatial analysis: Python (rasterio, geopandas, scikit-learn) or R; experience with Google Earth Engine is a plus;

• Experience with open-source tools (QGIS, GRASS GIS, GDAL) and spatial databases.

Soft Skills

• Scientific rigor and autonomy in conducting research;

• Ability to work in an interdisciplinary and multicultural context;

• Excellent writing skills in English (the project’s primary publication language). Knowledge of French required. Knowledge of Portuguese, Wolof, or Kinyarwanda is an asset;

• Sensitivity to gender equity issues and North-South research dynamics.

Vertical Africa: Visualizing Urban Change, Negotiating Power, Designing Sustainable Cities (VERTICAF) wird vom Schweizerischen Nationalfonds (SNF) finanziert und gemeinsam von den Professoren Didier Péclard (UNIGE), Armelle Choplin (UNIGE) und Jérôme Chenal (EPFL) in Partnerschaft mit den Universitäten Dakar, Kigali und Luanda geleitet.

Das Projekt Vertical Africa (VERTICAF) zielt darauf ab, die Dynamik der Vertikalisierung in afrikanischen Städten und ihre Auswirkungen auf die urbane Zukunft Afrikas zu analysieren. Es kombiniert Raumanalyse, Politikwissenschaft, Architektur und Stadtstudien, um zu untersuchen, wie vertikales Wachstum Städte ökologisch, sozial und politisch verändert.

Das Projekt wird in drei Städten – Dakar (Senegal), Kigali (Ruanda) und Luanda (Angola) – mit einem vergleichenden Ansatz durchgeführt, der sich auf wichtige städtische Gebiete konzentriert, darunter historische Zentren, Stadtrandgebiete und Satellitensiedlungen.

Der wissenschaftliche Beitrag von VERTICAF ist dreifach: (1) Methoden zur Messung der Vertikalität und ihrer Auswirkungen in datenarmen Kontexten in Afrika und anderswo zu entwickeln; (2) sowohl theoretisch als auch empirisch die Wechselwirkungen zwischen vertikalem Wachstum, Kapitalismus, Governance, Ungleichheit und Alltag zu dokumentieren; und (3) nachhaltigere und integrativere Modelle für die Zukunft afrikanischer Städte mitzugestalten, die bis 2100 eine große Herausforderung für die globale Governance darstellen werden.

• Durchführung gezielter photogrammetrischer Analysen und Integration geolokalisierter Crowdsourcing-Bilder (Flickr, SenseCity), um Satellitendaten auf Meso-Ebene zu ergänzen;

• Programmierkenntnisse für die Geodatenanalyse: Python (Rasterio, Geopandas, scikit-learn) oder R; Erfahrung mit Google Earth Engine ist ein Plus;

L'EPFL, l'Institut fédéral de technologie de Lausanne, est l'un des campus universitaires les plus dynamiques d'Europe et figure parmi les 20 meilleures universités au monde. L'EPFL emploie plus de 6 500 personnes qui soutiennent les trois missions principales des institutions : l'éducation, la recherche et l'innovation. Le campus de l'EPFL offre un environnement de travail exceptionnel au cœur d'une communauté de plus de 18 500 personnes, dont plus de 14 000 étudiants et 4 000 chercheurs de plus de 120 pays différents.

Dans le cadre de l'Afrique Verticale. Visualizing Urban Change, Négociing Power, Designing Sustainable Cities (VERTICAF), financé par la Fondation nationale suisse des sciences, nous recherchons un doctorant à plein temps (100 %) à l'EPFL Lausanne.

Afrique Verticale : Visualiser le changement urbain, le pouvoir de négociation, concevoir des villes durables (VERTICAF) est financé par la Fondation nationale suisse des sciences (SNSF) et codirigé par les professeurs Didier Péclard (UNIGE), Armelle Choplin (UNIGE) et Jérôme Chenal (EPFL), en partenariat avec les universités de Dakar, Kigali et Luanda.

Le projet Vertical Africa (VERTICAF) vise à analyser la dynamique de la verticalisation dans les villes africaines et leurs implications pour l'avenir urbain de l'Afrique. Il combine l'analyse spatiale, la science politique, l'architecture et les études urbaines pour examiner comment la croissance verticale transforme les villes en termes écologiques, sociaux et politiques.

Le projet sera mené dans trois villes — Dakar (Sénégal), Kigali (Rwanda) et Luanda (Angola) — en utilisant une approche comparative axée sur les principales zones urbaines, y compris les centres historiques, les zones périurbaines et les établissements satellites.

La contribution scientifique du VERTICAF est triple : 1) développer des méthodes de mesure de la verticalité et de ses impacts dans les contextes de données, en Afrique et ailleurs ; 2) documenter, théoriquement et empiriquement, les interactions entre croissance verticale, capitalisme, gouvernance, inégalités et vie quotidienne ; et 3) co-concevoir des modèles plus durables et inclusifs pour l'avenir des villes africaines, qui représenteront un défi majeur pour la gouvernance mondiale d'ici 2100.

• Créer une base de données harmonisée sur la verticalité urbaine pour les trois villes (Dakar, Kigali, Luanda) depuis 2000;

jobs.description:
Profile

The Structural Xploration Lab is seeking a new research collaborator with a PhD in building technology, preferably in the field of building materials and/or building envelope performance and/or building renovation. The candidate must be familiar with contemporary construction techniques and have an interest in 20th-century construction techniques or vernacular architecture. Experience in Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), Building Information Modelling (BIM), Geographic Information Systems (GIS) or computer programming is a plus. A master's degree or professional experience in architecture is preferred but not required.

The employment rate varies between 80% and 100%, depending on the candidate's availability. This is a 9-month contract, renewable. The earliest start date is May 1st or as soon as possible.

Missions

The main research activities will be related to the characterization and circular performance assessment of building envelopes in Europe, with a scope ranging from construction details and building archetypes to large-scale inference of building stocks. The project is embedded into a EU-Horizon project in collaboration with foreign industrial and research partners.

The candidate may also contribute to other research and teaching activities as well as to the supervision of architecture students at bachelor's and master's level.

About us

The Structural Xploration Lab is a group of doctoral and postdoctoral researchers in architecture and civil engineering. It is known for its development of tools, design methods, large-scale analyses and built prototypes aimed at enabling the Architecture, Engineering and Construction (AEC) sector to adopt more circular load-bearing systems. SXL also contributes to teaching building technologies and circular practices to undergraduate, master's students and professionals in architecture and civil engineering. As a unit of EPFL's ENAC faculty and located in the Smart Living Lab in Fribourg (CH), SXL benefits from state-of-the-art research infrastructure and offers an inclusive, international and stimulating work environment.

Application

Only applications submitted through the online platform are considered. You are asked to supply your CV and a brief statement of interests.

For any further information, please contact teresa.messina@epfl.ch .

Profil

Das Structural Xploration Lab sucht einen neuen Forschungsmitarbeiter mit einem Doktortitel in Gebäudetechnik, vorzugsweise im Bereich Baumaterialien und/oder Gebäudehüllenleistung und/oder Gebäudesanierung. Der Kandidat muss mit zeitgenössischen Bautechniken vertraut sein und sich für Bautechniken des 20. Jahrhunderts oder die einheimische Architektur interessieren. Erfahrung in Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), Building Information Modeling (BIM), Geographic Information Systems (GIS) oder Computerprogrammierung ist ein Plus. Ein Master-Abschluss oder Berufserfahrung in der Architektur ist bevorzugt, aber nicht erforderlich.

Die Beschäftigungsquote variiert zwischen 80% und 100%, abhängig von der Verfügbarkeit des Kandidaten. Dies ist ein 9-Monats-Vertrag, erneuerbar. Der frühe Starttermin ist der 1. Mai oder so schnell wie möglich.

Dienstreisen

Die Hauptforschungsaktivitäten werden sich auf die Charakterisierung und zirkuläre Leistungsbewertung von Gebäudehüllen in Europa beziehen, wobei die Entdeckung von Konstruktionsdetails und Gebäudearchetypen bis hin zu groß angelegten Rückschlüssen auf Gebäudebestände reicht. Das Projekt ist in ein EU-Horizon-Projekt in Zusammenarbeit mit ausländischen Industrie- und Forschungspartnern eingebettet.

Der Kandidat kann auch zu anderen Forschungs- und Lehraktivitäten sowie zur Betreuung von Architekturstudenten auf Bachelor- und Master-Niveau beitragen.

Über uns

Das Structural Xploration Lab ist eine Gruppe von Doktoranden und Postdoktoranden in Architektur und Bauingenieurwesen. Es ist bekannt für seine Entwicklung von Werkzeugen, Konstruktionsmethoden, groß angelegten Analysen und gebauten Prototypen, die den Architektur-, Ingenieur- und Bausektor (AEC) dabei unterstützen, mehr kreisförmige tragende Systeme zu übernehmen. SXL leistet auch Beiträge zum Unterrichten von Technologien und Kreislaufpraktiken für Studenten, Masterstudenten und Fachleute in Architektur und Bauingenieurwesen. Als Einheit der ENAC-Fakultät der EPFL im Smart Living Lab in Fribourg (CH) profitiert SXL von einer hochmodernen Forschungsinfrastruktur und bietet ein integratives, internationales und anregendes Arbeitsumfeld.

Antragstellung

Nur über die Online-Plattform eingereichte Bewerbungen werden berücksichtigt. Sie werden gebeten, Ihren Lebenslauf und eine kurze Interessenerklärung vorzulegen.

Für weitere Informationen wenden Sie sich bitte an teresa.messena@epfl.ch.

Profil

Le structural Xploration Lab cherche un nouveau collaborateur de recherche avec un doctorat en technologie du bâtiment, de préférence dans le domaine des matériaux de construction et/ou de la performance de l'enveloppe du bâtiment et/ou de la rénovation du bâtiment. Le candidat doit connaître les techniques de construction contemporaines et s'intéresser aux techniques de construction du XXe siècle ou à l'architecture vernaculaire. Expérience de l'évaluation du cycle de vie, de la modélisation de l'information sur les bâtiments, des systèmes d'information géographique ou de la programmation informatique est un atout. Une maîtrise ou une expérience professionnelle en architecture est préférée mais non requise.

Le taux d'emploi varie entre 80 % et 100 %, selon la disponibilité du candidat. C'est un contrat de 9 mois, renouvelable. La date de début est le 1er mai ou le plus tôt possible.

Missions

Les principales activités de recherche seront liées à la caractérisation et à l'évaluation circulaire des enveloppes de construction en Europe, avec une découverte allant des détails de construction et des archétypes de construction à l'inférence à grande échelle des stocks de construction. Le projet est intégré dans un projet UE-Horizon en collaboration avec des partenaires industriels et de recherche étrangers.

Le candidat peut également contribuer à d'autres activités de recherche et d'enseignement ainsi qu'à la supervision des étudiants en architecture au niveau du baccalauréat et de la maîtrise.

Sur nous

Le Laboratoire de Xpluration structurale est un groupe de chercheurs doctorals et postdoctoraux en architecture et en génie civil. Il est connu pour son développement d'outils, de méthodes de conception, d'analyses à grande échelle et de prototypes construits aidant le secteur de l'architecture, de l'ingénierie et de la construction (AEC) à adopter des systèmes de charge plus circulaires. SXL contribue également à l'enseignement des technologies et des pratiques circulaires aux étudiants de premier cycle, aux étudiants de maîtrise et aux professionnels en architecture et en génie civil. En tant qu'unité de la faculté ENAC de l'EPFL et située dans le Smart Living Lab de Fribourg (CH), SXL bénéficie d'une infrastructure de recherche de pointe et offre un environnement de travail inclusif, international et stimulant.

Demande

Seules les demandes soumises par le biais de la plateforme en ligne sont prises en considération. On vous demande de fournir votre CV et une brève déclaration d'intérêt.

Pour toute information complémentaire, veuillez contacter teresa.messena@epfl.ch .

titleByLocale.it: Post-Training Ingegnere - Apertus
titleByLocale.en: Post-Training Engineer - Apertus
titleByLocale.fr: Ingénieurs en recherche sur l'IA - Initiative Apertus

jobs.description:
Introduction

The Apertus project, a joint effort between EPFL and ETH Zürich, is seeking a practical and motivated engineer to help build the next generation of open foundation models. The successful candidate will help develop and run post-training and reinforcement learning pipelines for the Apertus project.

Apertus is trained and developed on Alps, the Swiss National Supercomputing Centre’s supercomputing infrastructure. The role requires someone who is comfortable working in an HPC environment and collaborating with researchers and infrastructure engineers.

Main duties and responsibilities

The engineer will contribute to the development, execution, and evaluation of scalable post-training workflows for Apertus.

Infrastructure and systems engineering

• Build and maintain containerized environments for LLM post-training and RL workloads.

• Adapt containers and dependencies for execution on Alps / CSCS infrastructure.

• Run and monitor Slurm-based training and evaluation jobs.

• Debug failures related to distributed execution, checkpointing, filesystem performance, networking, and GPU utilization.

• Help maintain reproducible training recipes, configuration files, launch scripts, and documentation.

• Work with researchers and CSCS engineers to improve the reliability and performance of large-scale experiments.

LLM post-training and Reinforcement Learning

• Support SFT, preference optimization, and reinforcement learning workflows.

• Build and run RL environments for tasks with verifiable outcomes, such as mathematics, code, tool-use, and reasoning.

• Develop reward modeling, reward calibration and verifier-based training.

• Generate and validate synthetic or gym training tasks.

• Run ablation studies comparing algorithms, reward functions, data mixtures, hyperparameters, and infrastructure settings.

• Evaluate model behavior across reasoning, coding, mathematics, instruction-following, multilingual, tool-use, and safety benchmarks.

• Debug common post-training issues, including optimization instability, reward hacking, regressions, and evaluation failures.

Profile

Essential

• MSc or PhD in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related field. Exceptional BSc candidates with strong engineering experience will also be considered.

• Experience in AI and neural network architectures

• Strong collaboration and communication skills and ability to work across research and engineering teams.

Strongly preferred

• Experience with Slurm or another HPC workload manager.

• Experience building or adapting containers for HPC or GPU clusters.

• Experience with LLM fine-tuning, post-training, preference optimization, or reinforcement learning.

• Familiarity with distributed training concepts such as data parallelism, tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, checkpointing, and GPU communication.

• Experience with frameworks such as veRL, slime, Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, TRL, vLLM, SGLang, or similar tools.

Nice to have

• Experience with RL for LLMs, online policy optimization, reward modeling, or RLVR.

descriptionByLocale.en:
Introduction

The Apertus project, a joint effort between EPFL and ETH Zürich, is seeking a practical and motivated engineer to help build the next generation of open foundation models. The successful candidate will help develop and run post-training and reinforcement learning pipelines for the Apertus project.

Apertus is trained and developed on Alps, the Swiss National Supercomputing Centre’s supercomputing infrastructure. The role requires someone who is comfortable working in an HPC environment and collaborating with researchers and infrastructure engineers.

Main duties and responsibilities

The engineer will contribute to the development, execution, and evaluation of scalable post-training workflows for Apertus.

Infrastructure and systems engineering

• Build and maintain containerized environments for LLM post-training and RL workloads.

• Adapt containers and dependencies for execution on Alps / CSCS infrastructure.

• Run and monitor Slurm-based training and evaluation jobs.

• Debug failures related to distributed execution, checkpointing, filesystem performance, networking, and GPU utilization.

• Help maintain reproducible training recipes, configuration files, launch scripts, and documentation.

• Work with researchers and CSCS engineers to improve the reliability and performance of large-scale experiments.

LLM post-training and Reinforcement Learning

• Support SFT, preference optimization, and reinforcement learning workflows.

• Build and run RL environments for tasks with verifiable outcomes, such as mathematics, code, tool-use, and reasoning.

• Develop reward modeling, reward calibration and verifier-based training.

• Generate and validate synthetic or gym training tasks.

• Run ablation studies comparing algorithms, reward functions, data mixtures, hyperparameters, and infrastructure settings.

• Evaluate model behavior across reasoning, coding, mathematics, instruction-following, multilingual, tool-use, and safety benchmarks.

• Debug common post-training issues, including optimization instability, reward hacking, regressions, and evaluation failures.

Profile

Essential

• MSc or PhD in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related field. Exceptional BSc candidates with strong engineering experience will also be considered.

• Experience in AI and neural network architectures

• Strong collaboration and communication skills and ability to work across research and engineering teams.

Strongly preferred

• Experience with Slurm or another HPC workload manager.

• Experience building or adapting containers for HPC or GPU clusters.

• Experience with LLM fine-tuning, post-training, preference optimization, or reinforcement learning.

• Familiarity with distributed training concepts such as data parallelism, tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, checkpointing, and GPU communication.

• Experience with frameworks such as veRL, slime, Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, TRL, vLLM, SGLang, or similar tools.

Nice to have

• Experience with RL for LLMs, online policy optimization, reward modeling, or RLVR.

• Experience creating verifiable tasks for mathematics, code, reasoning, or tool use.

• Familiarity with lower-level GPU/distributed libraries such as NCCL, Transformer Engine, FlashAttention, or communication backends.

• Experience with large-scale evaluation pipelines.

Mission

The EPFL computer vision lab ( https://www.epfl.ch/labs/cvlab/ ) is looking for a postdoctoral fellow to work on issues related to co-design for aerodynamic shape and control along the lines described in the following tech report https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.06760 . A potential target application is the design of model gliders to compete in FAI competitions such as https://www.fai.org/page/f5-electric-flight .

Profile

Potential candidates are expected to have:

• A doctorate in a Machine-Learning related field

• A deep knowledge of Control Theory, both classical and deep learning based

• A solid publication record in top level ML venues such as NeurIPs, ICML, and ICLR

• Familiarity with aerodynamics and aircraft design would be a plus

We offer

• Competitive salary and excellent working conditions – more information can be found on our website ( https://www.epfl.ch/campus/services/human-resources/en/basic-starting-salary-of-doctoral-assistants-and-postdocs/)

• Opportunity to interact with internationally renowned experts, and with a strong team of postdoctoral researchers and PhD students

Informations

Only applications submitted through the online platform are considered. You are asked to supply:

A brief cover letter (pdf, up to 2 pages).

And in one PDF:

A CV with a publication list.
A research statement (pdf, up to 3 pages).
Contact details for 3 referees.

Contract start date : Flexible (Fall 2026 preferred)

Activity rate : 100%

Contract type : CDD

Duration : One year, renewable

jobs.description:
Mission

The A. Mathis Group for Computational Neuroscience and AI (CNAI), led by Professor Alexander Mathis, is seeking two postdoctoral fellows to join our team working at the intersection of artificial intelligence and neuroscience. Our research is built around three intertwined questions: how to measure and understand behavior with AI, how brains and embodied agents learn to control the body, and how the brain builds a sense of its body through proprioception. We develop widely-used open-source tools (e.g., DeepLabCut), train biomechanically realistic embodied agents (e.g., MuscleMimic, Kinesis, Arnold), and build AI-based models of sensorimotor processing.

We are recruiting two postdocs:

• Postdoc in Computer Vision & AI for Behavior Analysis

• Postdoc in Embodied AI (Reinforcement Learning for Motor Control)

Main duties and responsibilities

For both positions:

• Conduct innovative, independent research aligned with the lab's mission and the candidate's interests

• Contribute to the lab's open-source software, datasets, and benchmarks

• Mentor PhD and Master's students and contribute to the lab's collaborative culture

• Engage with collaborators across EPFL and beyond (neuroscience labs, ecology partners, clinical collaborators)

• Present research at international conferences and workshops

Position 1: Computer Vision & AI for Behavior Analysis

• Contribute to the creation of behavioral datasets for groups of animals

• Develop methods for animal and environment reconstruction

• Develop methods for behavior understanding from multi-view video and audio recordings

• Advance multimodal large language models for fine-grained action understanding and reasoning

• Help shape the next generation of DeepLabCut and related open-source tools used by labs worldwide.

Position 2: Embodied AI

• Train muscle-actuated, biomechanically realistic agents to perform skilled motor tasks using reinforcement learning, imitation learning, and curriculum methods;

• Develop new methods for full-body musculoskeletal control

• Probe links between learned control policies and neural representations of movement in collaboration with experimental labs

Profile

Common requirements:

• PhD (completed or close to completion) in computer science, applied mathematics, computational neuroscience, robotics, physics or a closely related field;

• Strong publication record in relevant venues;

• Solid programming skills in Python and a modern deep-learning framework

• Excellent communication skills in spoken and written English;

• Self-motivated, collaborative, and committed to open science and reproducible research;

• Demonstrated ability to work both independently and as part of a team.

Position 1 — additional desirable expertise:
computer vision, video understanding, action recognition, multimodal/vision-language models, pose estimation, or large-scale self-supervised learning. Familiarity with neuroscience, or ethology is a plus.

Position 2 — additional desirable expertise:
reinforcement learning, imitation learning, optimal control, dynamical systems, or related ML areas; experience with physics simulators (MuJoCo). Familiarity with motor neuroscience and biomechanics is a plus.

We offer

• A vibrant, collaborative research environment at the intersection of AI and neuroscience

• Access to EPFL's compute infrastructure and to the broader EPFL ecosystem

• Competitive salary in line with EPFL postdoc standards

• Excellent working conditions

• Opportunities for international collaboration, conference travel, and professional development

Informations

• Contract start date: flexible, ideally summer 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter

• Activity rate: 100%

• Contract type: fixed-term, initially one year with the possibility of extension

• Work location: Campus Biotech, Geneva

How to apply

Applications should be submitted exclusively through the EPFL website. Postdoctoral applications should consist of:

• A motivati

descriptionByLocale.it:
Missione

Il gruppo A. Mathis per la neuroscienza computazionale e AI (CNAI), guidato dal professor Alexander Mathis, sta cercando due compagni postdoctorali per unirsi al nostro team lavorando all'intersezione tra intelligenza artificiale e neuroscienza. La nostra ricerca è costruita intorno a tre domande intrecciate: come misurare e capire il comportamento con l'AI, come i cervelli e gli agenti incarnati imparano a controllare il corpo e come il cervello costruisce un senso del suo corpo attraverso la costrizione.

Sviluppiamo strumenti open-source ampiamente utilizzati (ad esempio DeepLabCut), addestriamo agenti incarnati biomeccanicamente realistici (ad esempio MuscleMimic, Kinisis, Arnold) e costruiamo modelli basati su AI di processore a sensori motori.

Stiamo reclutando due postdocs:

- Postdoc in Computer Vision & AI per l'analisi dei comportamenti - Postdoc in Embodied AI (Apprendimento di sicurezza per il controllo del motore)

Principali compiti e responsabilità

Per entrambe le posizioni:

- Condurre ricerche innovative e indipendenti in linea con la missione del laboratorio e gli interessi del candidato - Contribuire al software, agli dataset e ai benchmark open source del laboratorio - Studenti di dottorato e Master Mentor e contribuire alla cultura collaborativa del laboratorio - Intraprendere 1100 persone in tutta l'EPFL e oltre (laboratori di neuroscienze, partner ecologici, clinici 1100rs) - Presenti ricerche in conferenze e workshop internazionali

Posizione 1: Visione del computer e AI per l'analisi del comportamento

- Contribuire alla creazione di set di dati per gruppi di animali - Sviluppare metodi per la ricostruzione di animali e ambiente - Sviluppare metodi per la comprensione di effetti da registrazioni video e audio multi-view - Avanzare modelli multimodali di lingua larga per la comprensione e il ragionamento a grana fine - Aiutare a modellare la prossima generazione di DeepLabCut e relativi strumenti open-source utilizzati dai laboratori di tutto il mondo.

Posizione 2: AI incarnato

- Train mucho-acted, biomechanically reactive agenti per eseguire compiti motorie qualificati utilizzando l'apprendimento del rinforzo, l'apprendimento dell'imitazione, e metodi di curriculum; - Sviluppare nuovi metodi per il controllo muscolo-scheletrico completo corpo - Collegamenti sonda tra politiche di controllo imparato e rappresentazioni neurali del movimento in collaborazione con laboratori sperimentali

Profilo

Requisiti comuni:

- Dottorato di ricerca (completato o prossimo al completamento) in informatica, matematica applicata, neuroscienze computazionali, robotica, fisica o un campo strettamente correlato; - Forte record di pubblicazione in luoghi rilevanti; - Abilità di programmazione solida in Python e un moderno quadro di apprendimento profondo - Ottime capacità di comunicazione in inglese parlato e scritto; - Auto-YVIII, collaborativa, e impegnata ad aprire la scienza e la ricerca riproducibile; - Capacità dimostrativa di lavorare sia indipendentemente che come parte di un team.

Posizione 1. competenze supplementari desiderabili:

visione informatica, comprensione video, riconoscimento dell'azione, modelli multimodali/vision-lingua, stima posa, o apprendimento auto-sorvegliato su larga scala. Fa 1steranno con neuroscienza, o etologia è un plus.

descriptionByLocale.en:
Mission

The A. Mathis Group for Computational Neuroscience and AI (CNAI), led by Professor Alexander Mathis, is seeking two postdoctoral fellows to join our team working at the intersection of artificial intelligence and neuroscience. Our research is built around three intertwined questions: how to measure and understand behavior with AI, how brains and embodied agents learn to control the body, and how the brain builds a sense of its body through proprioception. We develop widely-used open-source tools (e.g., DeepLabCut), train biomechanically realistic embodied agents (e.g., MuscleMimic, Kinesis, Arnold), and build AI-based models of sensorimotor processing.

We are recruiting two postdocs:

- Postdoc in Computer Vision & AI for Behavior Analysis
- Postdoc in Embodied AI (Reinforcement Learning for Motor Control)

Main duties and responsibilities

For both positions:

- Conduct innovative, independent research aligned with the lab's mission and the candidate's interests
- Contribute to the lab's open-source software, datasets, and benchmarks
- Mentor PhD and Master's students and contribute to the lab's collaborative culture
- Engage with collaborators across EPFL and beyond (neuroscience labs, ecology partners, clinical collaborators)
- Present research at international conferences and workshops

Position 1: Computer Vision & AI for Behavior Analysis

- Contribute to the creation of behavioral datasets for groups of animals
- Develop methods for animal and environment reconstruction
- Develop methods for behavior understanding from multi-view video and audio recordings
- Advance multimodal large language models for fine-grained action understanding and reasoning
- Help shape the next generation of DeepLabCut and related open-source tools used by labs worldwide.

Position 2: Embodied AI

- Train muscle-actuated, biomechanically realistic agents to perform skilled motor tasks using reinforcement learning, imitation learning, and curriculum methods;
- Develop new methods for full-body musculoskeletal control
- Probe links between learned control policies and neural representations of movement in collaboration with experimental labs

Profile

Common requirements:

- PhD (completed or close to completion) in computer science, applied mathematics, computational neuroscience, robotics, physics or a closely related field;
- Strong publication record in relevant venues;
- Solid programming skills in Python and a modern deep-learning framework
- Excellent communication skills in spoken and written English;
- Self-motivated, collaborative, and committed to open science and reproducible research;
- Demonstrated ability to work both independently and as part of a team.

Position 1 — additional desirable expertise:

computer vision, video understanding, action recognition, multimodal/vision-language models, pose estimation, or large-scale self-supervised learning. Familiarity with neuroscience, or ethology is a plus.

Position 2 — additional desirable expertise:

reinforcement learning, imitation learning, optimal control, dynamical systems, or related ML areas; experience with physics simulators (MuJoCo). Familiarity with motor neuroscience and biomechanics is a plus.

We offer

- A vibrant, collaborative research environment at the intersection of AI and neuroscience
- Access to EPFL's compute infrastructure and to the broader EPFL ecosystem
- Competitive salary in line with EPFL postdoc standards
- Excellent working conditions
- Opportunities for international collaboration, conference travel, and professional development

Informations

- Contract start date: flexible, ideally summer 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter
- Activity rate: 100%
- Contract type: fixed-term, initially one year with the possibility of extension
- Work location: Campus Biotech, Geneva

Applications should be submitted exclusively through the EPFL website. Postdoctoral applications should consist of:

descriptionByLocale.de:
Auftrag

Die A. Mathis Group for Computational Neuroscience and AI (CNAI), geleitet von Professor Alexander Mathis, sucht zwei Postdoc-Stipendiaten, die sich unserem Team anschließen, das an der Schnittstelle von künstlicher Intelligenz und Neurowissenschaften arbeitet. Unsere Forschungen sind auf drei miteinander verflochtene Fragen aufgebaut: wie man das Verhalten mit KI misst und versteht, wie Gehirne und verkörperte Agenten lernen, den Körper zu kontrollieren, und wie das Gehirn durch Propriozeption ein Gefühl seines Körpers baut.

Wir entwickeln weit verbreitete Open-Source-Tools (z.B. DeepLabCut), trainieren biomechanisch realistische verkörperte Wirkstoffe (z.B. MuscleMimic, Kinesis, Arnold) und bauen KI-basierte Modelle der Sensorimotorik auf.

Wir rekrutieren zwei Postdocs:

- Postdoc in Computer Vision & AI für Verhaltensanalyse - Postdoc in Embodyd AI (Reinforcement Learning for Motor Control)

Hauptaufgaben und Zuständigkeiten

Für beide Positionen:

- Führen Sie innovative, unabhängige Forschung auf die Mission des Labors und die Interessen des Kandidaten ausgerichtet - Tragen Sie zur Open-Source-Software des Labors, Datensätze und Benchmarks - Mentor PhD und Master-Studenten und Beitrag zur Kollaborationskultur des Labors - Engagement mit Mitarbeitern in der gesamten EPFL und darüber hinaus (Neuroscience-Labore, Ökologie-Partner, klinische Mitarbeiter) - Präsentieren Sie Forschung auf internationalen Konferenzen und Workshops

Position 1: Computer Vision & KI für Verhaltensanalyse

- Beitrag zur Erstellung von Verhaltensdatensätzen für Tiergruppen - Entwicklung von Methoden für Tier- und Umweltrekonstruktion - Entwicklung von Methoden für das Verhalten Verständnis von Multi-View-Video- und Audioaufnahmen - Weiterentwicklung multimodaler Großsprachenmodelle für feinkörniges Handlungsverständnis und -verdacht - Hilfe bei der Gestaltung der nächsten Generation von DeepLabCut und damit verbundenen Open-Source-Tools, die von Laboren weltweit eingesetzt werden.

Position 2: Körperliche KI

- Ausbildung von muskelaktiven, biomechanisch realistischen Wirkstoffen zur Durchführung von motorischen Aufgaben mit Hilfe von Verstärkungslern, Nachahmungslern und Lehrplänen; - Entwicklung neuer Methoden für die Ganzkörpermuskuloskeletalkontrolle; - Verbindung zwischen gelernter Kontrollpolitik und neuronalen Darstellungen von Bewegung in Zusammenarbeit mit experimentellen Laboren.

Profil

Gemeinsame Anforderungen:

- Doktorat (abgeschlossen oder kurz vor Abschluss) in Informatik, angewandter Mathematik, Computerneurologie, Robotik, Physik oder einem eng verwandten Bereich; - Starke Publikationsbilanz an relevanten Orten; - Solide Programmierkenntnisse in Python und ein modernes Deep-Learning-Rahmenwerk - Ausgezeichnete Kommunikationsfähigkeiten in gesprochenem und geschriebenem Englisch; - Selbst-motiviert, kollaborativ und verpflichtet zur offenen Wissenschaft und reproduzierbarer Forschung; - Demonstration der Fähigkeit, unabhängig und als Teil eines Teams zu arbeiten.

Position 1 — zusätzliches wünschenswertes Fachwissen:

Computer Vision, Video-Verständnis, Action-Erkennung, multimodale/visionssprachliche Modelle, Pose Schätzung oder groß angelegtes Selbst-überwachtes Lernen. Vertrautheit mit der Neurowissenschaft oder Ethologie ist ein Plus.

Position 2 — zusätzliches wünschenswertes Fachwissen:

Verstärkungslernen, Nachahmung, optimale Steuerung, dynamische Systeme oder verwandte ML-Bereiche; Erfahrung mit Physiksimulatoren (MuJoCo).Die Vertrautheit mit motorischen Neurowissenschaften und Biomechanik ist ein Plus.

Wir bieten

- Eine lebendige, kollaborative Forschungsumgebung an der Schnittstelle von KI und Neurowissenschaften - Zugang zur Computerinfrastruktur von EPFL und zum erweiterten EPFL-Ökosystem - Kompetitives Gehalt gemäß den Postdoc-Standards der EPFL - Ausgezeichnete Arbeitsbedingungen - Möglichkeiten für internationale Zusammenarbeit, Konferenzreisen und berufliche Entwicklung

Information

- Vertragsbeginn: flexibel, ideal Sommer 2026 oder so bald wie möglich danach - Aktivitätsrate: 100% - Vertragsart: befristet, zunächst ein Jahr mit Verlängerungsmöglichkeit - Standort: Campus Biotech, Genf

The Laboratory of Visual Intelligence for Transportation ( VITA ) is looking for a postdoctoral researcher in the area of Generative AI.

VITA research interests lie at the intersection of Computer Vision, Machine Learning (Deep Learning), and Human-Robot Interaction to redefine how machines interpret human actions, anticipate intentions, and interact seamlessly with people in various settings.

The successful candidate will be developing new methods for Real-time Video Generation, digital double, human-like avatars.

Profile

• PhD in Computer Vision

• Background in CS

• Research experience in gen AI, deep learning

• Strong computational and analytical skills, as well as experience handling large datasets

• Independent, creative, and solution-oriented

• Good interpersonal skills, team player

• Good knowledge of English (written and spoken)

We offer

• A dynamic and interdisciplinary research group

• A stimulating and international working environment

• Competitive salary and excellent working conditions – more information can be found on our website ( https://www.epfl.ch/campus/services/human-resources/en/basic-starting-salary-of-doctoral-assistants-and-postdocs/)

• Opportunity to perform state-of-the-art research in one of the most dynamic scientific institutions in Europe

• Opportunity to interact with internationally renowned experts, and with a strong team of postdoctoral researchers and PhD students

Informations

Only applications submitted through the online platform are considered. You are asked to supply:

• A brief cover letter (pdf, up to 2 pages)

And in one PDF:

• A CV with a publication list

• A research statement (pdf, up to 3 pages)

• Contact details for 3 referees.

• Developing verification techniques for establishing correctness with respect to formal specifications

Missione

L'EPFL Networked Systems Abstractions Lab (LASeR) sviluppa linguaggi di programmazione e strumenti di ragionamento formale per sistemi in rete. Le reti sono l'infrastruttura invisibile che collega il mondo moderno, ma la programmazione e il ragionamento su di loro sono sorprendentemente difficili. La nostra ricerca affronta questa sfida nei seguenti settori:

• Progettazione di linguaggi espressivi per specificare il comportamento di rete

• Sviluppare tecniche di verifica per stabilire la correttezza rispetto alle specifiche formali

• Ingegneria efficienti implementazioni che rendono pratiche astrazioni di alto livello

Cerchiamo candidati eccezionali che lavorano in linguaggi di programmazione, metodi formali e/o in rete, con interessi in una o più delle seguenti aree: NetKAT e le sue estensioni, automi simbolici, algebre routing, programmazione di pacchetti e sicurezza informatica basata su AI.

Principali doveri e responsabilità

• Condurre la ricerca sulle astrazioni di rete, la progettazione della lingua, l'implementazione e la verifica. Il focus preciso sarà discusso con il candidato di successo a seconda del loro background, competenza e affinità. Le possibili indicazioni includono:

• Entwicklung von Verifikationstechniken zur Feststellung der Richtigkeit in Bezug auf formale Spezifikationen

• Engineering effiziente Implementierungen, die High-Level-Abstraktionen praktisch machen

jobs.description:
Mission

The performance of X-ray microscopy has improved significantly over the last decade, enabling synchrotron-based X-ray imaging to resolve individual transistors in modern semiconductor devices. As the industry moves to 3D transistor architectures and stacked, hybrid-bonded devices, it becomes important to study the initiation and propagation of defects due to thermal and electrical phenomena (e.g., dielectric breakdown or electromigration). Compared to other imaging modalities such as electron microscopy, X-ray microscopy is non-destructive and hence ideally suited for in-situ and operando 3D imaging. However, at the sufficient imaging resolutions (sub-20 nm) measurements become slow, and because dose accumulates with every repeated measurement, radiation damage sets a hard limit on how long a process can be followed.

During conventional 3D imaging, the goal is to resolve every single voxel of the 3D volume. However, the underlying dynamic changes can be temporally sparse and highly localized, meaning that only a small fraction of the sample voxels need to be re-measured to detect the change, rather than the complete 3D volume. Microchip samples are also highly structured, with known design rules, which can enable us to more easily detect sparse dynamic changes with as few measurements as possible. The newly established Laboratory for Nanoscale X-ray Metrology is looking for a motivated postdoctoral researcher to develop time-resolved imaging methods and apply them to semiconductor reliability problems.

This is one of two postdoctoral positions opening in the group. This position focuses on time-resolved imaging of dynamic processes, while the companion position focuses on high-throughput imaging of static structural defects . Each postdoc will lead their own independent research direction, with an opportunity for close collaborative work.

Main duties and responsibilities

You will develop an acquisition and reconstruction framework that exploits sparsity of the underlying dynamics and microchip sample structure to detect nanoscale sample changes from the smallest possible number of X-ray measurements. Our pipeline reconstructs each projection from thousands of diffraction patterns, followed by volume reconstruction from projections measured at many rotation angles. These are two inverse problems, each with its own sampling requirements that can be significantly relaxed through sparsity.

The questions we want to answer:

• How temporal and structural sparsity can be incorporated into the 3D dynamics reconstruction model?

• How sparse can a measurement be and still capture a high-resolution dynamic event?

• How do temporal resolution, spatial resolution, and radiation dose trade against one another, and what semiconductor dynamics can be observed?

The primary focus will be on algorithm development, followed by their demonstration at synchrotron experiments. You will start working with an existing data acquisition and reconstruction pipeline which will be improved and extended for semiconductor imaging. You will also get a chance to perform experiments at the cSAXS beamline of the upgraded Swiss Light Source synchrotron, as well as other facilities around the world.

Profile

We are looking for a person with:

• PhD in physics, engineering, computer science, or a related field.

• Experience with inverse problems and 3D reconstruction methods for tomography, laminography, or a closely related modality.

• Strong scientific programming in Python and experience with GPU processing of large-scale datasets.

• Excellent written and oral communication skills in English.

We also value applications from people with the following experience (or similar):

• Coherent diffractive imaging, especially ptychography.

• Sparse sensing, optimization, or Bayesian experimental design.

• Machine learning for imaging.

• Synchrotron experiment experience.

• Semiconductor devices or metrology.

descriptionByLocale.it:
Missione

Le prestazioni della microscopia a raggi X sono migliorate in modo significativo nell'ultimo decennio, consentendo l'imaging a raggi X basato su sincrotroni per risolvere i singoli transistor nei moderni dispositivi a semiconduttore. Mentre l'industria si sposta in architetture transistor 3D e dispositivi impilati e ibridi, diventa importante studiare l'iniziazione e la propagazione dei difetti a causa di fenomeni termici ed elettrici (ad esempio, la ripartizione dielettrica o l'elettromigrazione). Rispetto ad altre modalità di imaging come la microscopia elettronica, la microscopia a raggi X è non distruttiva e quindi ideale per l'imaging 3D in-situ e operando. Tuttavia, alle misure di risoluzione di immagini sufficienti (sotto-20 nm) diventano lenti, e perché la dose si accumula con ogni misura ripetuta, i danni alle radiazioni imposta un limite duro su quanto tempo un processo può essere seguito.

Durante l'imaging 3D convenzionale, l'obiettivo è quello di risolvere ogni singolo voxel del volume 3D. Tuttavia, i cambiamenti dinamici sottostanti possono essere temporalmente radi e altamente localizzati, il che significa che solo una piccola frazione del campione voxels deve essere ri-measured per rilevare il cambiamento, piuttosto che il volume 3D completo. I campioni di microchip sono anche altamente strutturati, con regole di progettazione note, che possono permetterci di rilevare più facilmente cambi dinamici radi con il minor numero possibile di misurazioni. Il nuovo laboratorio per la metrologia a raggi X Nanoscale sta cercando un ricercatore postdoctoral motivato per sviluppare metodi di imaging risolti nel tempo e applicarli a problemi di affidabilità dei semiconduttori.

Questa è una delle due posizioni postdoctoral che si aprono nel gruppo. Questa posizione si concentra sull'imaging risolto nel tempo dei processi dinamici, mentre la posizione del compagno si concentra sull'imaging ad alto rendimento dei difetti strutturali statici. Ogni postdoc porterà la propria direzione di ricerca indipendente, con l'opportunità di un lavoro collaborativo ravvicinato.

Principali doveri e responsabilità

Svilupperai un quadro di acquisizione e ricostruzione che sfrutta la parsimonia delle dinamiche sottostanti e la struttura campione microchip per rilevare i cambiamenti del campione su scala nano dal minor numero possibile di misurazioni a raggi X. La nostra pipeline ricostruisce ogni proiezione da migliaia di modelli di diffrazione, seguiti dalla ricostruzione del volume da proiezioni misurate a molti angoli di rotazione. • Come la sparsità temporale e strutturale può essere incorporata nel modello di ricostruzione dinamica 3D?

• Quanto può essere rada una misura e ancora catturare un evento dinamico ad alta risoluzione?

• Come si fa la risoluzione temporale, la risoluzione spaziale e il commercio di dosi di radiazione l'uno contro l'altro, e quali dinamiche semiconduttori possono essere osservate?

Mission

The performance of X-ray microscopy has improved significantly over the last decade, enabling synchrotron-based X-ray imaging to resolve individual transistors in modern semiconductor devices. As the industry moves to 3D transistor architectures and stacked, hybrid-bonded devices, it becomes important to study the initiation and propagation of defects due to thermal and electrical phenomena (e.g., dielectric breakdown or electromigration). Compared to other imaging modalities such as electron microscopy, X-ray microscopy is non-destructive and hence ideally suited for in-situ and operando 3D imaging. However, at the sufficient imaging resolutions (sub-20 nm) measurements become slow, and because dose accumulates with every repeated measurement, radiation damage sets a hard limit on how long a process can be followed.

During conventional 3D imaging, the goal is to resolve every single voxel of the 3D volume. However, the underlying dynamic changes can be temporally sparse and highly localized, meaning that only a small fraction of the sample voxels need to be re-measured to detect the change, rather than the complete 3D volume. Microchip samples are also highly structured, with known design rules, which can enable us to more easily detect sparse dynamic changes with as few measurements as possible. The newly established Laboratory for Nanoscale X-ray Metrology is looking for a motivated postdoctoral researcher to develop time-resolved imaging methods and apply them to semiconductor reliability problems.

This is one of two postdoctoral positions opening in the group. This position focuses on time-resolved imaging of dynamic processes, while the companion position focuses on high-throughput imaging of static structural defects . Each postdoc will lead their own independent research direction, with an opportunity for close collaborative work.

Main duties and responsibilities

You will develop an acquisition and reconstruction framework that exploits sparsity of the underlying dynamics and microchip sample structure to detect nanoscale sample changes from the smallest possible number of X-ray measurements. Our pipeline reconstructs each projection from thousands of diffraction patterns, followed by volume reconstruction from projections measured at many rotation angles. These are two inverse problems, each with its own sampling requirements that can be significantly relaxed through sparsity.

The questions we want to answer:

• How temporal and structural sparsity can be incorporated into the 3D dynamics reconstruction model?

• How sparse can a measurement be and still capture a high-resolution dynamic event?

• How do temporal resolution, spatial resolution, and radiation dose trade against one another, and what semiconductor dynamics can be observed?

The primary focus will be on algorithm development, followed by their demonstration at synchrotron experiments. You will start working with an existing data acquisition and reconstruction pipeline which will be improved and extended for semiconductor imaging. You will also get a chance to perform experiments at the cSAXS beamline of the upgraded Swiss Light Source synchrotron, as well as other facilities around the world.

• PhD in physics, engineering, computer science, or a related field.

• Strong scientific programming in Python and experience with GPU processing of large-scale datasets.

• Excellent written and oral communication skills in English.

Mission

Die Leistung der Röntgenmikroskopie hat sich in den letzten zehn Jahren deutlich verbessert, so dass die synchrotronbasierte Röntgenbildgebung einzelne Transistoren in modernen Halbleiterbauelementen auflösen kann. Da sich die Industrie zu 3D-Transistorarchitekturen und gestapelten, hybridgebundenen Bauelementen bewegt, wird es wichtig, die Initiierung und Ausbreitung von Defekten aufgrund thermischer und elektrischer Phänomene (z. B. dielektrischer Zusammenbruch oder Elektromigration) zu untersuchen. Im Vergleich zu anderen Bildgebungsmodalitäten wie der Elektronenmikroskopie ist die Röntgenmikroskopie zerstörungsfrei und daher ideal für In-situ- und Operando-3D-Bildgebung geeignet. Bei ausreichenden Bildauflösungen (Sub-20 nm) werden die Messungen jedoch langsam, und da sich die Dosis mit jeder wiederholten Messung ansammelt, setzt der Strahlenschaden eine harte Grenze, wie lange ein Prozess verfolgt werden kann.

Bei der herkömmlichen 3D-Bildgebung besteht das Ziel darin, jedes einzelne Voxel des 3D-Volumens aufzulösen. Die zugrunde liegenden dynamischen Veränderungen können jedoch zeitlich spärlich und stark lokalisiert sein, was bedeutet, dass nur ein kleiner Teil der Probenvoxel neu gemessen werden muss, um die Veränderung zu erkennen, anstatt das gesamte 3D-Volumen. Mikrochip-Proben sind auch hochstrukturiert, mit bekannten Konstruktionsregeln, die es uns ermöglichen, spärliche dynamische Veränderungen mit möglichst wenigen Messungen leichter zu erkennen. Das neu gegründete Labor für Nanoskalige Röntgenmetrologie sucht einen motivierten Postdoktoranden, der zeitaufgelöste Bildgebungsmethoden entwickelt und sie auf Probleme mit der Zuverlässigkeit von Halbleitern anwendet.

Dies ist eine von zwei postdoc-positionen, die in der gruppe eröffnet werden. Diese Position konzentriert sich auf die zeitaufgelöste Abbildung dynamischer Prozesse, während sich die Begleitposition auf die Hochdurchsatz-Bildgebung statischer struktureller Defekte konzentriert. Jeder Postdoc wird seine eigene unabhängige Forschungsrichtung leiten, mit der Möglichkeit einer engen Zusammenarbeit.

Hauptaufgaben und Zuständigkeiten

Sie werden ein Erfassungs- und Rekonstruktions-Framework entwickeln, das die geringe Anzahl der zugrunde liegenden Dynamik und die Mikrochip-Probenstruktur ausnutzt, um nanoskalige Probenänderungen aus der geringstmöglichen Anzahl von Röntgenmessungen zu erkennen. Unsere Pipeline rekonstruiert jede Projektion aus Tausenden von Beugungsmustern, gefolgt von einer Volumenrekonstruktion aus Projektionen, die bei vielen Rotationswinkeln gemessen wurden. Dies sind zwei inverse Probleme, jedes mit seinen eigenen Probenahmeanforderungen, die durch Sparsity erheblich gelockert werden können.

Die Fragen, die wir beantworten wollen:

• Wie können zeitliche und strukturelle Sparsity in das 3D-Dynamik-Rekonstruktionsmodell integriert werden?

• Wie spärlich kann eine Messung sein und trotzdem ein hochauflösendes dynamisches Ereignis erfassen?

• Wie handeln zeitliche Auflösung, räumliche Auflösung und Strahlendosis gegeneinander und welche Halbleiterdynamik kann beobachtet werden?

Der Schwerpunkt wird auf der Entwicklung von Algorithmen liegen, gefolgt von ihrer Demonstration bei Synchrotronexperimenten. Sie werden mit einer bestehenden Datenerfassungs- und Rekonstruktionspipeline arbeiten, die für die Halbleiterbildgebung verbessert und erweitert wird. Sie erhalten auch die Möglichkeit, Experimente an der cSAXS-Beamline des verbesserten Synchrotrons Swiss Light Source sowie an anderen Einrichtungen auf der ganzen Welt durchzuführen.

descriptionByLocale.fr:
Mission

La performance de la microscopie à rayons X s'est considérablement améliorée au cours de la dernière décennie, permettant à l'imagerie à rayons X à base de synchrotron de résoudre les transistors individuels dans les dispositifs à semi-conducteur modernes. Au fur et à mesure que l'industrie passe aux architectures de transistors 3D et aux dispositifs empilés à liaison hybride, il devient important d'étudier l'initiation et la propagation des défauts dus à des phénomènes thermiques et électriques (par exemple, la dégradation diélectrique ou l'électromigration). Par rapport à d'autres modalités d'imagerie telles que la microscopie électronique, la microscopie aux rayons X est non destructive et donc idéale pour l'imagerie in-situ et opérando 3D. Cependant, à des résolutions d'imagerie suffisantes (sous- 20 nm) les mesures deviennent lentes, et comme la dose s'accumule à chaque mesure répétée, les dommages causés par les rayonnements limitent considérablement la durée du processus.

Lors de l'imagerie 3D conventionnelle, le but est de résoudre chaque voxel du volume 3D. Cependant, les changements dynamiques sous-jacents peuvent être temporellement clairsemés et hautement localisés, ce qui signifie qu'une petite fraction seulement des voxels de l'échantillon doivent être re-mesurés pour détecter le changement, plutôt que le volume 3D complet. Les échantillons de micropuces sont également très structurés, avec des règles de conception connues, ce qui peut nous permettre de détecter plus facilement des changements dynamiques clairsemés avec le moins de mesures possibles. Le Laboratoire de métrologie à rayons X nouvellement créé cherche un chercheur postdoctoral motivé pour développer des méthodes d'imagerie résolues dans le temps et les appliquer aux problèmes de fiabilité des semi-conducteurs.

Il s'agit de l'un des deux postes postdoctoraux du groupe. Cette position se concentre sur l'imagerie des processus dynamiques résolues dans le temps, tandis que la position d'accompagnement se concentre sur l'imagerie à haut débit des défauts structurels statiques. Chaque postdoctorant dirigera sa propre direction de recherche indépendante, avec l'occasion de travailler en étroite collaboration.

Principales fonctions et responsabilités

Vous développerez un cadre d'acquisition et de reconstruction qui exploite la sparsité de la dynamique sous-jacente et de la structure d'échantillon de micropuces pour détecter les changements d'échantillon nanométriques à partir du plus petit nombre possible de mesures de rayons X. Notre pipeline reconstitue chaque projection à partir de milliers de schémas de diffraction, puis la reconstruction en volume à partir de projections mesurées à de nombreux angles de rotation. Il s'agit de deux problèmes inverses, chacun avec ses propres exigences d'échantillonnage qui peuvent être considérablement assouplis par la sparosité.

Les questions que nous voulons répondre:

• Comment la sparosité temporelle et structurelle peut-elle être intégrée au modèle de reconstruction dynamique 3D?

• Dans quelle mesure une mesure peut-elle être et peut-elle encore capturer un événement dynamique à haute résolution?

• Comment la résolution temporelle, la résolution spatiale et les doses de rayonnement échangent-ils entre eux, et quelle dynamique de semi-conducteur peut-on observer?

L'accent sera principalement mis sur le développement d'algorithmes, suivi de leur démonstration lors d'expériences de synchrotron. Vous commencerez à travailler avec un pipeline existant d'acquisition et de reconstruction de données qui sera amélioré et étendu pour l'imagerie semi-conducteur. Vous aurez également l'occasion de réaliser des expériences à la ligne de faisceaux cSAXS du synchrotron Swiss Light Source amélioré, ainsi que d'autres installations dans le monde entier.

Profil

Nous cherchons une personne avec:

• Doctorat en physique, en génie, en informatique ou dans un domaine connexe.

• Expérience des problèmes inverses et des méthodes de reconstruction 3D pour la tomographie, la laminographie ou une modalité étroitement liée.

• Forte programmation scientifique en Python et expérience avec le traitement GPU des ensembles de données à grande échelle.

• Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et orale en anglais.

Nous apprécions également les applications de personnes ayant l'expérience suivante (ou similaire):

• Imagerie diffractive cohérente, en particulier la ptychographie.

• Détection, optimisation ou conception expérimentale bayésienne.

• Apprentissage automatique pour l'imagerie.

• Expérience synchrotron.

• Dispositifs semiconducteurs ou métrologie.

jobs.description:
Mission

The performance of X-ray microscopy has improved significantly over the last decade, enabling synchrotron-based X-ray imaging to resolve individual transistors in modern semiconductor devices. As the industry moves to 3D transistor architectures and stacked, hybrid-bonded devices, non-destructive, high-resolution 3D imaging is becoming a necessity. Unfortunately, current 3D X-ray nanoimaging methods are prohibitively slow for practical semiconductor metrology and inspection applications.

Unlike most samples placed under a microscope, microchips are manufactured objects that follow strict design rules. This allows us to shift from the standard imaging question of "what is the structure of this sample?" to "how does the structure differ from the known design?". The second question can be answered with far fewer measurements than the first. The newly established Laboratory for Nanoscale X-ray Metrology is looking for a motivated postdoctoral researcher to turn this idea into a working method.

This is one of two postdoctoral positions opening in the group. This position focuses on high-throughput imaging of static structural defects, while the companion position focuses on time-resolved imaging of dynamic processes . Each postdoc will lead their own independent research direction, with an opportunity for close collaborative work.

Main duties and responsibilities

You will develop an acquisition and reconstruction framework that uses the known geometry, composition, and layout regularity of semiconductor devices as prior information to detect deeply buried defects from the smallest possible number of X-ray measurements. Our pipeline reconstructs each projection from thousands of diffraction patterns, followed by volume reconstruction from projections measured at many rotation angles. These are two inverse problems, each with its own sampling requirements.

The questions we want to answer:

• What is the minimum number of diffraction patterns and projections needed to identify a defect?

• Can we detect defects from diffraction patterns alone, bypassing projection reconstruction?

• Can we reliably identify defects without ever resolving them?

• What is the best way to incorporate the known design information into the imaging process?

The primary focus will be on algorithm development, followed by their demonstration at synchrotron experiments. You will start working with real already existing experimental datasets and will have the opportunity to extend our established reconstruction pipeline, and integrate with new data acquisition methods. You will also get a chance to perform experiments at the cSAXS beamline of the upgraded Swiss Light Source synchrotron, as well as other facilities around the world.

Profile

We are looking for a person with:

• PhD in physics, engineering, computer science, or a related field.

• Strong scientific programming in Python and experience with GPU processing of large-scale datasets.

• Experience with inverse problems and 3D reconstruction methods for tomography, laminography, or a closely related modality.

• Excellent written and oral communication skills in English.

We also value applications from people with the following experience (or similar):

• Coherent diffractive imaging, especially ptychography.

• Sparse sensing, optimization, or Bayesian experimental design.

• Machine learning for imaging.

• Synchrotron experiment experience.

• Semiconductor devices or metrology.

We offer

We offer a fully funded postdoctoral position for two years (with a possibility of an extension) in a unique dual environment. Contracts are issued for one year and renewable annually according to standard EPFL procedures. You will be employed by EPFL, one of the world’s leading technical universities.
